texts.mat.7.27: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and smote upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall thereof.
texts.mat.7.28: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, the multitudes were astonished at his teaching:
texts.mat.7.29: for he taught them as [one] having authority, and not as their scribes.
texts.mat.8.1: And when he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.
texts.mat.8.2: And behold, there came to him a leper and worshipped him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
texts.mat.8.3: And he stretched forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou made clean. And straightway his leprosy was cleansed.
texts.mat.8.4: And Jesus saith unto him, See thou tell no man; but go, show thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
texts.mat.8.5: And when he was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,
texts.mat.8.6: and saying, Lord, my servant lieth in the house sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.
texts.mat.8.7: And he saith unto him, I will come and heal him.
texts.mat.8.8: And the centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof; but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed.
texts.mat.8.9: For I also am a man under authority, having under myself soldiers: and I say to this one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
texts.mat.8.10: And when Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
texts.mat.8.11: And I say unto you, that many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven:
texts.mat.8.12: but the sons of the kingdom shall be cast forth into the outer darkness: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.8.13: And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; as thou hast believed, [so] be it done unto thee. And the servant was healed in that hour.
texts.mat.8.14: And when Jesus was come into Peter's house, he saw his wife's mother lying sick of a fever.
texts.mat.8.15: And he touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she arose, and ministered unto him.
texts.mat.8.16: And when even was come, they brought unto him many possessed with demons: and he cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all that were sick:
texts.mat.8.17: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying: Himself took our infirmities, and bare our diseases.
texts.mat.8.18: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes about him, he gave commandments to depart unto the other side.
texts.mat.8.19: And there came a scribe, and said unto him, Teacher, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.
texts.mat.8.20: And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the heaven [have] nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
texts.mat.8.21: And another of the disciples said unto him, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.
texts.mat.8.22: But Jesus saith unto him, Follow me; and leave the dead to bury their own dead.
texts.mat.8.23: And when he was entered into a boat, his disciples followed him.
texts.mat.8.24: And behold, there arose a great tempest in the sea, insomuch that the boat was covered with the waves: but he was asleep.
texts.mat.8.25: And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Save, Lord; we perish.
texts.mat.8.26: And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
texts.mat.8.27: And the men marvelled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?
texts.mat.8.28: And when he was come to the other side into the country of the Gadarenes, there met him two possessed with demons, coming forth out of the tombs, exceeding fierce, so that no man could pass by that way.
texts.mat.8.29: And behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with thee, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?
texts.mat.8.30: Now there was afar off from them a herd of many swine feeding.
texts.mat.8.31: And the demons besought him, saying, If thou cast us out, send us away into the herd of swine.
texts.mat.8.32: And he said unto them, Go. And they came out, and went into the swine: and behold, the whole herd rushed down the steep into the sea, and perished in the waters.
texts.mat.8.33: And they that fed them fled, and went away into the city, and told everything, and what was befallen to them that were possessed with demons.
texts.mat.8.34: And behold, all the city came out to meet Jesus: and when they saw him, they besought [him] that he would depart from their borders.
texts.mat.9.1: And he entered into a boat, and crossed over, and came into his own city.
texts.mat.9.2: And behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, be of good cheer; thy sins are forgiven.
texts.mat.9.3: And behold, certain of the scribes said within themselves, This man blasphemeth.
texts.mat.9.4: And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?
texts.mat.9.5: For which is easier, to say, Thy sins are forgiven; or to say, Arise, and walk?
texts.mat.9.6: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath authority on earth to forgive sins (then saith he to the sick of the palsy), Arise, and take up thy bed, and go up unto thy house.
texts.mat.9.7: And he arose, and departed to his house.
texts.mat.9.8: But when the multitudes saw it, they were afraid, and glorified God, who had given such authority unto men.
texts.mat.9.9: And as Jesus passed by from thence, he saw a man, called Matthew, sitting at the place of toll: and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.
texts.mat.9.10: And it came to pass, as he sat at meat in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with Jesus and his disciples.
texts.mat.9.11: And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Teacher with the publicans and sinners?
texts.mat.9.12: But when he heard it, he said, They that are whole have no need of a physician, but they that are sick.
texts.mat.9.13: But go ye and learn what [this] meaneth, I desire mercy, and not sacrifice, for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.
texts.mat.9.14: Then come to him the disciples of John, saying, Why do we and the Pharisees fast oft, but thy disciples fast not?
texts.mat.9.15: And Jesus said unto them, Can the sons of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then will they fast.
texts.mat.9.16: And no man putteth a piece of undressed cloth upon an old garment; for that which should fill it up taketh from the garment, and a worse rent is made.
texts.mat.9.17: Neither do [men] put new wine into old wine-skins: else the skins burst, and the wine is spilled, and the skins perish: but they put new wine into fresh wine-skins, and both are preserved.
texts.mat.9.18: While he spake these things unto them, behold, there came a ruler, and worshipped him, saying, My daughter is even now dead: but come and lay thy hand upon her, and she shall live.
texts.mat.9.19: And Jesus arose, and followed him, and [so did] his disciples.
texts.mat.9.20: And behold, a woman, who had an issue of blood twelve years, came behind him, and touched the border of his garment:
texts.mat.9.21: for she said within herself, If I do but touch his garment, I shall be made whole.
texts.mat.9.22: But Jesus turning and seeing her said, Daughter, be of good cheer; thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.
texts.mat.9.23: And when Jesus came into the ruler's house, and saw the flute-players, and the crowd making a tumult,
texts.mat.9.24: he said, Give place: for the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed him to scorn.
texts.mat.9.25: But when the crowd was put forth, he entered in, and took her by the hand; and the damsel arose.
texts.mat.9.26: And the fame hereof went forth into all that land.
texts.mat.9.27: And as Jesus passed by from thence, two blind men followed him, crying out, and saying, Have mercy on us, thou son of David.
texts.mat.9.28: And when he was come into the house, the blind men came to him: and Jesus saith unto them, Believe ye that I am able to do this? They say unto him, Yea, Lord.
texts.mat.9.29: Then touched he their eyes, saying, According to your faith be it done unto you.
texts.mat.9.30: And their eyes were opened. And Jesus strictly charged them, saying, See that no man know it.
texts.mat.9.31: But they went forth, and spread abroad his fame in all that land.
texts.mat.9.32: And as they went forth, behold, there was brought to him a dumb man possessed with a demon.
texts.mat.9.33: And when the demon was cast out, the dumb man spake: and the multitudes marvelled, saying, It was never so seen in Israel.
texts.mat.9.34: But the Pharisees said, By the prince of the demons casteth he out demons.
texts.mat.9.35: And Jesus went about all the cities and the villages, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of disease and all manner of sickness.
texts.mat.9.36: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion for them, because they were distressed and scattered, as sheep not having a shepherd.
texts.mat.9.37: Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest indeed is plenteous, but the laborers are few.
texts.mat.9.38: Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he send forth laborers into his harvest.
texts.mat.10.1: And he called unto him his twelve disciples, and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of disease and all manner of sickness.
texts.mat.10.2: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the [son] of Zebedee, and John his brother;
texts.mat.10.3: Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the [son] of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
texts.mat.10.4: Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
texts.mat.10.5: These twelve Jesus sent forth, and charged them, saying, Go not into [any] way of the Gentiles, and enter not into any city of the Samaritans:
texts.mat.10.6: but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
texts.mat.10.7: And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.
texts.mat.10.8: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons: freely ye received, freely give.
texts.mat.10.9: Get you no gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses;
texts.mat.10.10: no wallet for [your] journey, neither two coats, nor shoes, nor staff: for the laborer is worthy of his food.
texts.mat.10.11: And into whatsoever city or village ye shall enter, search out who in it is worthy; and there abide till ye go forth.
texts.mat.10.12: And as ye enter into the house, salute it.
texts.mat.10.13: And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you.
texts.mat.10.14: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, as ye go forth out of that house or that city, shake off the dust of your feet.
texts.mat.10.15: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment, than for that city.
texts.mat.10.16: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
texts.mat.10.17: But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to councils, and in theirs synagogues they will scourge you;
texts.mat.10.18: yea and before governors and kings shall ye be brought for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
texts.mat.10.19: But when they deliver you up, be not anxious how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that hour what ye shall speak.
texts.mat.10.20: For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father that speaketh in you.
texts.mat.10.21: And brother shall deliver up brother to death, and the father his child: and children shall rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.
texts.mat.10.22: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved.
texts.mat.10.23: But when they persecute you in this city, flee into the next: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone through the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.
texts.mat.10.24: A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his lord.
texts.mat.10.25: It is enough for the disciple that he be as his teacher, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more them of his household!
texts.mat.10.26: Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.
texts.mat.10.27: What I tell you in the darkness, speak ye in the light; and what ye hear in the ear, proclaim upon the house-tops.
texts.mat.10.28: And be not afraid of them that kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
texts.mat.10.29: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? and not one of them shall fall on the ground without your Father:
texts.mat.10.30: but the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
texts.mat.10.31: Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.
texts.mat.10.32: Every one therefore who shall confess me before men, him will I also confess before my Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.10.33: But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.10.34: Think not that I came to send peace on the earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.
texts.mat.10.35: For I came to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law:
texts.mat.10.36: and a man's foes [shall be] they of his own household.
texts.mat.10.37: He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
texts.mat.10.38: And he that doth not take his cross and follow after me, is not worthy of me.
texts.mat.10.39: He that findeth his life shall lose it; and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.
texts.mat.10.40: He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.
texts.mat.10.41: He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet's reward: and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man's reward.
texts.mat.10.42: And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only, in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you he shall in no wise lose his reward.
texts.mat.11.1: And it came to pass when Jesus had finished commanding his twelve disciples, he departed thence to teach and preach in their cities.
texts.mat.11.2: Now when John heard in the prison the works of the Christ, he sent by his disciples
texts.mat.11.3: and said unto him, Art thou he that cometh, or look we for another?
texts.mat.11.4: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and tell John the things which ye hear and see:
texts.mat.11.5: the blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, and the dead are raised up, and the poor have good tidings preached to them.
texts.mat.11.6: And blessed is he, whosoever shall find no occasion of stumbling in me.
texts.mat.11.7: And as these went their way, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to behold? a reed shaken with the wind?
texts.mat.11.8: But what went ye out to see? a man clothed in soft [raiment]? Behold, they that wear soft [raiment] are in king's houses.
texts.mat.11.9: But wherefore went ye out? to see a prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.
texts.mat.11.10: This is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, Who shall prepare thy way before thee.
texts.mat.11.11: Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not arisen a greater than John the Baptist: yet he that is but little in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
texts.mat.11.12: And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and men of violence take it by force.
texts.mat.11.13: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.
texts.mat.11.14: And if ye are willing to receive [it,] this is Elijah, that is to come.
texts.mat.11.15: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.mat.11.16: But whereunto shall I liken this generation? It is like unto children sitting in the marketplaces, who call unto their fellows
texts.mat.11.17: and say, We piped unto you, and ye did not dance; we wailed, and ye did not mourn.
texts.mat.11.18: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He hath a demon.
texts.mat.11.19: The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold, a gluttonous man and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners! And wisdom is justified by her works.
texts.mat.11.20: Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not.
texts.mat.11.21: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
texts.mat.11.22: But I say unto you, it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the day of judgment than for you.
texts.mat.11.23: And thou, Capernaum, shalt thou be exalted unto heaven? thou shalt go down unto Hades: for if the mighty works had been done in Sodom which were done in thee, it would have remained until this day.
texts.mat.11.24: But I say unto you that it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.
texts.mat.11.25: At that season Jesus answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou didst hide these things from the wise and understanding, and didst reveal them unto babes:
texts.mat.11.26: yea, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in thy sight.
texts.mat.11.27: All things have been delivered unto me of my Father: and no one knoweth the Son, save the Father; neither doth any know the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son willeth to reveal [him.]
texts.mat.11.28: Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
texts.mat.11.29: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
texts.mat.11.30: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
texts.mat.12.1: At that season Jesus went on the sabbath day through the grainfields; and his disciples were hungry and began to pluck ears and to eat.
texts.mat.12.2: But the Pharisees, when they saw it, said unto him, Behold, thy disciples do that which it is not lawful to do upon the sabbath.
texts.mat.12.3: But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was hungry, and they that were with him;
texts.mat.12.4: how he entered into the house of God, and ate the showbread, which it was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them that were with him, but only for the priests?
texts.mat.12.5: Or have ye not read in the law, that on the sabbath day the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are guiltless?
texts.mat.12.6: But I say unto you, that one greater than the temple is here.
texts.mat.12.7: But if ye had known what this meaneth, I desire mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.
texts.mat.12.8: For the Son of man is lord of the sabbath.
texts.mat.12.9: And he departed thence, and went into their synagogue:
texts.mat.12.10: and behold, a man having a withered hand. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day? that they might accuse him.
texts.mat.12.11: And he said unto them, What man shall there be of you, that shall have one sheep, and if this fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out?
texts.mat.12.12: How much then is a man of more value than a sheep! Wherefore it is lawful to do good on the sabbath day.
texts.mat.12.13: Then saith he to the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, as the other.
texts.mat.12.14: But the Pharisees went out, and took counsel against him, how they might destroy him.
texts.mat.12.15: And Jesus perceiving [it] withdrew from thence: and many followed him; and he healed them all,
texts.mat.12.16: and charged them that they should not make him known:
texts.mat.12.17: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,
texts.mat.12.18: Behold, my servant whom I have chosen; My beloved in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my Spirit upon him, And he shall declare judgment to the Gentiles.
texts.mat.12.19: He shall not strive, nor cry aloud; Neither shall any one hear his voice in the streets.
texts.mat.12.20: A bruised reed shall he not break, And smoking flax shall he not quench, Till he send forth judgment unto victory.
texts.mat.12.21: And in his name shall the Gentiles hope.
texts.mat.12.22: Then was brought unto him one possessed with a demon, blind and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the dumb man spake and saw.
texts.mat.12.23: And all the multitudes were amazed, and said, Can this be the son of David?
texts.mat.12.24: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, This man doth not cast out demons, but by Beelzebub the prince of the demons.
texts.mat.12.25: And knowing their thoughts he said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand:
texts.mat.12.26: and if Satan casteth out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then shall his kingdom stand?
texts.mat.12.27: And if I by Beelzebub cast out demons, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges.
texts.mat.12.28: But if I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then is the kingdom of God come upon you.
texts.mat.12.29: Or how can one enter into the house of the strong [man,] and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong [man]? and then he will spoil his house.
texts.mat.12.30: He that is not with me is against me, and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.
texts.mat.12.31: Therefore I say unto you, Every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men; but the blasphemy against the Spirit shall not be forgiven.
texts.mat.12.32: And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him; but whosoever shall speak against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, nor in that which is to come.
texts.mat.12.33: Either make the tree good, and its fruit good; or make the tree corrupt, and its fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by its fruit.
texts.mat.12.34: Ye offspring of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.
texts.mat.12.35: The good man out of his good treasure bringeth forth good things: and the evil man out of his evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.
texts.mat.12.36: And I say unto you, that every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.
texts.mat.12.37: For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.
texts.mat.12.38: Then certain of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying, Teacher, we would see a sign from thee.
texts.mat.12.39: But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given it but the sign of Jonah the prophet:
texts.mat.12.40: for as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the whale; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
texts.mat.12.41: The men of Nineveh shall stand up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, a greater than Jonah is here.
texts.mat.12.42: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, a greater than Solomon is here.
texts.mat.12.43: But the unclean spirit, when he is gone out of the man, passeth through waterless places, seeking rest, and findeth it not.
texts.mat.12.44: Then he saith, I will return into my house whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished.
texts.mat.12.45: Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man becometh worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this evil generation.
texts.mat.12.46: While he was yet speaking to the multitudes, behold, his mother and his brethren stood without, seeking to speak to him.
texts.mat.12.47: And one said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren stand without, seeking to speak to thee.
texts.mat.12.48: But he answered and said unto him that told him, Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?
texts.mat.12.49: And he stretched forth his hand towards his disciples, and said, Behold, my mother and my brethren!
texts.mat.12.50: For whosoever shall do the will of my Father who is in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.
texts.mat.13.1: On that day went Jesus out of the house, and sat by the sea side.
texts.mat.13.2: And there were gathered unto him great multitudes, so that he entered into a boat, and sat; and all the multitude stood on the beach.
texts.mat.13.3: And he spake to them many things in parables, saying, Behold, the sower went forth to sow;
texts.mat.13.4: and as he sowed, some [seeds] fell by the way side, and the birds came and devoured them:
texts.mat.13.5: and others fell upon the rocky places, where they had not much earth: and straightway they sprang up, because they had no deepness of earth:
texts.mat.13.6: and when the sun was risen, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away.
texts.mat.13.7: And others fell upon the thorns; and the thorns grew up and choked them:
texts.mat.13.8: and others fell upon the good ground, and yielded fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
texts.mat.13.9: He that hath ears, let him hear.
texts.mat.13.10: And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables?
texts.mat.13.11: And he answered and said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.
texts.mat.13.12: For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that which he hath.
texts.mat.13.13: Therefore speak I to them in parables; because seeing they see not, and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.
texts.mat.13.14: And unto them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall in no wise understand; And seeing ye shall see, and shall in no wise perceive:
texts.mat.13.15: For this people's heart is waxed gross, And their ears are dull of hearing, And their eyes they have closed; Lest haply they should perceive with their eyes, And hear with their ears, And understand with their heart, And should turn again, And I should heal them.
texts.mat.13.16: But blessed are your eyes, for they see; and your ears, for they hear.
texts.mat.13.17: For verily I say unto you, that many prophets and righteous men desired to see the things which ye see, and saw them not; and to hear the things which ye hear, and heard them not.
texts.mat.13.18: Hear then ye the parable of the sower.
texts.mat.13.19: When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, [then] cometh the evil [one], and snatcheth away that which hath been sown in his heart. This is he that was sown by the way side.
texts.mat.13.20: And he that was sown upon the rocky places, this is he that heareth the word, and straightway with joy receiveth it;
texts.mat.13.21: yet hath he not root in himself, but endureth for a while; and when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, straightway he stumbleth.
texts.mat.13.22: And he that was sown among the thorns, this is he that heareth the word; and the care of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful.
texts.mat.13.23: And he that was sown upon the good ground, this is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; who verily beareth fruit, and bringeth forth, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
texts.mat.13.24: Another parable set he before them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man that sowed good seed in his field:
texts.mat.13.25: but while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares also among the wheat, and went away.
texts.mat.13.26: But when the blade sprang up and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also.
texts.mat.13.27: And the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst thou not sow good seed in thy field? whence then hath it tares?
texts.mat.13.28: And he said unto them, An enemy hath done this. And the servants say unto him, Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up?
texts.mat.13.29: But he saith, Nay; lest haply while ye gather up the tares, ye root up the wheat with them.
texts.mat.13.30: Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of the harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather up first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them; but gather the wheat into my barn.
texts.mat.13.31: Another parable set he before them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like unto a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:
texts.mat.13.32: which indeed is less than all seeds; but when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the heaven come and lodge in the branches thereof.
texts.mat.13.33: Another parable spake he unto them; The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till it was all leavened.
texts.mat.13.34: All these things spake Jesus in parables unto the multitudes; and without a parable spake he nothing unto them:
texts.mat.13.35: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.
texts.mat.13.36: Then he left the multitudes, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Explain unto us the parable of the tares of the field.
texts.mat.13.37: And he answered and said, He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man;
texts.mat.13.38: and the field is the world; and the good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom; and the tares are the sons of the evil [one];
texts.mat.13.39: and the enemy that sowed them is the devil: and the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are angels.
texts.mat.13.40: As therefore the tares are gathered up and burned with fire; so shall it be in the end of the world.
texts.mat.13.41: The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that cause stumbling, and them that do iniquity,
texts.mat.13.42: and shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.13.43: Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He that hath ears, let him hear.
texts.mat.13.44: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a treasure hidden in the field; which a man found, and hid; and in his joy he goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.
texts.mat.13.45: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is a merchant seeking goodly pearls:
texts.mat.13.46: and having found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
texts.mat.13.47: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:
texts.mat.13.48: which, when it was filled, they drew up on the beach; and they sat down, and gathered the good into vessels, but the bad they cast away.
texts.mat.13.49: So shall it be in the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the righteous,
texts.mat.13.50: and shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.13.51: Have ye understood all these things? They say unto him, Yea.
texts.mat.13.52: And he said unto them, Therefore every scribe who hath been made a disciple to the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is a householder, who bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old.
texts.mat.13.53: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence.
texts.mat.13.54: And coming into his own country he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished, and said, Whence hath this man this wisdom, and these mighty works?
texts.mat.13.55: Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joseph, and Simon, and Judas?
texts.mat.13.56: And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?
texts.mat.13.57: And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honor, save in his own country, and in his own house.
texts.mat.13.58: And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief.
texts.mat.14.1: At that season Herod the tetrarch heard the report concerning Jesus,
texts.mat.14.2: and said unto his servants, This is John the Baptist; he is risen from the dead; and therefore do these powers work in him.
texts.mat.14.3: For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife.
texts.mat.14.4: For John said unto him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.
texts.mat.14.5: And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.
texts.mat.14.6: But when Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in the midst, and pleased Herod.
texts.mat.14.7: Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatsoever she should ask.
texts.mat.14.8: And she, being put forward by her mother, saith, Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.
texts.mat.14.9: And the king was grieved; but for the sake of his oaths, and of them that sat at meat with him, he commanded it to be given;
texts.mat.14.10: and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.
texts.mat.14.11: And his head was brought on a platter, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother.
texts.mat.14.12: And his disciples came, and took up the corpse, and buried him; and they went and told Jesus.
texts.mat.14.13: Now when Jesus heard [it], he withdrew from thence in a boat, to a desert place apart: and when the multitudes heard [thereof,] they followed him on foot from the cities.
texts.mat.14.14: And he came forth, and saw a great multitude, and he had compassion on them, and healed their sick.
texts.mat.14.15: And when even was come, the disciples came to him, saying, The place is desert, and the time is already past; send the multitudes away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves food.
texts.mat.14.16: But Jesus said unto them, They have no need to go away; give ye them to eat.
texts.mat.14.17: And they say unto him, We have here but five loaves, and two fishes.
texts.mat.14.18: And he said, Bring them hither to me.
texts.mat.14.19: And he commanded the multitudes to sit down on the grass; and he took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake and gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.
texts.mat.14.20: And they all ate, and were filled: and they took up that which remained over of the broken pieces, twelve baskets full.
texts.mat.14.21: And they that did eat were about five thousand men, besides women and children.
texts.mat.14.22: And straightway he constrained the disciples to enter into the boat, and to go before him unto the other side, till he should send the multitudes away.
texts.mat.14.23: And after he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into the mountain apart to pray: and when even was come, he was there alone.
texts.mat.14.24: But the boat was now in the midst of the sea, distressed by the waves; for the wind was contrary.
texts.mat.14.25: And in the fourth watch of the night he came unto them, walking upon the sea.
texts.mat.14.26: And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a ghost; and they cried out for fear.
texts.mat.14.27: But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.
texts.mat.14.28: And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto the upon the waters.
texts.mat.14.29: And he said, Come. And Peter went down from the boat, and walked upon the waters to come to Jesus.
texts.mat.14.30: But when he saw the wind, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, Lord, save me.
texts.mat.14.31: And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and took hold of him, and saith unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?
texts.mat.14.32: And when they were gone up into the boat, the wind ceased.
texts.mat.14.33: And they that were in the boat worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God.
texts.mat.14.34: And when they had crossed over, they came to the land, unto Gennesaret.
texts.mat.14.35: And when the men of that place knew him, they sent into all that region round about, and brought unto him all that were sick,
texts.mat.14.36: and they besought him that they might only touch the border of his garment: and as many as touched were made whole.
texts.mat.15.1: Then there come to Jesus from Jerusalem Pharisees and scribes, saying,
texts.mat.15.2: Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.
texts.mat.15.3: And he answered and said unto them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God because of your tradition?
texts.mat.15.4: For God said, Honor thy father and thy mother: and, He that speaketh evil of father or mother, let him die the death.
texts.mat.15.5: But ye say, whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, That wherewith thou mightest have been profited by me is given [to God];
texts.mat.15.6: he shall not honor his father. And ye have made void the word of God because of your tradition.
texts.mat.15.7: Ye hypocrites, well did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,
texts.mat.15.8: This people honoreth me with their lips; But their heart is far from me.
texts.mat.15.9: But in vain do they worship me, Teaching [as their] doctrines the precepts of men.
texts.mat.15.10: And he called to him the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand:
texts.mat.15.11: Not that which entereth into the mouth defileth the man; but that which proceedeth out of the mouth, this defileth the man.
texts.mat.15.12: Then came the disciples, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the Pharisees were offended, when they heard this saying?
texts.mat.15.13: But he answered and said, Every plant which my heavenly Father planted not, shall be rooted up.
texts.mat.15.14: Let them alone: they are blind guides. And if the blind guide the blind, both shall fall into a pit.
texts.mat.15.15: And Peter answered and said unto him, Declare unto us the parable.
texts.mat.15.16: And he said, Are ye also even yet without understanding?
texts.mat.15.17: Perceive ye not, that whatsoever goeth into the mouth passeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?
texts.mat.15.18: But the things which proceed out of the mouth come forth out of the heart; and they defile the man.
texts.mat.15.19: For out of the heart come forth evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, railings:
texts.mat.15.20: these are the things which defile the man; but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not the man.
texts.mat.15.21: And Jesus went out thence, and withdrew into the parts of Tyre and Sidon.
texts.mat.15.22: And behold, a Canaanitish woman came out from those borders, and cried, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a demon.
texts.mat.15.23: But he answered her not a word. And his disciples came and besought him, saying, Send her away; for she crieth after us.
texts.mat.15.24: But he answered and said, I was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
texts.mat.15.25: But she came and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me.
texts.mat.15.26: And he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to the dogs.
texts.mat.15.27: But she said, Yea, Lord: for even the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table.
texts.mat.15.28: Then Jesus answered and said unto her, O woman, great is thy faith: be it done unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was healed from that hour.
texts.mat.15.29: And Jesus departed thence, and came nigh unto the sea of Galilee; and he went up into the mountain, and sat there.
texts.mat.15.30: And there came unto him great multitudes, having with them the lame, blind, dumb, maimed, and many others, and they cast them down at this feet; and he healed them:
texts.mat.15.31: insomuch that the multitude wondered, when they saw the dumb speaking, the maimed whole, and lame walking, and the blind seeing: and they glorified the God of Israel.
texts.mat.15.32: And Jesus called unto him his disciples, and said, I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days and have nothing to eat: and I would not send them away fasting, lest haply they faint on the way.
texts.mat.15.33: And the disciples say unto him, Whence should we have so many loaves in a desert place as to fill so great a multitude?
texts.mat.15.34: And Jesus said unto them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven, and a few small fishes.
texts.mat.15.35: And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground;
texts.mat.15.36: and he took the seven loaves and the fishes; and he gave thanks and brake, and gave to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.
texts.mat.15.37: And they all ate, and were filled: and they took up that which remained over of the broken pieces, seven baskets full.
texts.mat.15.38: And they that did eat were four thousand men, besides women and children.
texts.mat.15.39: And he sent away the multitudes, and entered into the boat, and came into the borders of Magadan.
texts.mat.16.1: And the Pharisees and Sadducees came, and trying him asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
texts.mat.16.2: But he answered and said unto them, When it is evening, ye say, [It will be] fair weather: for the heaven is red.
texts.mat.16.3: And in the morning, [It will be] foul weather to-day: for the heaven is red and lowering. Ye know how to discern the face of the heaven; but ye cannot [discern] the signs of the times.
texts.mat.16.4: An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given unto it, but the sign of Jonah. And he left them, and departed.
texts.mat.16.5: And the disciples came to the other side and forgot to take bread.
texts.mat.16.6: And Jesus said unto them, Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
texts.mat.16.7: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, We took no bread.
texts.mat.16.8: And Jesus perceiving it said, O ye of little faith, why reason ye among yourselves, because ye have no bread?
texts.mat.16.9: Do ye not yet perceive, neither remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?
texts.mat.16.10: Neither the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?
texts.mat.16.11: How is it that ye do not perceive that I spake not to you concerning bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
texts.mat.16.12: Then understood they that he bade them not beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
texts.mat.16.13: Now when Jesus came into the parts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Who do men say that the Son of man is?
texts.mat.16.14: And they said, Some [say] John the Baptist; some, Elijah; and others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.
texts.mat.16.15: He saith unto them, But who say ye that I am?
texts.mat.16.16: And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.
texts.mat.16.17: And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jonah: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.16.18: And I also say unto thee, that thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
texts.mat.16.19: I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven; and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
texts.mat.16.20: Then charged he the disciples that they should tell no man that he was the Christ.
texts.mat.16.21: From that time began Jesus to show unto his disciples, that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.
texts.mat.16.22: And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall never be unto thee.
texts.mat.16.23: But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art a stumbling-block unto me: for thou mindest not the things of God, but the things of men.
texts.mat.16.24: Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man would come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
texts.mat.16.25: For whosoever would save his life shall lose it: and whosoever shall lose his life for my sake shall find it.
texts.mat.16.26: For what shall a man be profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and forfeit his life? or what shall a man give in exchange for his life?
texts.mat.16.27: For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then shall he render unto every man according to his deeds.
texts.mat.16.28: Verily I say unto you, there are some of them that stand here, who shall in no wise taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.
texts.mat.17.1: And after six days Jesus taketh with him Peter, and James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into a high mountain apart:
texts.mat.17.2: and he was transfigured before them; and his face did shine as the sun, and his garments became white as the light.
texts.mat.17.3: And behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elijah talking with him.
texts.mat.17.4: And Peter answered, and said unto Jesus, Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, I will make here three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
texts.mat.17.5: While he was yet speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold, a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.
texts.mat.17.6: And when the disciples heard it, they fell on their face, and were sore afraid.
texts.mat.17.7: And Jesus came and touched them and said, Arise, and be not afraid.
texts.mat.17.8: And lifting up their eyes, they saw no one, save Jesus only.
texts.mat.17.9: And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying, Tell the vision to no man, until the Son of man be risen from the dead.
texts.mat.17.10: And his disciples asked him, saying, Why then say the scribes that Elijah must first come?
texts.mat.17.11: And he answered and said, Elijah indeed cometh, and shall restore all things:
texts.mat.17.12: but I say into you, that Elijah is come already, and they knew him not, but did unto him whatsoever they would. Even so shall the Son of man also suffer of them.
texts.mat.17.13: Then understood the disciples that he spake unto them of John the Baptist.
texts.mat.17.14: And when they were come to the multitude, there came to him a man, kneeling to him, saying,
texts.mat.17.15: Lord, have mercy on my son: for he is epileptic, and suffereth grievously; for oft-times he falleth into the fire, and off-times into the water.
texts.mat.17.16: And I brought him to thy disciples, and they could not cure him.
texts.mat.17.17: And Jesus answered and said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I bear with you? bring him hither to me.
texts.mat.17.18: And Jesus rebuked him; and the demon went out of him: and the boy was cured from that hour.
texts.mat.17.19: Then came the disciples to Jesus apart, and said, Why could not we cast it out?
texts.mat.17.20: And he saith unto them, Because of your little faith: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.
texts.mat.17.21: [But this kind goeth not out save by prayer and fasting.]
texts.mat.17.22: And while they abode in Galilee, Jesus said unto them, The Son of man shall be delivered up into the hands of men;
texts.mat.17.23: and they shall kill him, and the third day he shall be raised up. And they were exceeding sorry.
texts.mat.17.24: And when they were come to Capernaum, they that received the half-shekel came to Peter, and said, Doth not your teacher pay the half-shekel?
texts.mat.17.25: He saith, Yea. And when he came into the house, Jesus spake first to him, saying, What thinkest thou, Simon? the kings of the earth, from whom do they receive toll or tribute? from their sons, or from strangers?
texts.mat.17.26: And when he said, From strangers, Jesus said unto him, Therefore the sons are free.
texts.mat.17.27: But, lest we cause them to stumble, go thou to the sea, and cast a hook, and take up the fish that first cometh up; and when thou hast opened his mouth, thou shalt find a shekel: that take, and give unto them for me and thee.
texts.mat.18.1: In that hour came the disciples unto Jesus, saying, Who then is greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
texts.mat.18.2: And he called to him a little child, and set him in the midst of them,
texts.mat.18.3: and said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye turn, and become as little children, ye shall in no wise enter into the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.18.4: Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.18.5: And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me:
texts.mat.18.6: But whoso shall cause one of these little ones that believe on me to stumble, it is profitable for him that a great millstone should be hanged about his neck, and [that] he should be sunk in the depth of the sea.
texts.mat.18.7: Woe unto the world because of occasions of stumbling! for it must needs be that the occasions come; but woe to that man through whom the occasion cometh!
texts.mat.18.8: And if thy hand or thy foot causeth thee to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from thee: it is good for thee to enter into life maimed or halt, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into the eternal fire.
texts.mat.18.9: And if thine eye causeth thee to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: it is good for thee to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the hell of fire.
texts.mat.18.10: See that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, that in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.18.11: [For the Son of man came to save that which was lost.]
texts.mat.18.12: How think ye? if any man have a hundred sheep, and one of them be gone astray, doth he not leave the ninety and nine, and go unto the mountains, and seek that which goeth astray?
texts.mat.18.13: And if so be that he find it, verily I say unto you, he rejoiceth over it more than over the ninety and nine which have not gone astray.
texts.mat.18.14: Even so it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish.
texts.mat.18.15: And if thy brother sin against thee, go, show him his fault between thee and him alone: if he hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.
texts.mat.18.16: But if he hear [thee] not, take with thee one or two more, that at the mouth of two witnesses or three every word may be established.
texts.mat.18.17: And if he refuse to hear them, tell it unto the church: and if he refuse to hear the church also, let him be unto thee as the Gentile and the publican.
texts.mat.18.18: Verily I say unto you, what things soever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven; and what things soever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
texts.mat.18.19: Again I say unto you, that if two of you shall agree on earth as touching anything that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.18.20: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
texts.mat.18.21: Then came Peter and said to him, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? until seven times?
texts.mat.18.22: Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times; but, Until seventy times seven.
texts.mat.18.23: Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, who would make a reckoning with his servants.
texts.mat.18.24: And when he had begun to reckon, one was brought unto him, that owed him ten thousand talents.
texts.mat.18.25: But forasmuch as he had not [wherewith] to pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.
texts.mat.18.26: The servant therefore fell down and worshipped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.
texts.mat.18.27: And the lord of that servant, being moved with compassion, released him, and forgave him the debt.
texts.mat.18.28: But that servant went out, and found one of his fellow-servants, who owed him a hundred shillings: and he laid hold on him, and took [him] by the throat, saying, Pay what thou owest.
texts.mat.18.29: So his fellow-servant fell down and besought him, saying, Have patience with me, and I will pay thee.
texts.mat.18.30: And he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay that which was due.
texts.mat.18.31: So when his fellow-servants saw what was done, they were exceeding sorry, and came and told unto their lord all that was done.
texts.mat.18.32: Then his lord called him unto him, and saith to him, Thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou besoughtest me:
texts.mat.18.33: shouldest not thou also have had mercy on thy fellow-servant, even as I had mercy on thee?
texts.mat.18.34: And his lord was wroth, and delivered him to the tormentors, till he should pay all that was due.
texts.mat.18.35: So shall also my heavenly Father do unto you, if ye forgive not every one his brother from your hearts.
texts.mat.19.1: And it came to pass when Jesus had finished these words, he departed from Galilee, and came into the borders of Judaea beyond the Jordan;
texts.mat.19.2: and great multitudes followed him; and he healed them there.
texts.mat.19.3: And there came unto him Pharisees, trying him, and saying, Is it lawful [for a man] to put away his wife for every cause?
texts.mat.19.4: And he answered and said, Have ye not read, that he who made [them] from the beginning made them male and female,
texts.mat.19.5: and said, For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh?
texts.mat.19.6: So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
texts.mat.19.7: They say unto him, Why then did Moses command to give a bill of divorcement, and to put [her] away?
texts.mat.19.8: He saith unto them, Moses for your hardness of heart suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it hath not been so.
texts.mat.19.9: And I say unto you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and he that marrieth her when she is put away committeth adultery.
texts.mat.19.10: The disciples say unto him, If the case of the man is so with his wife, it is not expedient to marry.
texts.mat.19.11: But he said unto them, Not all men can receive this saying, but they to whom it is given.
texts.mat.19.12: For there are eunuchs, that were so born from their mother's womb: and there are eunuchs, that were made eunuchs by men: and there are eunuchs, that made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven's sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it.
texts.mat.19.13: Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should lay his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them.
texts.mat.19.14: But Jesus said, Suffer the little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for to such belongeth the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.19.15: And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence.
texts.mat.19.16: And behold, one came to him and said, Teacher, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?
texts.mat.19.17: And he said unto him, Why askest thou me concerning that which is good? One there is who is good: but if thou wouldest enter into life, keep the commandments.
texts.mat.19.18: He saith unto him, Which? And Jesus said, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness,
texts.mat.19.19: Honor thy father and mother; and, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.
texts.mat.19.20: The young man saith unto him, All these things have I observed: what lack I yet?
texts.mat.19.21: Jesus said unto him, If thou wouldest be perfect, go, sell that which thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.
texts.mat.19.22: But when the young man heard the saying, he went away sorrowful; for he was one that had great possessions.
texts.mat.19.23: And Jesus said unto his disciples, Verily I say unto you, It is hard for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.19.24: And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
texts.mat.19.25: And when the disciples heard it, they were astonished exceedingly, saying, Who then can be saved?
texts.mat.19.26: And Jesus looking upon [them] said to them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
texts.mat.19.27: Then answered Peter and said unto him, Lo, we have left all, and followed thee; what then shall we have?
texts.mat.19.28: And Jesus said unto them, Verily I say unto you, that ye who have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit on the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
texts.mat.19.29: And every one that hath left houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or children, or lands, for my name's sake, shall receive a hundredfold, and shall inherit eternal life.
texts.mat.19.30: But many shall be last [that are] first; and first [that are] last.
texts.mat.20.1: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that was a householder, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers into his vineyard.
texts.mat.20.2: And when he had agreed with the laborers for a shilling a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
texts.mat.20.3: And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing in the marketplace idle;
texts.mat.20.4: and to them he said, Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right I will give you. And they went their way.
texts.mat.20.5: Again he went out about the sixth and the ninth hour, and did likewise.
texts.mat.20.6: And about the eleventh [hour] he went out, and found others standing; and he saith unto them, Why stand ye here all the day idle?
texts.mat.20.7: They say unto him, Because no man hath hired us. He saith unto them, Go ye also into the vineyard.
texts.mat.20.8: And when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward, Call the laborers, and pay them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first.
texts.mat.20.9: And when they came that [were hired] about the eleventh hour, they received every man a shilling.
texts.mat.20.10: And when the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; and they likewise received every man a shilling.
texts.mat.20.11: And when they received it, they murmured against the householder,
texts.mat.20.12: saying, These last have spent [but] one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.
texts.mat.20.13: But he answered and said to one of them, Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst not thou agree with me for a shilling?
texts.mat.20.14: Take up that which is thine, and go thy way; it is my will to give unto this last, even as unto thee.
texts.mat.20.15: Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? or is thine eye evil, because I am good?
texts.mat.20.16: So the last shall be first, and the first last.
texts.mat.20.17: And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples apart, and on the way he said unto them,
texts.mat.20.18: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be delivered unto the chief priests and scribes; and they shall condemn him to death,
texts.mat.20.19: and shall deliver him unto the Gentiles to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify: and the third day he shall be raised up.
texts.mat.20.20: Then came to him the mother of the sons of Zebedee with her sons, worshipping [him], and asking a certain thing of him.
texts.mat.20.21: And he said unto her, What wouldest thou? She saith unto him, Command that these my two sons may sit, one on thy right hand, and one on thy left hand, in thy kingdom.
texts.mat.20.22: But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink the cup that I am about to drink? They say unto him, We are able.
texts.mat.20.23: He saith unto them, My cup indeed ye shall drink: but to sit on my right hand, and on [my] left hand, is not mine to give; but [it is for them] for whom it hath been prepared of my Father.
texts.mat.20.24: And when the ten heard it, they were moved with indignation concerning the two brethren.
texts.mat.20.25: But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Ye know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
texts.mat.20.26: Not so shall it be among you: but whosoever would become great among you shall be your minister;
texts.mat.20.27: and whosoever would be first among you shall be your servant:
texts.mat.20.28: even as the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
texts.mat.20.29: And as they went out from Jericho, a great multitude followed him.
texts.mat.20.30: And behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, saying, Lord, have mercy on us, thou son of David.
texts.mat.20.31: And the multitude rebuked them, that they should hold their peace: but they cried out the more, saying, Lord, have mercy on us, thou son of David.
texts.mat.20.32: And Jesus stood still, and called them, and said, What will ye that I should do unto you?
texts.mat.20.33: They say unto him, Lord, that our eyes may be opened.
texts.mat.20.34: And Jesus, being moved with compassion, touched their eyes; and straightway they received their sight, and followed him.
texts.mat.21.1: And when they drew nigh unto Jerusalem, and came unto Bethphage, unto the mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
texts.mat.21.2: saying unto them, Go into the village that is over against you, and straightway ye shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose [them], and bring [them] unto me.
texts.mat.21.3: And if any one say aught unto you, ye shall say, The Lord hath need of them; and straightway he will send them.
texts.mat.21.4: Now this is come to pass, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying,
texts.mat.21.5: Tell ye the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, Meek, and riding upon an ass, And upon a colt the foal of an ass.
texts.mat.21.6: And the disciples went, and did even as Jesus appointed them,
texts.mat.21.7: and brought the ass, and the colt, and put on them their garments; and he sat thereon.
texts.mat.21.8: And the most part of the multitude spread their garments in the way; and others cut branches from the trees, and spread them in the way.
texts.mat.21.9: And the multitudes that went before him, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed [is] he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.
texts.mat.21.10: And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was stirred, saying, Who is this?
texts.mat.21.11: And the multitudes said, This is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.
texts.mat.21.12: And Jesus entered into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of he money-changers, and the seats of them that sold the doves;
texts.mat.21.13: and he saith unto them, It is written, My house shall be called a house of prayer: but ye make it a den of robbers.
texts.mat.21.14: And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple; and he healed them.
texts.mat.21.15: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children that were crying in the temple and saying, Hosanna to the son of David; they were moved with indignation,
texts.mat.21.16: and said unto him, Hearest thou what these are saying? And Jesus saith unto them, Yea: did ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou has perfected praise?
texts.mat.21.17: And he left them, and went forth out of the city to Bethany, and lodged there.
texts.mat.21.18: Now in the morning as he returned to the city, he hungered.
texts.mat.21.19: And seeing a fig tree by the way side, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only; and he saith unto it, Let there be no fruit from thee henceforward for ever. And immediately the fig tree withered away.
texts.mat.21.20: And when the disciples saw it, they marvelled, saying, How did the fig tree immediately wither away?
texts.mat.21.21: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Verily I say unto you, If ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only do what is done to the fig tree, but even if ye shall say unto this mountain, Be thou taken up and cast into the sea, it shall be done.
texts.mat.21.22: And all things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.
texts.mat.21.23: And when he was come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came unto him as he was teaching, and said, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority?
texts.mat.21.24: And Jesus answered and said unto them, I also will ask you one question, which if ye tell me, I likewise will tell you by what authority I do these things.
texts.mat.21.25: The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven or from men? And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say unto us, Why then did ye not believe him?
texts.mat.21.26: But if we shall say, From men; we fear the multitude; for all hold John as a prophet.
texts.mat.21.27: And they answered Jesus, and said, We know not. He also said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.
texts.mat.21.28: But what think ye? A man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to-day in the vineyard.
texts.mat.21.29: And he answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented himself, and went.
texts.mat.21.30: And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I [go], sir: and went not.
texts.mat.21.31: Which of the two did the will of his father? They say, The first. Jesus saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, that the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.
texts.mat.21.32: For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not; but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye saw it, did not even repent yourselves afterward, that ye might believe him.
texts.mat.21.33: Hear another parable: There was a man that was a householder, who planted a vineyard, and set a hedge about it, and digged a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into another country.
texts.mat.21.34: And when the season of the fruits drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, to receive his fruits.
texts.mat.21.35: And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.
texts.mat.21.36: Again, he sent other servants more than the first: and they did unto them in like manner.
texts.mat.21.37: But afterward he sent unto them his son, saying, They will reverence my son.
texts.mat.21.38: But the husbandmen, when they saw the son, said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and take his inheritance.
texts.mat.21.39: And they took him, and cast him forth out of the vineyard, and killed him.
texts.mat.21.40: When therefore the lord of the vineyard shall come, what will he do unto those husbandmen?
texts.mat.21.41: They say unto him, He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and will let out the vineyard unto other husbandmen, who shall render him the fruits in their seasons.
texts.mat.21.42: Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, The same was made the head of the corner; This was from the Lord, And it is marvelous in our eyes?
texts.mat.21.43: Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken away from you, and shall be given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.
texts.mat.21.44: And he that falleth on this stone shall be broken to pieces: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will scatter him as dust.
texts.mat.21.45: And when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they perceived that he spake of them.
texts.mat.21.46: And when they sought to lay hold on him, they feared the multitudes, because they took him for a prophet.
texts.mat.22.1: And Jesus answered and spake again in parables unto them, saying,
texts.mat.22.2: The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a certain king, who made a marriage feast for his son,
texts.mat.22.3: and sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the marriage feast: and they would not come.
texts.mat.22.4: Again he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell them that are bidden, Behold, I have made ready my dinner; my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come to the marriage feast.
texts.mat.22.5: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his own farm, another to his merchandise;
texts.mat.22.6: and the rest laid hold on his servants, and treated them shamefully, and killed them.
texts.mat.22.7: But the king was wroth; and he sent his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
texts.mat.22.8: Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they that were bidden were not worthy.
texts.mat.22.9: Go ye therefore unto the partings of the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage feast.
texts.mat.22.10: And those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was filled with guests.
texts.mat.22.11: But when the king came in to behold the guests, he saw there a man who had not on a wedding-garment:
texts.mat.22.12: and he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding-garment? And he was speechless.
texts.mat.22.13: Then the king said to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and cast him out into the outer darkness; there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.22.14: For many are called, but few chosen.
texts.mat.22.15: Then went the Pharisees, and took counsel how they might ensnare him in [his] talk.
texts.mat.22.16: And they send to him their disciples, with the Herodians, saying, Teacher, we know that thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth, and carest not for any one: for thou regardest not the person of men.
texts.mat.22.17: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?
texts.mat.22.18: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, Why make ye trial of me, ye hypocrites?
texts.mat.22.19: Show me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a denarius.
texts.mat.22.20: And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?
texts.mat.22.21: They say unto him, Caesar's. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's.
texts.mat.22.22: And when they heard it, they marvelled, and left him, and went away.
texts.mat.22.23: On that day there came to him Sadducees, they that say that there is no resurrection: and they asked him,
texts.mat.22.24: saying, Teacher, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
texts.mat.22.25: Now there were with us seven brethren: and the first married and deceased, and having no seed left his wife unto his brother;
texts.mat.22.26: in like manner the second also, and the third, unto the seventh.
texts.mat.22.27: And after them all, the woman died.
texts.mat.22.28: In the resurrection therefore whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.
texts.mat.22.29: But Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.
texts.mat.22.30: For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as angels in heaven.
texts.mat.22.31: But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying,
texts.mat.22.32: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not [the God] of the dead, but of the living.
texts.mat.22.33: And when the multitudes heard it, they were astonished at his teaching.
texts.mat.22.34: But the Pharisees, when they heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, gathered themselves together.
texts.mat.22.35: And one of them, a lawyer, asked him a question, trying him:
texts.mat.22.36: Teacher, which is the great commandment in the law?
texts.mat.22.37: And he said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
texts.mat.22.38: This is the great and first commandment.
texts.mat.22.39: And a second like [unto it] is this, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.
texts.mat.22.40: On these two commandments the whole law hangeth, and the prophets.
texts.mat.22.41: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question,
texts.mat.22.42: saying, What think ye of the Christ? whose son is he? They say unto him, [The son] of David.
texts.mat.22.43: He saith unto them, How then doth David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,
texts.mat.22.44: The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, Till I put thine enemies underneath thy feet?
texts.mat.22.45: If David then calleth him Lord, how is he his son?
texts.mat.22.46: And no one was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions.
texts.mat.23.1: Then spake Jesus to the multitudes and to his disciples,
texts.mat.23.2: saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses seat:
texts.mat.23.3: all things therefore whatsoever they bid you, [these] do and observe: but do not ye after their works; for they say, and do not.
texts.mat.23.4: Yea, they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with their finger.
texts.mat.23.5: But all their works they do to be seen of men: for they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders [of their garments],
texts.mat.23.6: and love the chief place at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues,
texts.mat.23.7: and the salutations in the marketplaces, and to be called of men, Rabbi.
texts.mat.23.8: But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your teacher, and all ye are brethren.
texts.mat.23.9: And call no man your father on the earth: for one is your Father, [even] he who is in heaven.
texts.mat.23.10: Neither be ye called masters: for one is your master, [even] the Christ.
texts.mat.23.11: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.
texts.mat.23.12: And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be humbled; and whosoever shall humble himself shall be exalted.
texts.mat.23.13: But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye shut the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye enter not in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering in to enter[.]
texts.mat.23.14: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, even while for a pretence ye make long prayers: therefore ye shall receive greater condemnation.
texts.mat.23.15: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he is become so, ye make him twofold more a son of hell than yourselves.
texts.mat.23.16: Woe unto you, ye blind guides, that say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor.
texts.mat.23.17: Ye fools and blind: for which is greater, the gold, or the temple that hath sanctified the gold?
texts.mat.23.18: And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gift that is upon it, he is a debtor.
texts.mat.23.19: Ye blind: for which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift?
texts.mat.23.20: He therefore that sweareth by the altar, sweareth by it, and by all things thereon.
texts.mat.23.21: And he that sweareth by the temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein.
texts.mat.23.22: And he that sweareth by the heaven, sweareth by the throne of God, and by him that sitteth thereon.
texts.mat.23.23: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye tithe mint and anise and cummin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law, justice, and mercy, and faith: but these ye ought to have done, and not to have left the other undone.
texts.mat.23.24: Ye blind guides, that strain out the gnat, and swallow the camel!
texts.mat.23.25: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full from extortion and excess.
