texts.mat.26.51: E eis que um dos que estavam com Jesus, estendendo a mão, puxou da espada e, ferindo o servo do summo sacerdote, cortou-lhe uma orelha.
texts.mat.26.52: Então Jesus disse-lhe: Mette no seu logar a tua espada; porque todos os que lançarem mão da espada á espada morrerão.
texts.mat.26.53: Ou pensas tu que não poderia eu agora orar a meu Pae, e elle não me daria mais de doze legiões d’anjos?
texts.mat.26.54: Como pois se cumpririam as Escripturas, que dizem que assim convem que aconteça?
texts.mat.26.55: Então disse Jesus á multidão: Saistes, como a um salteador, com espadas e varapaus para me prender? todos os dias me assentava junto de vós, ensinando no templo, e não me prendestes.
texts.mat.26.56: Mas tudo isto aconteceu para que se cumpram as escripturas dos prophetas. Então todos os discipulos, deixando-o, fugiram.
texts.mat.26.57: E, os que prenderam a Jesus, o conduziram ao summo sacerdote, Caiphás, onde os escribas e os anciãos estavam reunidos.
texts.mat.26.58: E Pedro o seguiu de longe até ao pateo do summo sacerdote: e, entrando dentro, assentou-se entre os creados, para vêr o fim.
texts.mat.26.59: E os principes dos sacerdotes, e os anciãos, e todo o conselho, buscavam falso testemunho contra Jesus, para o poderem matar,
texts.mat.26.60: Mas não o achavam, apezar de se apresentarem muitas testemunhas falsas; mas por fim chegaram duas falsas testemunhas,
texts.mat.26.61: E disseram: Este disse: Eu posso derribar o templo de Deus, e reedifical-o em tres dias.
texts.mat.26.62: E, levantando-se o summo sacerdote, disse-lhe: Não respondes coisa alguma ao que estes depõem contra ti?
texts.mat.26.63: Jesus, porém, guardava silencio. E, insistindo o summo sacerdote, disse-lhe: Conjuro-te pelo Deus vivo que nos digas se tu és o Christo, o Filho de Deus.
texts.mat.26.64: Disse-lhe Jesus: Tu o disseste; digo-vos, porém, que vereis em breve o Filho do homem assentado á direita da magestade divina, e vindo sobre as nuvens do céu.
texts.mat.26.65: Então o summo sacerdote rasgou os seus vestidos, dizendo: Blasphemou; para que precisamos ainda de testemunhas? Eis que bem ouvistes agora a sua blasphemia.
texts.mat.26.66: Que vos parece? E elles, respondendo, disseram: E réu de morte.
texts.mat.26.67: Então cuspiram-lhe no rosto; e uns lhe davam punhadas, e outros o esbofeteavam,
texts.mat.26.68: Dizendo: Prophetiza-nos, Christo, quem é o que te bateu?
texts.mat.26.69: E Pedro estava assentado fóra, no pateo, e approximou-se d’elle uma creada, dizendo: Tu tambem estavas com Jesus, o galileo.
texts.mat.26.70: Mas elle negou diante de todos, dizendo: Não sei o que dizes.
texts.mat.26.71: E, saindo para o vestibulo, viu-o outra, e disse aos que ali estavam: Este tambem estava com Jesus, o nazareno.
texts.mat.26.72: E elle negou outra vez com juramento, dizendo: Não conheço tal homem.
texts.mat.26.73: E, d’ahi a pouco, approximando-se os que ali estavam, disseram a Pedro: Verdadeiramente tambem tu és um d’elles, pois a tua falla te denuncia.
texts.mat.26.74: Então começou elle a imprecar e a jurar, dizendo: Não conheço esse homem. E immediatamente o gallo cantou.
texts.mat.26.75: E lembrou-se Pedro das palavras de Jesus, que lhe dissera: Antes que o gallo cante, tres vezes me negarás. E, saindo d’ali, chorou amargamente.
texts.mat.27.1: E, chegando a manhã, todos os principes dos sacerdotes, e os anciãos do povo, formavam juntamente conselho contra Jesus, para o matarem;
texts.mat.27.2: E levaram-n’o maniatado, e entregaram-n’o ao presidente Poncio Pilatos.
texts.mat.27.3: Então Judas, o que o trahira, vendo que fôra condemnado, devolveu, arrependido, as trinta moedas de prata aos principes dos sacerdotes e aos anciãos,
texts.mat.27.4: Dizendo: Pequei, trahindo o sangue innocente. Elles, porém, disseram: Que nos importa? Isso é comtigo.
texts.mat.27.5: E elle, atirando para o templo as moedas de prata, retirou-se, e, indo, enforcou-se.
texts.mat.27.6: E os principes dos sacerdotes, tomando as moedas de prata, disseram: Não é licito mettel-as no cofre das offertas, porque são preço de sangue.
texts.mat.27.7: E, tendo deliberado juntamente, compraram com ellas o campo do oleiro, para sepultura dos estrangeiros.
texts.mat.27.8: Por isso foi chamado aquelle campo, até ao dia d’hoje, Campo de sangue.
texts.mat.27.9: Então se realisou o que vaticinara o propheta Jeremias: Tomaram as trinta moedas de prata, preço do avaliado, que os filhos d’Israel avaliaram,
texts.mat.27.10: E deram-n’as pelo campo do oleiro, segundo o que o Senhor determinou.
texts.mat.27.11: E foi Jesus apresentado ao presidente, e o presidente o interrogou, dizendo: És tu o Rei dos judeos? E disse-lhe Jesus: Tu o dizes.
texts.mat.27.12: E, sendo accusado pelos principes dos sacerdotes e pelos anciãos, nada respondeu.
texts.mat.27.13: Disse-lhe então Pilatos: Não ouves quanto testificam contra ti?
texts.mat.27.14: E nem uma palavra lhe respondeu, de sorte que o presidente estava muito maravilhado.
texts.mat.27.15: Ora, por occasião da festa, costumava o presidente soltar um preso, escolhendo o povo aquelle que quizesse.
texts.mat.27.16: E tinham então um preso bem conhecido, chamado Barrabás.
texts.mat.27.17: Portanto, reunindo-se elles, disse-lhes Pilatos: Qual quereis que vos solte? Barrabás, ou Jesus, chamado Christo?
texts.mat.27.18: Porque sabia que por inveja o haviam entregado.
texts.mat.27.19: E, estando elle assentado no tribunal, mandou sua mulher dizer-lhe: Não entres na questão d’esse justo, porque n’um sonho muito soffri por causa d’elle.
texts.mat.27.20: Mas os principes dos sacerdotes e os anciãos persuadiram á multidão que pedisse Barrabás e matasse Jesus.
texts.mat.27.21: E, respondendo o presidente, disse-lhes: Qual d’esses dois quereis vós que eu solte? E elles disseram: Barrabás.
texts.mat.27.22: Disse-lhes Pilatos: Que farei então de Jesus, chamado Christo? Disseram-lhe todos: Seja crucificado.
texts.mat.27.23: O presidente, porém, disse: Pois que mal tem feito? E elles mais clamavam, dizendo: Seja crucificado.
texts.mat.27.24: Então Pilatos, vendo que nada aproveitava, antes o tumulto crescia, tomando agua, lavou as mãos diante da multidão, dizendo: Estou innocente do sangue d’este justo: considerae-o vós.
texts.mat.27.25: E, respondendo todo o povo, disse: O seu sangue seja sobre nós e sobre nossos filhos.
texts.mat.27.26: Então soltou-lhes Barrabás, e, tendo mandado açoitar a Jesus, entregou-o para ser crucificado.
texts.mat.27.27: E logo os soldados do presidente, conduzindo Jesus á audiencia, reuniram junto d’elle toda a cohorte.
texts.mat.27.28: E, despindo-o, o cobriram com uma capa de escarlata;
texts.mat.27.29: E, tecendo uma corôa d’espinhos, pozeram-lh’a na cabeça, e em sua mão direita uma canna; e, ajoelhando diante d’elle, o escarneciam, dizendo: Salve, Rei dos judeos.
texts.mat.27.30: E, cuspindo n’elle, tiraram-lhe a canna, e batiam-lhe com ella na cabeça.
texts.mat.27.31: E, depois de o haverem escarnecido, tiraram-lhe a capa, vestiram-lhe os seus vestidos e o levaram a crucificar.
texts.mat.27.32: E, quando sahiam, encontraram um homem cyreneo, chamado Simão: a este constrangeram a levar a sua cruz.
texts.mat.27.33: E, chegando ao logar chamado Golgotha, que se diz: Logar da Caveira,
texts.mat.27.34: Deram-lhe a beber vinagre misturado com fel; mas, provando-o, não quiz beber.
texts.mat.27.35: E, havendo-o crucificado, repartiram os seus vestidos, lançando sortes: para que se cumprisse o que foi dito pelo propheta: Repartiram entre si os meus vestidos, e sobre a minha tunica lançaram sortes.
texts.mat.27.37: E por cima da sua cabeça pozeram escripta a sua accusação: ESTE É JESUS, O REI DOS JUDEOS.
texts.mat.27.38: E foram crucificados com elle dois salteadores, um á direita, e outro á esquerda.
texts.mat.27.39: E os que passavam blasphemavam d’elle, meneando as cabeças,
texts.mat.27.40: E dizendo: Tu, que destroes o templo, e em tres dias o reedificas, salva-te a ti mesmo; se és Filho de Deus, desce da cruz.
texts.mat.27.41: E da mesma maneira tambem os principes dos sacerdotes, com os escribas, e anciãos, e phariseos, escarnecendo, diziam:
texts.mat.27.42: Salvou a outros, a si mesmo não pode salvar-se. Se é o Rei d’Israel, desça agora da cruz, e creremos n’elle;
texts.mat.27.43: Confiou em Deus; livre-o agora, se o ama; porque disse: Sou Filho de Deus.
texts.mat.27.44: E o mesmo lhe lançaram tambem em rosto os salteadores que estavam crucificados com elle.
texts.mat.27.45: E desde a hora sexta houve trevas sobre toda a terra, até á hora nona.
texts.mat.27.46: E perto da hora nona exclamou Jesus em alta voz, dizendo: Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani; isto é, Deus meu, Deus meu, porque me desamparaste?
texts.mat.27.47: E alguns dos que ali estavam, ouvindo isto, diziam: Este chama por Elias.
texts.mat.27.48: E logo um d’elles, correndo, tomou uma esponja, e encheu-a de vinagre, e, pondo-a n’uma canna, dava-lhe de beber.
texts.mat.27.49: Os outros, porém, diziam: Deixa, vejamos se Elias vem livral-o.
texts.mat.27.50: E Jesus, clamando outra vez com grande voz, rendeu o espirito.
texts.mat.27.51: E eis que o véu do templo se rasgou em dois, d’alto a baixo; e tremeu a terra, e fenderam-se as pedras,
texts.mat.27.52: E abriram-se os sepulchros, e muitos corpos de sanctos que dormiam foram resuscitados,
texts.mat.27.53: E, saindo dos sepulchros, depois da resurreição d’elle, entraram na cidade sancta, e appareceram a muitos.
texts.mat.27.54: E o centurião e os que com elle guardavam a Jesus, vendo o terremoto, e as coisas que haviam succedido, tiveram grande temor, e disseram: Verdadeiramente este era o Filho de Deus.
texts.mat.27.55: E estavam ali olhando de longe muitas mulheres que tinham seguido Jesus desde a Galilea, servindo-o,
texts.mat.27.56: Entre as quaes estavam Maria Magdalena, e Maria, mãe de Thiago e de José, e a mãe dos filhos de Zebedeo.
texts.mat.27.57: E, vinda já a tarde, chegou um homem rico de Arimathea, por nome José, que tambem era discipulo de Jesus.
texts.mat.27.58: Este chegou a Pilatos, e pediu-lhe o corpo de Jesus. Então Pilatos mandou que o corpo lhe fosse dado.
texts.mat.27.59: E José, tomando o corpo, envolveu-o n’um fino e limpo lençol,
texts.mat.27.60: E o poz no seu sepulchro novo, que havia lavrado n’uma rocha, e, revolvendo uma grande pedra para a porta do sepulchro, foi-se.
texts.mat.27.61: E estavam ali Maria Magdalena e a outra Maria, assentadas defronte do sepulchro.
texts.mat.27.62: E no dia seguinte, que é depois da preparação, reuniram-se os principes dos sacerdotes e os phariseos em casa de Pilatos,
texts.mat.27.63: Dizendo: Senhor, lembramo-nos de que aquelle enganador, vivendo ainda, disse: Depois de tres dias resuscitarei.
texts.mat.27.64: Manda pois que o sepulchro seja guardado com segurança até ao terceiro dia, não seja caso que os seus discipulos vão de noite, e o furtem, e digam ao povo: Resuscitou dos mortos; e assim o ultimo erro será peior do que o primeiro.
texts.mat.27.65: E disse-lhes Pilatos: Tendes a guarda; ide, guardae-o como entenderdes.
texts.mat.27.66: E, indo elles, seguraram o sepulchro com a guarda, sellando a pedra.
texts.mat.28.1: E, no fim do sabbado, quando já começava a despontar para o primeiro dia da semana, Maria Magdalena e a outra Maria foram vêr o sepulchro;
texts.mat.28.2: E eis que houvera um grande terremoto, porque o anjo do Senhor, descendo do céu, chegou, e revolveu a pedra da porta, e estava assentado sobre ella.
texts.mat.28.3: E o seu aspecto era como um relampago, e o seu vestido branco como neve.
texts.mat.28.4: E os guardas, com medo d’elle, ficaram muito assombrados, e tornaram-se como mortos.
texts.mat.28.5: Mas o anjo, fallando, disse ás mulheres: Vós não tenhaes medo; pois eu sei que buscaes a Jesus, que foi crucificado.
texts.mat.28.6: Não está aqui, porque já resuscitou, como havia dito. Vinde, vêde o logar onde o Senhor jazia.
texts.mat.28.7: E ide immediatamente, e dizei aos seus discipulos que já resuscitou dos mortos. E eis que elle vae adiante de vós para a Galilea; ali o vereis. Eis que eu vol-o tenho dito.
texts.mat.28.8: E, saindo ellas pressurosamente do sepulchro, com temor e grande alegria, correram a annuncial-o aos seus discipulos;
texts.mat.28.9: E, indo ellas annuncial-o aos seus discipulos, eis que Jesus lhes sae ao encontro, dizendo: Eu vos saúdo. E ellas, chegando, abraçaram os seus pés, e o adoraram.
texts.mat.28.10: Então Jesus disse-lhes: Não temaes; ide, e annunciae a meus irmãos que vão a Galilea, e lá me verão.
texts.mat.28.11: E, indo ellas, eis que alguns da guarda, chegando á cidade, annunciaram aos principes dos sacerdotes todas as coisas que haviam acontecido.
texts.mat.28.12: E, congregados elles com os anciãos, e tomando conselho entre si, deram muito dinheiro aos soldados, dizendo:
texts.mat.28.13: Dizei: Vieram de noite os seus discipulos e, dormindo nós, o furtaram;
texts.mat.28.14: E, se isto chegar a ser ouvido pelo presidente, nós o persuadiremos, e vos poremos em segurança.
texts.mat.28.15: E elles, recebendo o dinheiro, fizeram como estavam instruidos. E foi divulgado este dito entre os judeos, até ao dia d’hoje.
texts.mat.28.16: E os onze discipulos partiram para Galilea, para o monte, que Jesus lhes tinha destinado.
texts.mat.28.17: E, quando o viram o adoraram; mas alguns duvidaram.
texts.mat.28.18: E, chegando-se Jesus, fallou-lhes, dizendo: É-me dado todo o poder no céu e na terra.
texts.mat.28.19: Portanto ide, ensinae todas as nações, baptizando-as em nome do Pae, e do Filho e do Espirito Sancto;
texts.mat.28.20: Ensinando-as a guardar todas as coisas que eu vos tenho mandado; e eis que eu estou comvosco todos os dias, até á consummação do mundo. Amen.

texts.mat.1.1: The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
texts.mat.1.2: Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judah and his brethren;
texts.mat.1.3: And Judah begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram;
texts.mat.1.4: And Aram begat Aminadab; and Aminadab begat Naasson; and Naasson begat Salmon;
texts.mat.1.5: And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse;
texts.mat.1.6: And Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Uriah;
texts.mat.1.7: And Solomon begat Roboam; and Roboam begat Abia; and Abia begat Asa;
texts.mat.1.8: And Asa begat Josaphat; and Josaphat begat Joram; and Joram begat Ozias;
texts.mat.1.9: And Ozias begat Joatham; and Joatham begat Achaz; and Achaz begat Ezekias;
texts.mat.1.10: And Ezekias begat Manasses; and Manasses begat Amon; and Amon begat Josias;
texts.mat.1.11: And Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren, about the time they were carried away to Babylon:
texts.mat.1.12: And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel;
texts.mat.1.13: And Zorobabel begat Abiud; and Abiud begat Eliakim; and Eliakim begat Azor;
texts.mat.1.14: And Azor begat Sadoc; and Sadoc begat Achim; and Achim begat Eliud;
texts.mat.1.15: And Eliud begat Eleazar; and Eleazar begat Matthan; and Matthan begat Jacob;
texts.mat.1.16: And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
texts.mat.1.17: So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon to Christ are fourteen generations.
texts.mat.1.18: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was in this manner: When his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child by the Holy Spirit.
texts.mat.1.19: Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a public example, purposed to put her away privately.
texts.mat.1.20: But while he thought on these things, the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take to thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is by the Holy Spirit.
texts.mat.1.21: And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.
texts.mat.1.22: Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken from the Lord by the prophet, saying,
texts.mat.1.23: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us.
texts.mat.1.24: Then Joseph, being raised from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took to him his wife:
texts.mat.1.25: And knew her not till she had brought forth her first-born son: and he called his name JESUS.
texts.mat.2.1: Now, after Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,
texts.mat.2.2: Saying, Where is he that is born king of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and have come to worship him.
texts.mat.2.3: When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
texts.mat.2.4: And when he had assembled all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired of them where Christ should be born.
texts.mat.2.5: And they said to him, In Bethlehem of Judea: for thus it is written by the prophet,
texts.mat.2.6: And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, art not the least among the princes of Judah: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.
texts.mat.2.7: Then Herod, when he had privately called the wise men, inquired of them diligently what time the star appeared.
texts.mat.2.8: And he sent them to Bethlehem, and said, Go, and search diligently for the young child; and when ye have found him, bring me word again, that I may come and worship him also.
texts.mat.2.9: When they had heard the king, they departed; and lo, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.
texts.mat.2.10: When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.
texts.mat.2.11: And when they had come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshiped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented to him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
texts.mat.2.12: And being warned by God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way.
texts.mat.2.13: And when they had departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.
texts.mat.2.14: When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt:
texts.mat.2.15: And was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken from the Lord by the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son.
texts.mat.2.16: Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked by the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all its borders, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently inquired of the wise men.
texts.mat.2.17: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, saying,
texts.mat.2.18: In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.
texts.mat.2.19: But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeareth in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
texts.mat.2.20: Saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel: for they are dead who sought the young child's life.
texts.mat.2.21: And he arose, and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel.
texts.mat.2.22: But when he heard that Archelaus reigned in Judea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned by God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee:
texts.mat.2.23: And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.
texts.mat.3.1: In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judea,
texts.mat.3.2: And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
texts.mat.3.3: For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Isaiah, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
texts.mat.3.4: And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his food was locusts and wild honey.
texts.mat.3.5: Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judea, and all the region about Jordan,
texts.mat.3.6: And were baptized by him in Jordan, confessing their sins.
texts.mat.3.7: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said to them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
texts.mat.3.8: Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance:
texts.mat.3.9: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham for our father: for I say to you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children to Abraham.
texts.mat.3.10: And now also the ax is laid to the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.
texts.mat.3.11: I indeed baptize you with water to repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit, and with fire:
texts.mat.3.12: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his floor, and gather his wheat into the granary; but he will burn the chaff with unquenchable fire.
texts.mat.3.13: Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan to John, to be baptized by him.
texts.mat.3.14: But John forbad him, saying, I have need to be baptized by thee, and comest thou to me?
texts.mat.3.15: And Jesus answering said to him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfill all righteousness. Then he suffered him.
texts.mat.3.16: And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up immediately out of the water: and lo, the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:
texts.mat.3.17: And lo, a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
texts.mat.4.1: Then was Jesus led by the Spirit into the wilderness, to be tempted by the devil.
texts.mat.4.2: And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward hungry.
texts.mat.4.3: And when the tempter came to him, he said, If thou art the son of God, command that these stones be made bread.
texts.mat.4.4: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
texts.mat.4.5: Then the devil taketh him up into the holy city, and setteth him on a pinnacle of the temple,
texts.mat.4.6: And saith to him, If thou art the Son of God, cast thyself down, for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee: and in their hands they shall uphold thee, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.
texts.mat.4.7: Jesus said to him, It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.
texts.mat.4.8: Again, the devil taketh him up upon an exceeding high mountain, and showeth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them,
texts.mat.4.9: And saith to him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.
texts.mat.4.10: Then saith Jesus to him, Be gone, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
texts.mat.4.11: Then the devil leaveth him, and behold, angels came and ministered to him.
texts.mat.4.12: Now when Jesus had heard that John was cast into prison, he departed into Galilee.
texts.mat.4.13: And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim;
texts.mat.4.14: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, saying,
texts.mat.4.15: The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles:
texts.mat.4.16: The people who sat in darkness, saw great light; and to them who sat in the region and shades of death, light hath arisen.
texts.mat.4.17: From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
texts.mat.4.18: And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.
texts.mat.4.19: And he saith to them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
texts.mat.4.20: And they immediately left their nets, and followed him.
texts.mat.4.21: And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets: and he called them.
texts.mat.4.22: And they immediately left the boat, and their father, and followed him.
texts.mat.4.23: And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness, and all manner of disease among the people.
texts.mat.4.24: And his fame spread throughout all Syria: and they brought to him all sick people that were taken with diverse diseases and torments, and those who were possessed with demons, and those who were lunatic, and those that had the palsy; and he healed them.
texts.mat.4.25: And there followed him great multitudes of people from Galilee, and from Decapolis, and from Jerusalem, and from Judea, and from beyond Jordan.
texts.mat.5.1: And seeing the multitudes, he ascended a mountain: and when he was seated, his disciples came to him.
texts.mat.5.2: And he opened his mouth, and taught them, saying,
texts.mat.5.3: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.5.4: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
texts.mat.5.5: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.
texts.mat.5.6: Blessed are they who hunger and thirst for righteousness: for they shall be filled.
texts.mat.5.7: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
texts.mat.5.8: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
texts.mat.5.9: Blessed are the peace-makers: for they shall be called children of God.
texts.mat.5.10: Blessed are they who are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.5.11: Blessed are ye when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake.
texts.mat.5.12: Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
texts.mat.5.13: Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt hath lost its savor, with what shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot by men.
texts.mat.5.14: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hid.
texts.mat.5.15: Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a close vessel, but on a candlestick: and it giveth light to all that are in the house.
texts.mat.5.16: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.5.17: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfill.
texts.mat.5.18: For verily I say to you, Till heaven and earth shall pass away, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.
texts.mat.5.19: Whoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whoever shall do, and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.5.20: For I say to you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.5.21: Ye have heard that it was said to them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whoever shall kill, shall be in danger of the judgment:
texts.mat.5.22: But I say to you, That whoever is angry with his brother without a cause, shall be in danger of the judgment: and whoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell-fire.
texts.mat.5.23: Therefore if thou shalt bring thy gift to the altar, and there remember that thy brother hath aught against thee;
texts.mat.5.24: Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.
texts.mat.5.25: Agree with thy adversary quickly, while thou art in the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison.
texts.mat.5.26: Verily, I say to thee, thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou hast paid the uttermost farthing.
texts.mat.5.27: Ye have heard that it was said to them of old time, Thou shalt not commit adultery:
texts.mat.5.28: But I say to you, That whoever looketh on a woman to lust after her, hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.
texts.mat.5.29: And if thy right eye shall cause thee to sin, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.
texts.mat.5.30: And if thy right hand shall cause thee to sin, cut it off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.
texts.mat.5.31: It hath been said, Whoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:
texts.mat.5.32: But I say to you, That whoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of lewdness, causeth her to commit adultery: and whoever shall marry her that is divorced, committeth adultery.
texts.mat.5.33: Again, ye have heard that it hath been said to them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform to the Lord thy oaths:
texts.mat.5.34: But I say to you, Swear not at all: neither by heaven; for it is God's throne:
texts.mat.5.35: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King,
texts.mat.5.36: Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.
texts.mat.5.37: But let your communication be, Yea, yea, Nay, nay: for whatever is more than these cometh of evil.
texts.mat.5.38: Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.
texts.mat.5.39: But I say to you, That ye resist not evil: but whoever shall strike thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.
texts.mat.5.40: And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also.
texts.mat.5.41: And whoever shall constrain thee to go one mile, go with him two.
texts.mat.5.42: Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee, turn not thou away.
texts.mat.5.43: Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbor, and hate thy enemy:
texts.mat.5.44: But I say to you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them who despitefully use you, and persecute you;
texts.mat.5.45: That ye may be the children of your Father who is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.
texts.mat.5.46: For if ye love them who love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same?
texts.mat.5.47: And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? do not even the publicans so?
texts.mat.5.48: Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father who is in heaven is perfect.
texts.mat.6.1: Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen by them: otherwise ye have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.6.2: Therefore, when thou doest thy alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do, in the synagogues, and in the streets, that they may have glory from men. Verily, I say to you, they have their reward.
texts.mat.6.3: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:
texts.mat.6.4: That thy alms may be in secret; and thy Father who seeth in secret, himself will reward thee openly.
texts.mat.6.5: And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues, and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Verily, I say to you, they have their reward.
texts.mat.6.6: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father who is in secret, and thy Father who seeth in secret, will reward thee openly.
texts.mat.6.7: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.
texts.mat.6.8: Therefore be ye not like them: for your Father knoweth what things ye need before ye ask him.
texts.mat.6.9: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
texts.mat.6.10: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
texts.mat.6.11: Give us this day our daily bread.
texts.mat.6.12: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
texts.mat.6.13: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
texts.mat.6.14: For, if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
texts.mat.6.15: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
texts.mat.6.16: Moreover, when ye fast, be not as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear to men to fast. Verily, I say to you, they have their reward.
texts.mat.6.17: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thy head, and wash thy face;
texts.mat.6.18: That thou mayest not appear to men to fast, but to thy Father, who is in secret: and thy Father, who seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.
texts.mat.6.19: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:
texts.mat.6.20: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal.
texts.mat.6.21: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
texts.mat.6.22: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thy eye be single, thy whole body will be full of light.
texts.mat.6.23: But if thy eye be evil, thy whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee is darkness, how great is that darkness!
texts.mat.6.24: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
texts.mat.6.25: Therefore I say to you, Be not anxious for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than food, and the body than raiment?
texts.mat.6.26: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
texts.mat.6.27: Which of you by anxious care can add one cubit to his stature?
texts.mat.6.28: And why are ye anxious for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field how they grow? they toil not, neither do they spin?
texts.mat.6.29: And yet I say to you, that even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
texts.mat.6.30: Wherefore, if God so clotheth the grass of the field, which to-day is, and to-morrow is cast into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?
texts.mat.6.31: Therefore be not anxious, saying, What shall we eat? or what shall we drink? or, with what shall we be clothed?
texts.mat.6.32: (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.
texts.mat.6.33: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you.
texts.mat.6.34: Therefore be not anxious for the morrow: for the morrow will be solicitous for the things of itself. Sufficient to the day is its own evil.
texts.mat.7.1: Judge not, that ye be not judged.
texts.mat.7.2: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and the measure which ye give, shall be measured to you again.
texts.mat.7.3: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thy own eye?
texts.mat.7.4: Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thy eye; and behold, a beam is in thy own eye?
texts.mat.7.5: Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thy own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye.
texts.mat.7.6: Give not that which is holy to dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.
texts.mat.7.7: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and the door shall be opened to you:
texts.mat.7.8: For every one that asketh, receiveth; and he that seeketh, findeth; and to him that knocketh, the door shall be opened.
texts.mat.7.9: Or what man is there of you, who, if his son shall ask bread, will give him a stone?
texts.mat.7.10: Or if he shall ask a fish, will he give him a serpent?
texts.mat.7.11: If ye then being evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more shall your Father who is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?
texts.mat.7.12: Therefore all things whatever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
texts.mat.7.13: Enter ye in at the strait gate; for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there are who go in by it.
texts.mat.7.14: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth to life, and few there are that find it.
texts.mat.7.15: Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.
texts.mat.7.16: Ye shall know them by their fruits: Do men gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles:
texts.mat.7.17: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.
texts.mat.7.18: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.
texts.mat.7.19: Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.
texts.mat.7.20: Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them,
texts.mat.7.21: Not every one that saith to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.7.22: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out demons? and in thy name done many wonderful works?
texts.mat.7.23: And then will I profess to them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.
texts.mat.7.24: Therefore whoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him to a wise man, who built his house upon a rock:
texts.mat.7.25: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.
texts.mat.7.26: And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened to a foolish man, who built his house upon the sand:
texts.mat.7.27: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell, and great was the fall of it.
texts.mat.7.28: And it came to pass when Jesus had ended these sayings, the people were astonished at his doctrine.
texts.mat.7.29: For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
texts.mat.8.1: When he had come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.
texts.mat.8.2: And behold, there came a leper and worshiped him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
texts.mat.8.3: And Jesus put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou clean. And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
texts.mat.8.4: And Jesus saith to him, See thou tell no man; but go, show thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.
texts.mat.8.5: And when Jesus had entered into Capernaum, there came to him a centurion, beseeching him,
texts.mat.8.6: And saying, Lord, my servant lieth at home sick with the palsy, grievously tormented.
texts.mat.8.7: And Jesus saith to him, I will come and heal him.
texts.mat.8.8: The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant will be healed.
texts.mat.8.9: For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
texts.mat.8.10: When Jesus heard it, he marveled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say to you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
texts.mat.8.11: And I say to you, that many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.8.12: But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into utter darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.8.13: And Jesus said to the centurion, Depart; and as thou hast believed, so be it done to thee. And his servant was healed in the same hour.
texts.mat.8.14: And when Jesus had come into Peter's house, he saw his wife's mother laid, and sick with a fever.
texts.mat.8.15: And he touched her hand, and the fever left her: and she arose, and ministered to them.
texts.mat.8.16: When the evening was come, they brought to him many that were possessed with demons: and he cast out the spirits with his word, and healed all that were sick;
texts.mat.8.17: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, saying, He himself took our infirmities, and bore our sicknesses.
texts.mat.8.18: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes about him, he gave commandment to depart to the other side.
texts.mat.8.19: And a certain scribe came, and said to him, Master, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.
texts.mat.8.20: And Jesus saith to him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
texts.mat.8.21: And another of his disciples said to him, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.
texts.mat.8.22: But Jesus said to him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.
texts.mat.8.23: And when he had entered into a boat, his disciples followed him.
texts.mat.8.24: And behold, there arose a great tempest in the sea, insomuch that the boat was covered with the waves: but he was asleep.
texts.mat.8.25: And his disciples came to him, and awoke him, saying, Lord, save us: we perish.
texts.mat.8.26: And he saith to them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
texts.mat.8.27: But the men marveled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!
texts.mat.8.28: And when he had come to the other side, into the country of the Gergesenes, there met him two possessed with demons, coming out of the tombs, exceeding fierce, so that no man might pass by that way.
texts.mat.8.29: And behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?
texts.mat.8.30: And there was a good way off from them a herd of many swine, feeding.
texts.mat.8.31: So the demons besought him, saying, If thou expellest us, suffer us to go away into the herd of swine.
texts.mat.8.32: And he said to them, Go. And when they had come out, they went into the herd of swine: and behold, the whole herd of swine ran violently down a steep place into the sea, and perished in the waters.
texts.mat.8.33: And they that kept them, fled, and went into the city, and told every thing; and what had befallen to the possessed with demons.
texts.mat.8.34: And behold, the whole city came out to meet Jesus: and when they saw him, they besought him that he would depart out of their borders.
texts.mat.9.1: And he entered into a boat, and passed over, and came into his own city.
texts.mat.9.2: And behold, they brought to him a man sick with the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the sick of the palsy, Son, be of good cheer; thy sins are forgiven thee.
texts.mat.9.3: And behold, certain of the scribes said within themselves, This man blasphemeth.
texts.mat.9.4: And Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said, Why think ye evil in your hearts?
texts.mat.9.5: For which is easier, to say, Thy sins are forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk?
texts.mat.9.6: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (then saith he to the sick with the palsy,) Arise, take up thy bed, and go to thy house.
texts.mat.9.7: And he arose, and departed to his house.
texts.mat.9.8: But when the multitude saw it, they marveled, and glorified God, who had given such power to men.
texts.mat.9.9: And as Jesus was passing from thence, he saw a man named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he saith to him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.
texts.mat.9.10: And it came to pass, as Jesus sat at table in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples.
texts.mat.9.11: And when the Pharisees saw it, they said to his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?
texts.mat.9.12: But when Jesus heard that, he said to them, They that are in health need not a physician, but they that are sick.
texts.mat.9.13: But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
texts.mat.9.14: Then came to him the disciples of John, saying, Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but thy disciples fast not?
texts.mat.9.15: And Jesus said to them, Can the children of the bride-chamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then they will fast.
texts.mat.9.16: No man putteth a piece of new cloth to an old garment: for that which is put in to fill it up, taketh from the garment, and the rent is made worse.
texts.mat.9.17: Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.
texts.mat.9.18: While he was speaking these things to them, behold, there came a certain ruler, and worshiped him, saying, My daughter is even now dead: but come and lay thy hand upon her, and she will live.
texts.mat.9.19: And Jesus arose, and followed him, and so did his disciples.
texts.mat.9.20: (And behold, a woman who was diseased with an issue of blood twelve years, came behind him, and touched the hem of his garment.
texts.mat.9.21: For she said within herself, If I may but touch his garment, I shall be whole.
texts.mat.9.22: But Jesus turned himself about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.)
texts.mat.9.23: And when Jesus came into the ruler's house, and saw the minstrels and the people making a noise,
texts.mat.9.24: He said to them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleepeth. And they derided him.
texts.mat.9.25: But when the people were put forth, he went in, and took her by the hand, and the maid arose.
texts.mat.9.26: And the fame of this went abroad into all that land.
texts.mat.9.27: And when Jesus departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, Thou son of David, have mercy on us.
texts.mat.9.28: And when he had come into the house, the blind men came to him: and Jesus saith to them, Believe ye that I am able to do this? They said to him, Yes, Lord.
texts.mat.9.29: Then he touched their eyes, saying, According to your faith, be it to you.
texts.mat.9.30: And their eyes were opened; and Jesus strictly charged them, saying, See that no man know it.
texts.mat.9.31: But they, when they had departed, spread abroad his fame in all that country.
texts.mat.9.32: As thy went out, behold, they brought to him a dumb man possessed with a demon.
texts.mat.9.33: And when the demon was cast out, the dumb spoke: and the multitudes marveled, saying, It was never so seen in Israel.
texts.mat.9.34: But the Pharisees said, He casteth out demons, through the prince of the demons.
texts.mat.9.35: And Jesus went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every sickness, and every disease among the people.
texts.mat.9.36: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.
texts.mat.9.37: Then saith he to his disciples, The harvest truly is plentiful, but the laborers are few.
texts.mat.9.38: Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth laborers into his harvest.
texts.mat.10.1: And when he had called to him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness, and all manner of disease.
texts.mat.10.2: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
texts.mat.10.3: Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alpheus, and Lebbeus, whose surname was Thaddeus;
texts.mat.10.4: Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
texts.mat.10.5: These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and enter ye not into any city of the Samaritans.
texts.mat.10.6: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
texts.mat.10.7: And as ye go, proclaim, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.
texts.mat.10.8: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out demons: freely ye have received, freely give.
texts.mat.10.9: Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses;
texts.mat.10.10: Nor bag for your journey, neither two coats, neither shoes, nor a staff: for the workman is worthy of his food.
texts.mat.10.11: And into whatever city or town ye shall enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and there abide till ye go thence.
texts.mat.10.12: And when ye come into a house, salute it.
texts.mat.10.13: And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you.
texts.mat.10.14: And whoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart from that house, or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
texts.mat.10.15: Verily, I say to you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah, in the day of judgment, than for that city.
texts.mat.10.16: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
texts.mat.10.17: But beware of men: for they will deliver you to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues.
texts.mat.10.18: And ye will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.
texts.mat.10.19: But when they deliver you up, be not anxious how or what ye shall speak, for it shall be given to you in that same hour what ye shall speak.
texts.mat.10.20: For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.
texts.mat.10.21: And the brother will deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child: and the children will rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death.
texts.mat.10.22: And ye will be hated by all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
texts.mat.10.23: But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say to you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel till the Son of man shall have come.
texts.mat.10.24: The disciple is not above his teacher, nor the servant above his lord.
texts.mat.10.25: It is enough for the disciple that he should be as his teacher, and the servant as his lord: if they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more will they call them of his household?
texts.mat.10.26: Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.
texts.mat.10.27: What I tell you in darkness, that speak ye in light: and what ye hear in the ear, that publish ye upon the house-tops.
texts.mat.10.28: And fear not them who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
texts.mat.10.29: Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and not one of them shall fall on the ground without your Father.
texts.mat.10.30: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
texts.mat.10.31: Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.
texts.mat.10.32: Whoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I also confess before my Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.10.33: But whoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.10.34: Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.
texts.mat.10.35: For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
texts.mat.10.36: And a man's foes will be they of his own household.
texts.mat.10.37: He that loveth father or mother more than me, is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me, is not worthy of me.
texts.mat.10.38: And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth me, is not worthy of me.
texts.mat.10.39: He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake, shall find it.
texts.mat.10.40: He that receiveth you, receiveth me, and he that receiveth me, receiveth him that sent me.
texts.mat.10.41: He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet, shall receive a prophet's reward; and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man, shall receive a righteous man's reward.
texts.mat.10.42: And whoever shall give to drink to one of these little ones, a cup of cold water only, in the name of a disciple, verily, I say to you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.
texts.mat.11.1: And it came to pass when Jesus had made an end of commanding his twelve disciples, he departed thence to teach and to preach in their cities.
texts.mat.11.2: Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples,
texts.mat.11.3: And said to him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?
texts.mat.11.4: Jesus answered and said to them, Go and show John again those things which ye hear and see:
texts.mat.11.5: The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.
texts.mat.11.6: And blessed is he to whom I shall not be the cause of his falling into sin.
texts.mat.11.7: And as they departed, Jesus began to say to the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to see? a reed shaken with the wind?
texts.mat.11.8: But what went ye out to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings' houses.
texts.mat.11.9: But what went ye out to see? A prophet? yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
texts.mat.11.10: For this is he concerning whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, who shall prepare thy way before thee.
texts.mat.11.11: Verily, I say to you, among them that are born of women, there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding, he that is least in the kingdom of heaven, is greater than he.
texts.mat.11.12: And from the days of John the Baptist, until now, the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.
texts.mat.11.13: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.
texts.mat.11.14: And if ye will receive it, this is Elijah who was to come.
texts.mat.11.15: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.mat.11.16: But to what shall I liken this generation? It is like to children sitting in the markets, and calling to their fellows,
texts.mat.11.17: And saying, We have piped to you, and ye have not danced; We have mourned to you, and ye have not lamented.
texts.mat.11.18: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He hath a demon.
texts.mat.11.19: The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold, a man gluttonous, and a wine-bibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified by her children.
texts.mat.11.20: Then he began to upbraid the cities in which most of his mighty works had been done, because they repented not.
texts.mat.11.21: Woe to thee, Chorazin; woe to thee, Bethsaida: for if the mighty works which have been done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
texts.mat.11.22: But I say to you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.
texts.mat.11.23: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.
texts.mat.11.24: But I say to you, that it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom, in the day of judgment, than for thee.
texts.mat.11.25: At that time Jesus answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to babes.
texts.mat.11.26: Even so, Father, for so it seemed good in thy sight.
texts.mat.11.27: All things are delivered to me by my Father; and no man knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.
texts.mat.11.28: Come to me, all ye that labor, and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
texts.mat.11.29: Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me: for I am meek and lowly in heart; and ye shall find rest to your souls.
texts.mat.11.30: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
texts.mat.12.1: At that time Jesus went on the sabbath through the corn, and his disciples were hungry, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat.
texts.mat.12.2: But when the Pharisees saw it, they said to him, Behold, thy disciples do that which it is not lawful to do on the sabbath.
texts.mat.12.3: But he said to them, Have ye not read what David did when he was hungry, and they that were with him;
texts.mat.12.4: How he entered into the house of God, and ate the show-bread, which it was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them who were with him, but only for the priests?
texts.mat.12.5: Or have ye not read in the law, that on the sabbath the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?
texts.mat.12.6: But I say to you, that in this place is one greater than the temple.
texts.mat.12.7: But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.
texts.mat.12.8: For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath.
texts.mat.12.9: And when he had departed thence, he went into their synagogue.
texts.mat.12.10: And behold, there was a man who had his hand withered. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath? that they might accuse him.
texts.mat.12.11: And he said to them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it shall fall into a pit on the sabbath, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out?
texts.mat.12.12: How much then is a man better than a sheep? wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.
texts.mat.12.13: Then saith he to the man, Stretch out thy hand. And he stretched it out; and it was restored to a sound state like the other.
texts.mat.12.14: Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.
texts.mat.12.15: But when Jesus knew it, he withdrew himself from thence: and great multitudes followed him, and he healed them all.
texts.mat.12.16: And charged them that they should not make him known:
texts.mat.12.17: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, saying,
texts.mat.12.18: Behold, my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit upon him, and he shall show judgment to the Gentiles.
texts.mat.12.19: He shall not contend, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets.
texts.mat.12.20: A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he shall send forth judgment to victory.
texts.mat.12.21: And in his name shall the Gentiles trust.
texts.mat.12.22: Then was brought to him one possessed with a demon, blind and dumb; and he healed him, so that the blind and dumb both spoke and saw.
texts.mat.12.23: And all the people were amazed, and said, Is not this the son of David?
texts.mat.12.24: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, This man doth not cast out demons, but by Beelzebub the prince of the demons.
texts.mat.12.25: And Jesus knew their thoughts, and said to them, Every kingdom divided against itself, is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself, shall not stand.
texts.mat.12.26: And if Satan casteth out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then shall his kingdom stand?
texts.mat.12.27: And if I by Beelzebub cast out demons, by whom do your children expel them? therefore they shall be your judges.
texts.mat.12.28: But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come to you.
texts.mat.12.29: Or else, how can one enter into a strong man's house, and seize his goods, except he shall first bind the strong man? and then he will plunder his house.
texts.mat.12.30: He that is not with me, is against me; and he that gathereth not with me, scattereth abroad.
texts.mat.12.31: Wherefore I say to you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven to men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit shall not be forgiven to men.
texts.mat.12.32: And whoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whoever speaketh against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.
texts.mat.12.33: Either make the tree good, and its fruit good; or else make the tree corrupt, and its fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by its fruit.
texts.mat.12.34: O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaketh.
texts.mat.12.35: A good man, out of the good treasure of the heart, bringeth forth good things: and an evil man, out of the evil treasure, bringeth forth evil things.
texts.mat.12.36: But I say to you, That for every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account in the day of judgment.
texts.mat.12.37: For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.
texts.mat.12.38: Then certain of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from thee.
texts.mat.12.39: But he answered and said to them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh for a sign, and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonah.
texts.mat.12.40: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the whale's belly: so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
texts.mat.12.41: The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, a greater than Jonah is here.
texts.mat.12.42: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, a greater than Solomon is here.
texts.mat.12.43: When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and he findeth none.
texts.mat.12.44: Then he saith, I will return into my house from whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished.
texts.mat.12.45: Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also to this wicked generation.
texts.mat.12.46: While he was yet speaking to the people, behold, his mother and his brethren stood without, desiring to speak with him.
texts.mat.12.47: Then one said to him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to speak with thee.
texts.mat.12.48: But he answered and said to him that told him, Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?
texts.mat.12.49: And he stretched forth his hand towards his disciples, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren!
texts.mat.12.50: For whoever shall do the will of my Father who is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.
texts.mat.13.1: The same day Jesus went out of the house, and sat by the sea side.
texts.mat.13.2: And great multitudes were gathered to him, so that he went into a boat, and sat down; and the whole multitude stood on the shore.
texts.mat.13.3: And he spoke many things to them in parables, saying, Behold, a sower went forth to sow;
texts.mat.13.4: And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them:
texts.mat.13.5: Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth:
texts.mat.13.6: And when the sun had risen, they were scorched; and because they had not root, they withered.
texts.mat.13.7: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them:
texts.mat.13.8: But others fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some a hundred-fold, some sixty-fold, some thirty-fold.
texts.mat.13.9: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.mat.13.10: And the disciples came, and said to him, Why speakest thou to them in parables?
texts.mat.13.11: He answered and said to them, Because it is given to you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.
texts.mat.13.12: For whoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that which he hath.
texts.mat.13.13: Therefore I speak to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.
texts.mat.13.14: And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive:
texts.mat.13.15: For this people's heart is become gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
texts.mat.13.16: But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.
texts.mat.13.17: For verily I say to you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see the things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear the things which ye hear, and have not heard them.
texts.mat.13.18: Hear ye therefore the parable of the sower.
texts.mat.13.19: When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he who received seed by the way side.
texts.mat.13.20: But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and immediately with joy receiveth it;
texts.mat.13.21: Yet he hath not root in himself, but endureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, forthwith he is offended.
texts.mat.13.22: He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful.
texts.mat.13.23: But he that receiveth seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; who also beareth fruit, and bringeth forth, some a hundred fold, some sixty, some thirty.
texts.mat.13.24: Another parable he proposed to them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened to a man who sowed good seed in his field:
texts.mat.13.25: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and departed.
texts.mat.13.26: But when the blade had sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also.
texts.mat.13.27: So the servants of the householder came and said to him, Sir, didst thou not sow good seed in thy field? from whence then hath it tares?
texts.mat.13.28: He said to them, An enemy hath done this. The servants said to him, Wilt thou then that we go and gather them?
texts.mat.13.29: But he said, No; lest while ye gather the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them.
texts.mat.13.30: Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn.
texts.mat.13.31: Another parable he proposed to them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard-seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:
texts.mat.13.32: Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge on its branches.
texts.mat.13.33: Another parable he spoke to them; The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.
texts.mat.13.34: All these things Jesus spoke to the multitude in parables; and without a parable he spoke not to them:
texts.mat.13.35: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.
texts.mat.13.36: Then Jesus sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came to him, saying, Declare to us the parable of the tares of the field.
texts.mat.13.37: He answered and said to them, He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man;
texts.mat.13.38: The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one;
texts.mat.13.39: The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels.
texts.mat.13.40: As therefore the tares are gathered and burned in the fire; so shall it be in the end of this world.
texts.mat.13.41: The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them who do iniquity;
texts.mat.13.42: And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.13.43: Then shall the righteous shine as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.mat.13.44: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like treasure hid in a field; which, when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.
texts.mat.13.45: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant seeking goodly pearls:
texts.mat.13.46: Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
texts.mat.13.47: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:
texts.mat.13.48: Which, when it was full, they drew to the shore, and sat down, and gathered the good into vessels, but cast away the bad.
texts.mat.13.49: So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just,
texts.mat.13.50: And shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.13.51: Jesus saith to them, Have ye understood all these things? They say to him, Yes, Lord.
texts.mat.13.52: Then said he to them, Therefore every scribe who is instructed to the kingdom of heaven, is like a man that is a householder, who bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old.
texts.mat.13.53: And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence.
texts.mat.13.54: And when he had come into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished, and said, Whence hath this man this wisdom, and these mighty works?
texts.mat.13.55: Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?
texts.mat.13.56: And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?
texts.mat.13.57: And they were offended in him. But Jesus said to them, A prophet is not without honor, save in his own country, and in his own house.
texts.mat.13.58: And he did not many mighty works there, because of their unbelief.
texts.mat.14.1: At that time Herod the Tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus,
texts.mat.14.2: And said to his servants, This is John the Baptist; he hath risen from the dead; and therefore mighty works do show forth themselves in him.
texts.mat.14.3: For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife.
texts.mat.14.4: For John had said to him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.
texts.mat.14.5: And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.
texts.mat.14.6: But when Herod's birth-day was kept, the daughter of Herodias danced before them, and pleased Herod.
texts.mat.14.7: Upon which he promised with an oath to give her whatever she would ask.
texts.mat.14.8: And she, being before instructed by her mother, said, Give me here the head of John the Baptist in a dish.
texts.mat.14.9: And the king was sorry: nevertheless for the sake of the oath, and of them who sat with him at table, he commanded it to be given her.
texts.mat.14.10: And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison.
texts.mat.14.11: And his head was brought in a dish, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother.
texts.mat.14.12: And his disciples came, and took up the body, and buried it, and went and told Jesus.
texts.mat.14.13: When Jesus heard of it, he departed thence in a boat, into a desert place apart: and when the people had heard of it, they followed him on foot out of the cities.
texts.mat.14.14: And Jesus went forth, and saw a great multitude, and was moved with compassion towards them, and he healed their sick.
texts.mat.14.15: And when it was evening, his disciples came to him, saying, This is a desert place, and the time is now past; send the multitude away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves victuals.
texts.mat.14.16: But Jesus said to them, They need not depart; give ye them to eat.
texts.mat.14.17: And they say to him, We have here but five loaves, and two fishes.
texts.mat.14.18: He said, Bring them hither to me.
texts.mat.14.19: And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and broke, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.
texts.mat.14.20: And they all ate, and were satisfied: and they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full.
texts.mat.14.21: And they that had eaten were about five thousand men, besides women and children.
texts.mat.14.22: And immediately Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a boat, and to go before him to the other side, while he sent the multitudes away.
texts.mat.14.23: And when he had sent the multitudes away, he ascended a mountain apart to pray: and when the evening was come, he was there alone.
texts.mat.14.24: But the boat was now in the midst of the sea, tossed with waves: for the wind was contrary.
texts.mat.14.25: And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went to them, walking on the sea.
texts.mat.14.26: And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear.
texts.mat.14.27: But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.
texts.mat.14.28: And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it is thou, bid me come to thee on the water.
texts.mat.14.29: And he said, Come. And when Peter had come down out of the boat, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus.
texts.mat.14.30: But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me.
texts.mat.14.31: And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said to him, O thou of little faith, Why didst thou doubt?
texts.mat.14.32: And when they had come into the boat, the wind ceased.
texts.mat.14.33: Then they that were in the boat came and worshiped him, saying, In truth thou art the son of God.
texts.mat.14.34: And when they had gone over, they came into the land of Gennesaret.
texts.mat.14.35: And when the men of that place had knowledge of him, they sent out into all the surrounding country, and brought to him all that were diseased;
texts.mat.14.36: And besought him that they might only touch the hem of his garment: and as many as touched were restored to health.
texts.mat.15.1: Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, who were of Jerusalem, saying,
texts.mat.15.2: Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.
texts.mat.15.3: But he answered and said to them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition?
texts.mat.15.4: For God commanded, saying, Honor thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.
texts.mat.15.5: But ye say, Whoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatever thou mightest be profited by me;
texts.mat.15.6: And honor not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of God of no effect by your tradition.
texts.mat.15.7: Ye hypocrites, well did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,
texts.mat.15.8: This people draw nigh to me with their mouth, and honor me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.
texts.mat.15.9: But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
texts.mat.15.10: And he called the multitude, and said to them, Hear, and understand:
