texts.mat.15.11: Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.
texts.mat.15.12: Then came his disciples, and said to him, Knowest thou that the Pharisees were offended after they heard this saying?
texts.mat.15.13: But he answered and said, Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be extirpated.
texts.mat.15.14: Let them alone: they are blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind leadeth the blind, both will fall into the ditch.
texts.mat.15.15: Then answered Peter and said to him, Declare to us this parable.
texts.mat.15.16: And Jesus said, Are ye also yet without understanding?
texts.mat.15.17: Do ye not yet understand, that whatever entereth in at the mouth goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?
texts.mat.15.18: But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.
texts.mat.15.19: For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies:
texts.mat.15.20: These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man.
texts.mat.15.21: Then Jesus went thence, and departed into the territories of Tyre and Sidon.
texts.mat.15.22: And behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same territories, and cried to him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou son of David; my daughter is grievously afflicted with a demon.
texts.mat.15.23: But he answered her not a word. And his disciples came and besought him, saying, Send her away; for she crieth after us.
texts.mat.15.24: But he answered and said, I am not sent but to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
texts.mat.15.25: Then came she and worshiped him, saying, Lord, help me.
texts.mat.15.26: But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children's bread, and to cast it to dogs.
texts.mat.15.27: And she said, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crums which fall from their master's table.
texts.mat.15.28: Then Jesus answered and said to her, O woman, great is thy faith: be it to thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was healed from that very hour.
texts.mat.15.29: And Jesus departed from thence, and came nigh to the sea of Galilee; and ascended a mountain, and sat down there.
texts.mat.15.30: And great multitudes came to him, having with them those that were lame, blind, dumb, maimed, and many others, and cast them down at Jesus' feet; and he healed them:
texts.mat.15.31: So that the multitude wondered, when they saw the dumb to speak, the maimed to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see: and they glorified the God of Israel.
texts.mat.15.32: Then Jesus called his disciples to him, and said, I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days, and have nothing to eat: and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way.
texts.mat.15.33: And his disciples say to him, Whence should we have so much bread in the wilderness, as to satisfy so great a multitude?
texts.mat.15.34: And Jesus saith to them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven, and a few little fishes.
texts.mat.15.35: And he commanded the multitude to sit on the ground.
texts.mat.15.36: And he took the seven loaves and the fishes, and gave thanks, and broke them, and gave to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.
texts.mat.15.37: And they all ate and were filled: and they took up of the fragments that were left seven baskets full.
texts.mat.15.38: And they that had eaten were four thousand men, besides women and children.
texts.mat.15.39: And he sent away the multitude, and took a boat, and came into the borders of Magdala.
texts.mat.16.1: The Pharisees also and the Sadducees came, and, tempting, desired him that he would show them a sign from heaven.
texts.mat.16.2: He answered and said to them, When it is evening, ye say, It will be fair weather: for the sky is red.
texts.mat.16.3: And in the morning, It will be foul weather to-day: for the sky is red and lowering. O ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky; but can ye not discern the signs of the times?
texts.mat.16.4: A wicked and adulterous generation seeketh for a sign; and there shall no sign been to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonah. And he left them, and departed.
texts.mat.16.5: And when his disciples had come to the other side, they had forgotten to take bread.
texts.mat.16.6: Then Jesus said to them, Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.
texts.mat.16.7: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have taken no bread.
texts.mat.16.8: Which when Jesus perceived, he said to them, O ye of little faith, why reason ye among yourselves, because ye have brought no bread?
texts.mat.16.9: Do ye not yet understand, neither remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?
texts.mat.16.10: Neither the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?
texts.mat.16.11: How is it that ye do not understand that I spoke not to you concerning bread, that ye should beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees?
texts.mat.16.12: Then they understood that he did not caution them against the leaven of bread, but against the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.
texts.mat.16.13: When Jesus came into the borders of Cesarea Phillippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Who do men say that I the Son of man am?
texts.mat.16.14: And they said, Some say that thou art John the Baptist: some Elijah; and others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.
texts.mat.16.15: He saith to them, But who say ye that I am?
texts.mat.16.16: And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.
texts.mat.16.17: And Jesus answered and said to him, Blessed art thou, Simon-Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it to thee, but my Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.16.18: And I say also to thee, that thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church: and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
texts.mat.16.19: And I will give to thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatever thou shalt bind on earth, shall be bound in heaven; and whatever thou shalt loose on earth, shall be loosed in heaven.
texts.mat.16.20: Then he charged his disciples that they should tell no man that he was Jesus the Christ.
texts.mat.16.21: From that time forth Jesus began to show to his disciples, that he must go to Jerusalem, and suffer many things from the elders and chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.
texts.mat.16.22: Then Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be to thee.
texts.mat.16.23: But he turned, and said to Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan; thou art an offense to me: for thou savorest not the things that are of God, but those that are of men.
texts.mat.16.24: Then said Jesus to his disciples, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
texts.mat.16.25: For whoever will save his life, shall lose it: and whoever will lose his life for my sake, shall find it.
texts.mat.16.26: For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?
texts.mat.16.27: For the Son of man will come in the glory of his Father, with his angels; and then he will reward every man according to his works.
texts.mat.16.28: Verily I say to you, There are some standing here, who shall not taste death, till they shall see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.
texts.mat.17.1: And after six days, Jesus taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them upon a high mountain apart.
texts.mat.17.2: And he was transfigured before them: and his face shone as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.
texts.mat.17.3: And behold, there appeared to them Moses and Elijah talking with him.
texts.mat.17.4: Then answered Peter, and said to Jesus, Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
texts.mat.17.5: While he was yet speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold, a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear ye him.
texts.mat.17.6: And when the disciples heard it, they fell on their face, and were in great fear.
texts.mat.17.7: And Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid.
texts.mat.17.8: And when they had lifted up their eyes, they saw no man, save Jesus only.
texts.mat.17.9: And as they were descending the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying, Tell the vision to no man, until the Son of man be raised again from the dead.
texts.mat.17.10: And his disciples asked him, saying, Why then say the scribes, that Elijah must first come?
texts.mat.17.11: And Jesus answered and said to them, Elijah truly will first come, and restore all things:
texts.mat.17.12: But I say to you, that Elijah is come already, and they knew him not, but have done to him whatever they pleased: likewise will also the Son of man suffer by them.
texts.mat.17.13: Then the disciples understood that he spoke to them concerning John the Baptist.
texts.mat.17.14: And when they had come to the multitude, there came to him a certain man kneeling down to him, and saying,
texts.mat.17.15: Lord, have mercy on my son; for he is lunatic, and grievously distressed; for often he falleth into the fire, and often into the water.
texts.mat.17.16: And I brought him to thy disciples, and they could not cure him.
texts.mat.17.17: Then Jesus answered and said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him hither to me.
texts.mat.17.18: And Jesus rebuked the demon, and he departed out of him: and the child was cured from that very hour.
texts.mat.17.19: Then came the disciples to Jesus apart, and said, Why could not we cast him out?
texts.mat.17.20: And Jesus said to them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say to you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard-seed, ye shall say to this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place, and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible to you.
texts.mat.17.21: However, this kind goeth not out, but by prayer and fasting.
texts.mat.17.22: And while they abode in Galilee, Jesus said to them, The Son of man will be betrayed into the hands of men:
texts.mat.17.23: And they will kill him, and the third day he will be raised again: And they were exceedingly grieved.
texts.mat.17.24: And when they had come to Capernaum, they that received tribute-money, came to Peter, and said, Doth not your Master pay tribute?
texts.mat.17.25: He saith, Yes. And when he had come into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying, What thinkest thou, Simon? from whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? from their own children, or from strangers?
texts.mat.17.26: Peter saith to him, From strangers. Jesus saith to him, Then are the children free.
texts.mat.17.27: Notwithstanding, lest we should offend them, go thou to the sea, and cast a hook, and take the fish that first cometh up: and when thou hast opened his mouth, thou shalt find a piece of money: take that, and give to them for me and thee.
texts.mat.18.1: At the same time came the disciples to Jesus, saying, Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
texts.mat.18.2: And Jesus called a little child to him, and set him in the midst of them,
texts.mat.18.3: And said, Verily I say to you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.18.4: Whoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.18.5: And whoever shall receive one such little child in my name, receiveth me.
texts.mat.18.6: But whoever shall cause one of these little ones who believe in me, to sin, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.
texts.mat.18.7: Woe to the world because of offenses! for it must needs be that offenses come; but woe to that man by whom the offense cometh!
texts.mat.18.8: Wherefore, if thy hand or thy foot causeth thee to sin, cut them off, and cast them from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life halt or maimed, rather than having two hands or two feet, to be cast into everlasting fire.
texts.mat.18.9: And if thy eye causeth thee to sin, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes, to be cast into hell-fire.
texts.mat.18.10: Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones: for I say to you, that in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.18.11: For the Son of man is come to save that which was lost.
texts.mat.18.12: How think ye? if a man hath a hundred sheep, and one of them is gone astray, doth he not leave the ninety and nine, and go to the mountains, and seek that which is gone astray?
texts.mat.18.13: And if he findeth it, verily I say to you, he rejoiceth more over that sheep, than over the ninety and nine which went not astray.
texts.mat.18.14: Even so it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish.
texts.mat.18.15: Moreover, if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.
texts.mat.18.16: But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.
texts.mat.18.17: And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it to the church: but if he shall neglect to hear the church, let him be to thee as a heathen and a publican.
texts.mat.18.18: Verily I say to you, Whatever ye shall bind on earth, shall be bound in heaven: and whatever ye shall loose on earth, shall be loosed in heaven.
texts.mat.18.19: Again I say to you, That if two of you shall agree on earth, concerning any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.18.20: For where two or three are assembled in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
texts.mat.18.21: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?
texts.mat.18.22: Jesus saith to him, I say not to thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.
texts.mat.18.23: Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened to a certain king who would take account of his servants.
texts.mat.18.24: And when he had begun to reckon, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents.
texts.mat.18.25: But as he had not ability to pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.
texts.mat.18.26: The servant therefore fell down, and worshiped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.
texts.mat.18.27: Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt.
texts.mat.18.28: But the same servant went out, and found one of his fellow-servants, who owed him a hundred pence: and he laid hands on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me what thou owest.
texts.mat.18.29: And his fellow-servant fell down at his feet, and besought him, saying, Have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.
texts.mat.18.30: And he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay the debt.
texts.mat.18.31: So when his fellow-servants saw what was done, they were very sorry, and came and told to their lord all that was done.
texts.mat.18.32: Then his lord, having called him, said to him, O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me:
texts.mat.18.33: Shouldst thou not also have had compassion on thy fellow-servant, even as I had pity on thee?
texts.mat.18.34: And his lord was wroth, and delivered him to the tormentors, till he should pay all that was due to him.
texts.mat.18.35: So likewise shall my heavenly Father do to you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.
texts.mat.19.1: And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these sayings, he departed from Galilee, and came into the borders of Judea, beyond Jordan:
texts.mat.19.2: And great multitudes followed him, and he healed them there.
texts.mat.19.3: The Pharisees also came to him, tempting him, and saying to him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?
texts.mat.19.4: And he answered and said to them, Have ye not read, that he who made them, at the beginning made them male and female,
texts.mat.19.5: And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they two shall be one flesh?
texts.mat.19.6: Wherefore they are no more two, but one flesh. Therefore what God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
texts.mat.19.7: They say to him, Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away?
texts.mat.19.8: He saith to them, Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so.
texts.mat.19.9: And I say to you, Whoever shall put away his wife, except for lewdness, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and whoever marrieth her who is put away, committeth adultery.
texts.mat.19.10: His disciples say to him, If the case of the man is so with his wife, it is not good to marry.
texts.mat.19.11: But he said to them, All men cannot receive this saying, save they to whom it is given.
texts.mat.19.12: For there are some eunuchs, who were so born from their mothers womb: and there are some eunuchs, who were made eunuchs by men: and there are eunuchs, who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven's sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it.
texts.mat.19.13: Then were brought to him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them.
texts.mat.19.14: But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not to come to me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.19.15: And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence.
texts.mat.19.16: And behold, one came and said to him, Good Master, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?
texts.mat.19.17: And he said to him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God: but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.
texts.mat.19.18: He saith to him, Which? Jesus said, Thou shalt do no murder, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness,
texts.mat.19.19: Honor thy father and thy mother: and, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.
texts.mat.19.20: The young man saith to him, All these things have I kept from my youth: what lack I yet?
texts.mat.19.21: Jesus said to him, If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell what thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.
texts.mat.19.22: But when the young man heard that saying, he went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions.
texts.mat.19.23: Then said Jesus to his disciples, Verily I say to you, that a rich man shall with difficulty enter into the kingdom of heaven.
texts.mat.19.24: And again I say to you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
texts.mat.19.25: When his disciples heard it, they were exceedingly amazed, saying, Who then can be saved?
texts.mat.19.26: But Jesus beheld them, and said to them, With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.
texts.mat.19.27: Then answered Peter, and said to him, Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee? what shall we have therefore?
texts.mat.19.28: And Jesus said to them, Verily I say to you, that ye who have followed me in the regeneration, when the Son of man shall sit on the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
texts.mat.19.29: And every one that hath forsaken houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands for my name's sake, shall receive a hundred-fold, and shall inherit everlasting life.
texts.mat.19.30: But many that are first shall be last, and the last shall be first.
texts.mat.20.1: For the kingdom of heaven is like to a man that is a householder, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers into his vineyard.
texts.mat.20.2: And when he had agreed with the laborers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
texts.mat.20.3: And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the market-place,
texts.mat.20.4: And said to them, Go ye also into the vineyard; and whatever is right, I will give you. And they departed.
texts.mat.20.5: Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hour, and did likewise.
texts.mat.20.6: And about the eleventh hour he went out, and found others standing idle, and saith to them, Why stand ye here all the day idle?
texts.mat.20.7: They say to him, Because no man hath hired us. He saith to them, Go ye also into the vineyard; and whatever is right, that shall ye receive.
texts.mat.20.8: So when evening was come, the lord of the vineyard saith to his steward, Call the laborers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last to the first.
texts.mat.20.9: And when they came that were hired about the eleventh hour, they received every man a penny.
texts.mat.20.10: But when the first came, they supposed that they should receive more; and they likewise received every man a penny.
texts.mat.20.11: And when they had received it, they murmured against the master of the house.
texts.mat.20.12: Saying, These last have wrought but one hour, and thou hast made them equal to us, who have borne the burden and heat of the day.
texts.mat.20.13: But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst thou not agree with me for a penny?
texts.mat.20.14: Take that which is thine, and depart: I will give to this last, even as to thee.
texts.mat.20.15: Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with my own? is thy eye evil because I am good?
texts.mat.20.16: So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many are called, but few chosen.
texts.mat.20.17: And Jesus going up to Jerusalem, took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said to them,
texts.mat.20.18: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man will be betrayed to the chief priests, and to the scribes, and they will condemn him to death,
texts.mat.20.19: And will deliver him to the Gentiles to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify him: and the third day he will rise again.
texts.mat.20.20: Then came to him the mother of Zebedee's children, with her sons, worshiping him, and desiring a certain thing of him.
texts.mat.20.21: And he said to her, What wilt thou: She saith to him, Grant that these my two sons may sit, the one on thy right hand, and the other on the left in thy kingdom.
texts.mat.20.22: But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say to him, We are able.
texts.mat.20.23: And he saith to them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared by my Father.
texts.mat.20.24: And when the ten heard it, they were moved with indignation against the two brethren.
texts.mat.20.25: But Jesus called them to him, and said, Ye know that the princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them.
texts.mat.20.26: But it shall not be so among you: but whoever will be great among you, let him be your minister;
texts.mat.20.27: And whoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant:
texts.mat.20.28: Even as the Son of man came not to be ministered to, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
texts.mat.20.29: And as they departed from Jericho, a great multitude followed him.
texts.mat.20.30: And behold, two blind men sitting by the way-side, when they heard that Jesus passed by, cried out, saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, thou son of David.
texts.mat.20.31: And the multitude rebuked them, that they should hold their peace: but they cried the more, saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, thou son of David.
texts.mat.20.32: And Jesus stood still, and called them, and said, What will ye that I shall do to you?
texts.mat.20.33: They say to him, Lord, that our eyes may be opened.
texts.mat.20.34: So Jesus had compassion on them, and touched their eyes: and immediately their eyes received sight, and they followed him.
texts.mat.21.1: And when they drew nigh to Jerusalem, and had come to Bethphage, to the mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
texts.mat.21.2: Saying to them, Go into the village over against you, and immediately ye shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her, loose them, and bring them to me.
texts.mat.21.3: And if any man shall say aught to you, ye shall say, The Lord hath need of them; and immediately he will send them.
texts.mat.21.4: All this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying,
texts.mat.21.5: Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh to thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass.
texts.mat.21.6: And the disciples went, and did as Jesus commanded them,
texts.mat.21.7: And brought the ass and the colt, and put on them their clothes, and they set him thereon.
texts.mat.21.8: And a very great multitude spread their garments in the way; others cut down branches from the trees, and strewed them in the way.
texts.mat.21.9: And the multitudes that went before, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the son of David: blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord: Hosanna in the highest.
texts.mat.21.10: And when he had come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, Who is this?
texts.mat.21.11: And the multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee.
texts.mat.21.12: And Jesus went into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the money-changers, and the seats of them that sold doves.
texts.mat.21.13: And said to them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer, but ye have made it a den of thieves.
texts.mat.21.14: And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple; and he healed them.
texts.mat.21.15: And when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, and saying, Hosanna to the son of David; they were greatly displeased,
texts.mat.21.16: And said to him, Hearest thou what these say? And Jesus saith to them, Yes: have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise?
texts.mat.21.17: And he left them, and went out of the city into Bethany, and he lodged there.
texts.mat.21.18: Now in the morning as he was returning into the city, he was hungry.
texts.mat.21.19: And when he saw a fig-tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing on it, but leaves only, and said to it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforth for ever. And immediately the fig-tree withered.
texts.mat.21.20: And when the disciples saw it, they marveled, saying, How soon is the fig-tree withered!
texts.mat.21.21: Jesus answered and said to them, Verily I say to you, If ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only do this which is done to the fig-tree, but also, if ye shall say to this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; it shall be done.
texts.mat.21.22: And all things whatever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.
texts.mat.21.23: And when he had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him as he was teaching, and said, By what authority doest thou these things; and who gave thee this authority?
texts.mat.21.24: And Jesus answered and said to them, I also will ask you one thing, which if ye tell me, I also will tell you by what authority I do these things.
texts.mat.21.25: The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven, or from men? And they reasoned with themselves, saying, if we shall say, From heaven; he will say to us, Why then did ye not believe him?
texts.mat.21.26: But if we shall say, From men; we fear the people: for all hold John as a prophet.
texts.mat.21.27: And they answered Jesus, and said, We cannot tell. And he said to them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
texts.mat.21.28: But what think ye? A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go, work to-day in my vineyard.
texts.mat.21.29: He answered and said, I will not; but afterward he repented, and went.
texts.mat.21.30: And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.
texts.mat.21.31: Which of the two did the will of his father? They say to him, The first. Jesus saith to them, Verily I say to you, that the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.
texts.mat.21.32: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.
texts.mat.21.33: Hear another parable; There was a certain householder, who planted a vineyard, and hedged it around, and digged a wine-press in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a remote country:
texts.mat.21.34: And when the time of the fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, that they might receive the fruits of it.
texts.mat.21.35: And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.
texts.mat.21.36: Again he sent other servants more than the first: and they did to them in like manner.
texts.mat.21.37: But last of all he sent to them his son, saying, They will reverence my son.
texts.mat.21.38: But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance.
texts.mat.21.39: And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.
texts.mat.21.40: When therefore the Lord of the vineyard cometh, what will he do to those husbandmen?
texts.mat.21.41: They say to him, He will miserably destroy those wicked men, and will let out his vineyard to other husbandmen, who will render him the fruits in their seasons.
texts.mat.21.42: Jesus saith to them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord's doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes?
texts.mat.21.43: Therefore I say to you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits of it.
texts.mat.21.44: And whoever shall fall on this stone, shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.
texts.mat.21.45: And when the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables, they perceived that he spoke of them.
texts.mat.21.46: But when they sought to lay hands on him, they feared the multitude, because they took him for a prophet.
texts.mat.22.1: And Jesus answered, and spoke to them again by parables, and said,
texts.mat.22.2: The kingdom of heaven is like to a certain king, who made a marriage for his son,
texts.mat.22.3: And sent his servants to call them that were invited to the wedding: and they would not come.
texts.mat.22.4: Again, he sent other servants, saying, Tell them who are invited, Behold, I have prepared my dinner: my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come to the marriage.
texts.mat.22.5: But they made light of it, and went, one to his farm, another to his merchandise.
texts.mat.22.6: And the remnant took his servants, and treated them spitefully, and slew them.
texts.mat.22.7: But when the king heard of it, he was wroth: and he sent his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city.
texts.mat.22.8: Then he saith to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they who were invited were not worthy.
texts.mat.22.9: Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, invite to the marriage.
texts.mat.22.10: So those servants went out into the highways, and collected all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.
texts.mat.22.11: And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man who had not a wedding-garment:
texts.mat.22.12: And he saith to him, Friend, how camest thou in hither, not having a wedding-garment? And he was speechless.
texts.mat.22.13: Then said the king to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into utter darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.22.14: For many are called, but few are chosen.
texts.mat.22.15: Then went the Pharisees, and took counsel how they might entangle him in his talk.
texts.mat.22.16: And they sent out to him their disciples, with the Herodians, saying, Master, we know that thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth, neither carest thou for any man: for thou regardest not the person of men.
texts.mat.22.17: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute to Cesar, or not?
texts.mat.22.18: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites?
texts.mat.22.19: Show me the tribute-money. And they brought to him a penny.
texts.mat.22.20: And he saith to them, Whose is this image, and superscription?
texts.mat.22.21: They say to him, Cesar's. Then saith he to them, Render therefore to Cesar, the things which are Cesar's; and to God, the things that are God's.
texts.mat.22.22: When they had heard these words, they marveled, and left him, and departed.
texts.mat.22.23: The same day came to him the Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, and asked him,
texts.mat.22.24: Saying, Master, Moses said, If a man shall die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed to his brother.
texts.mat.22.25: Now there were with us seven brothers: and the first, when he had married a wife, deceased; and having no issue, left his wife to his brother.
texts.mat.22.26: Likewise the second also, and the third, to the seventh.
texts.mat.22.27: And last of all the woman died also.
texts.mat.22.28: Therefore in the resurrection, whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.
texts.mat.22.29: Jesus answered and said to them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.
texts.mat.22.30: For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.
texts.mat.22.31: But as concerning the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,
texts.mat.22.32: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.
texts.mat.22.33: And when the multitude heard this, they were astonished at his doctrine.
texts.mat.22.34: But when the Pharisees had heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, they were assembled about him.
texts.mat.22.35: Then one of them who was a lawyer, asked him a question, tempting him, and saying,
texts.mat.22.36: Master, which is the great commandment in the law?
texts.mat.22.37: Jesus said to him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
texts.mat.22.38: This is the first and great commandment.
texts.mat.22.39: And the second is like it, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.
texts.mat.22.40: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
texts.mat.22.41: While the Pharisees were assembled, Jesus asked them,
texts.mat.22.42: Saying, What think ye of Christ? whose son is he? They say to him, The son of David.
texts.mat.22.43: He saith to them, How then doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying,
texts.mat.22.44: The LORD said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thy enemies thy footstool?
texts.mat.22.45: If David then calleth him Lord, how is he his son?
texts.mat.22.46: And no man was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man, from that day forth, ask him any more questions.
texts.mat.23.1: Then Jesus spoke to the multitude, and to his disciples,
texts.mat.23.2: Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses's seat.
texts.mat.23.3: All therefore, whatever they bid you observe, that observe and do: but do not ye according to their works: for they say, and do not.
texts.mat.23.4: For they bind heavy burdens, and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.
texts.mat.23.5: But all their works they do to be seen by men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,
texts.mat.23.6: And love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues,
texts.mat.23.7: And greetings in the markets, and to be called by men, Rabbi, Rabbi.
texts.mat.23.8: But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Christ; and all ye are brethren.
texts.mat.23.9: And call no man your father upon the earth: for one is your Father who is in heaven.
texts.mat.23.10: Neither be ye called masters: for one is your master, even Christ.
texts.mat.23.11: But he that is greatest among you, shall be your servant.
texts.mat.23.12: And whoever shall exalt himself, shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself, shall be exalted.
texts.mat.23.13: But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees! hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering, to go in.
texts.mat.23.14: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretense make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.
texts.mat.23.15: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him two-fold more the child of hell than yourselves.
texts.mat.23.16: Woe to you, ye blind guides, who say, Whoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor.
texts.mat.23.17: Ye fools, and blind: for which is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold?
texts.mat.23.18: And whoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever sweareth by the gift that is upon it, he is guilty.
texts.mat.23.19: Ye fools, and blind: for which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift?
texts.mat.23.20: Whoever therefore shall swear by the altar, sweareth by it, and by all things upon it.
texts.mat.23.21: And whoever shall swear by the temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth in it.
texts.mat.23.22: And he that shall swear by heaven, sweareth by the throne of God, and by him that sitteth upon it.
texts.mat.23.23: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint, and anise, and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ye ought to have done, and not to leave the others undone.
texts.mat.23.24: Ye blind guides, who strain out a gnat, and swallow a camel.
texts.mat.23.25: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.
texts.mat.23.26: Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also.
texts.mat.23.27: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like whitened sepulchers, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness.
texts.mat.23.28: Thus ye also outwardly appear righteous to men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
texts.mat.23.29: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchers of the righteous,
texts.mat.23.30: And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.
texts.mat.23.31: Wherefore ye are witnesses to yourselves, that ye are the children of them who killed the prophets.
texts.mat.23.32: Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.
texts.mat.23.33: Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?
texts.mat.23.34: Wherefore behold, I send to you prophets, and wise men, and scribes; and some of them ye will kill and crucify, and some of them ye will scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:
texts.mat.23.35: That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel, to the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.
texts.mat.23.36: Verily I say to you, all these things shall come upon this generation.
texts.mat.23.37: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them who are sent to thee, how often would I have gathered thy children, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
texts.mat.23.38: Behold, your house is left to you desolate.
texts.mat.23.39: For I say to you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
texts.mat.24.1: And Jesus went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.
texts.mat.24.2: And Jesus said to them, See ye not all these things? verily I say to you, There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.
texts.mat.24.3: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying, Tell us, when will these things be? and what will be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?
texts.mat.24.4: And Jesus answered and said to them, Take heed that no man deceive you.
texts.mat.24.5: For many will come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and will deceive many.
texts.mat.24.6: And ye will hear of wars, and rumors of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.
texts.mat.24.7: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there will be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes in divers places.
texts.mat.24.8: All these are the beginning of sorrows.
texts.mat.24.9: Then will they deliver you up to be afflicted, and will kill you: and ye will be hated by all nations for my name's sake.
texts.mat.24.10: And then will many be offended, and will betray one another, and will hate one another.
texts.mat.24.11: And many false prophets will rise, and will deceive many.
texts.mat.24.12: And because iniquity will abound, the love of many will become cold.
texts.mat.24.13: But he that shall endure to the end, the same shall be saved.
texts.mat.24.14: And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world, for a testimony to all nations; and then shall the end come.
texts.mat.24.15: When therefore ye shall see the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoever readeth, let him understand,)
texts.mat.24.16: Then let them who are in Judea flee to the mountains:
texts.mat.24.17: Let him who is on the house-top not come down to take any thing out of his house:
texts.mat.24.18: Neither let him who is in the field return back to take his clothes.
texts.mat.24.19: And woe to them that are with child, and to them that nurse infants in those days!
texts.mat.24.20: But pray ye that your flight may not be in the winter, neither on the sabbath:
texts.mat.24.21: For then shall be great tribulation, such as hath not been since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be.
texts.mat.24.22: And except those days should be shortened, there would no flesh be saved: but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened.
texts.mat.24.23: Then if any man shall say to you, Lo, here is Christ, or there; believe it not.
texts.mat.24.24: For false Christs will arise, and false prophets, and will show great signs and wonders; so that, if it were possible, they would deceive the very elect.
texts.mat.24.25: Behold, I have told you before.
texts.mat.24.26: Wherefore, if they shall say to you, Behold, he is in the desert; go not forth: behold, he is in the secret chambers; believe it not.
texts.mat.24.27: For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even to the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.
texts.mat.24.28: For wherever the carcass is, there will the eagles be collected.
texts.mat.24.29: Immediately after the tribulation of those days, shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
texts.mat.24.30: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
texts.mat.24.31: And he will send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
texts.mat.24.32: Now learn a parable of the fig-tree; When its branch is yet tender and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh:
texts.mat.24.33: So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.
texts.mat.24.34: Verily I say to you, This generation shall not pass, till all these things shall be fulfilled.
texts.mat.24.35: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.
texts.mat.24.36: But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
texts.mat.24.37: But as the days of Noah were, so will also the coming of the Son of man be.
texts.mat.24.38: For as in the days that were before the flood, they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark,
texts.mat.24.39: And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away: so also will be the coming of the Son of man.
texts.mat.24.40: Then will two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
texts.mat.24.41: Two women will be grinding at the mill; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
texts.mat.24.42: Watch therefore; for ye know not what hour your Lord cometh.
texts.mat.24.43: But know this, that if the master of the house knew in what watch the thief would come, he would watch, and would not suffer his house to be broken up.
texts.mat.24.44: Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not, the Son of man cometh.
texts.mat.24.45: Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his Lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them food in due season?
texts.mat.24.46: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord, when he cometh, shall find so doing.
texts.mat.24.47: Verily I say to you, that he will make him ruler over all his goods.
texts.mat.24.48: But if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My Lord delayeth his coming;
texts.mat.24.49: And shall begin to beat his fellow-servants, and to eat and drink with the drunken;
texts.mat.24.50: The Lord of that servant will come in a day when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of,
texts.mat.24.51: And will cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.25.1: Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened to ten virgins, who took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom.
texts.mat.25.2: And five of them were wise, and five were foolish.
texts.mat.25.3: They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them:
texts.mat.25.4: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.
texts.mat.25.5: While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept.
texts.mat.25.6: And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him.
texts.mat.25.7: Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.
texts.mat.25.8: And the foolish said to the wise, Give us of your oil: for our lamps are gone out.
texts.mat.25.9: But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves.
texts.mat.25.10: And while they were going to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready, went in with him to the marriage, and the door was shut.
texts.mat.25.11: Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us.
texts.mat.25.12: But he answered and said, Verily I say to you, I know you not.
texts.mat.25.13: Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour in which the Son of man cometh.
texts.mat.25.14: For the kingdom of heaven is as a man traveling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered to them his goods.
texts.mat.25.15: And to one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and forthwith took his journey.
texts.mat.25.16: Then he that had received the five talents, went and traded with the same, and gained other five talents.
texts.mat.25.17: And likewise he that had received two, he also gained other two.
texts.mat.25.18: But he that had received one, went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord's money.
texts.mat.25.19: After a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and reckoneth with them.
texts.mat.25.20: And he that had received five talents, came and brought other five talents, saying, Lord, thou deliveredst to me five talents: behold, I have gained besides them five talents more.
texts.mat.25.21: His lord said to him, Well done thou good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
texts.mat.25.22: He also that had received two talents came, and said, Lord, thou deliveredst to me two talents: behold, I have gained two other talents besides them.
texts.mat.25.23: His lord said to him, Well done, good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
texts.mat.25.24: Then he who had received the one talent came, and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art a hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strewed:
texts.mat.25.25: And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth: lo, there thou hast what is thine.
texts.mat.25.26: His lord answered and said to him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I have not sown, and gather where I have not strewed:
texts.mat.25.27: Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received my own with interest.
texts.mat.25.28: Take therefore the talent from him, and give it to him who hath ten talents.
texts.mat.25.29: For to every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath.
texts.mat.25.30: And cast ye the unprofitable servant into utter darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.25.31: When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then will he sit upon the throne of his glory:
texts.mat.25.32: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:
texts.mat.25.33: And he will set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.
texts.mat.25.34: Then will the King say to them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:
texts.mat.25.35: For I was hungry, and ye gave me food: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:
texts.mat.25.36: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came to me.
texts.mat.25.37: Then will the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee hungry, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink?
texts.mat.25.38: When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee?
texts.mat.25.39: Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came to thee?
texts.mat.25.40: And the king will answer and say to them, Verily I say to you, Inasmuch as ye have done it to one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it to me.
texts.mat.25.41: Then will he say also to them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:
texts.mat.25.42: For I was hungry, and ye gave me no food: I was thirsty, and ye gave me no drink:
texts.mat.25.43: I was a stranger, and ye took me not in: naked, and ye clothed me not: sick, and in prison, and ye visited me not.
texts.mat.25.44: Then will they also answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister to thee?
texts.mat.25.45: Then will he answer them, saying, Verily I say to you, Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me.
texts.mat.25.46: And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.
texts.mat.26.1: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these sayings, he said to his disciples,
texts.mat.26.2: Ye know that after two days is the passover, and the Son of man is betrayed to be crucified.
texts.mat.26.3: Then assembled the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders of the people, in the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,
texts.mat.26.4: And consulted that they might take Jesus by subtilty, and kill him.
texts.mat.26.5: But they said, Not on the feast-day, lest there be an uproar among the people.
texts.mat.26.6: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
texts.mat.26.7: There came to him a woman having an alabaster-box of very precious ointment, and poured it on his head as he sat at table.
texts.mat.26.8: But when his disciples saw it, they had indignation, saying, To what purpose is this waste?
texts.mat.26.9: For this ointment might have been sold for much, and given to the poor.
texts.mat.26.10: When Jesus understood it, he said to them, Why trouble ye the woman? for she hath wrought a good work upon me.
texts.mat.26.11: For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always.
texts.mat.26.12: For in that she hath poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial.
texts.mat.26.13: Verily I say to you, Wherever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, there shall also this, which this woman hath done, be told for a memorial of her.
texts.mat.26.14: Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests,
texts.mat.26.15: And said, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him to you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.
texts.mat.26.16: And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him.
texts.mat.26.17: Now the first day of the feast of unleavened bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying to him, Where wilt thou that we prepare for thee to eat the passover?
texts.mat.26.18: And he said, Go into the city to such a man, and say to him, The Master saith, My time is at hand; I will keep the passover at thy house with my disciples.
texts.mat.26.19: And the disciples did as Jesus had appointed them; and they made ready the passover.
texts.mat.26.20: Now when the evening was come, he sat down with the twelve.
texts.mat.26.21: And as they were eating, he said, Verily I say to you, that one of you will betray me.
texts.mat.26.22: And they were exceeding sorrowful, and began every one of them to say to him, Lord, is it I?
texts.mat.26.23: And he answered and said, He that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, the same will betray me.
texts.mat.26.24: The Son of man goeth, as it is written concerning him: but woe to that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man, if he had not been born.
texts.mat.26.25: Then Judas, who betrayed him, answered and said, Master, is it I? He said to him, Thou hast said.
texts.mat.26.26: And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body.
texts.mat.26.27: And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it;
texts.mat.26.28: For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sin.
texts.mat.26.29: But I say to you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom.
texts.mat.26.30: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the mount of Olives.
texts.mat.26.31: Then saith Jesus to them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad.
texts.mat.26.32: But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.
texts.mat.26.33: Peter answered and said to him, Though all men shall be offended because of thee, yet will I never be offended.
texts.mat.26.34: Jesus said to him, Verily I say to thee, that this night, before the cock shall crow, thou wilt deny me thrice.
texts.mat.26.35: Peter said to him, Though I should die with thee, yet will I not deny thee. Likewise also said all the disciples.
texts.mat.26.36: Then cometh Jesus with them to a place called Gethsemane, and saith to the disciples, Sit ye here, while I go yonder and pray.
texts.mat.26.37: And he took with him Peter, and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and very heavy.
texts.mat.26.38: Then saith he to them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even to death: tarry ye here, and watch with me.
texts.mat.26.39: And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless, not as I will, but as thou wilt.
texts.mat.26.40: And he cometh to the disciples, and findeth them asleep, and saith to Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour?
texts.mat.26.41: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
texts.mat.26.42: He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.
texts.mat.26.43: And he came and found them asleep again: for their eyes were heavy.
texts.mat.26.44: And he left them, and went away again, and prayed the third time, saying the same words.
texts.mat.26.45: Then he cometh to his disciples, and saith to them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
texts.mat.26.46: Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that doth betray me.
texts.mat.26.47: And while he was yet speaking, lo, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and staffs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
texts.mat.26.48: Now he that betrayed him, gave them a sign, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he; hold him fast.
texts.mat.26.49: And forthwith he came to Jesus, and said, Hail Master; and kissed him.
texts.mat.26.50: And Jesus said to him, Friend, Why art thou come? Then they came, and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.
texts.mat.26.51: And behold, one of them, who were with Jesus, stretched out his hand, and drew his sword, and struck a servant of the high priest, and smote off his ear.
texts.mat.26.52: Then said Jesus to him, Put up again thy sword into its place: for all they that take the sword, shall perish by the sword.
texts.mat.26.53: Thinkest thou that I cannot now pray to my Father, and he will presently give me more than twelve legions of angels?
texts.mat.26.54: But how then shall the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must be?
texts.mat.26.55: In that same hour said Jesus to the multitudes, Are ye come out as against a thief with swords and staffs to take me? I sat daily with you teaching in the temple, and ye laid no hold on me.
texts.mat.26.56: But all this was done, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples forsook him, and fled.
texts.mat.26.57: And they that had laid hold on Jesus, led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were assembled.
texts.mat.26.58: But Peter followed him at a distance, to the high priest's palace, and went in, and sat with the servants to see the end.
texts.mat.26.59: Now the chief priests and elders, and all the council, sought false testimony against Jesus, to put him to death;
texts.mat.26.60: But found none: and, though many false witnesses came, yet found they none. At the last came two false witnesses,
texts.mat.26.61: And said, This man said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.
texts.mat.26.62: And the high priest arose, and said to him, Answerest thou nothing, what is it which these testify against thee?
texts.mat.26.63: But Jesus held his peace. And the high priest answered and said to him, I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tell us whether thou art the Christ the Son of God.
texts.mat.26.64: Jesus saith to him, Thou hast said: nevertheless I say to you, Hereafter shall ye see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.
texts.mat.26.65: Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He hath spoken blasphemy; what further need have we of witnesses? behold, now ye have heard his blasphemy.
texts.mat.26.66: What think ye? They answered and said, He is guilty of death.
texts.mat.26.67: Then they spit in his face, and buffetted him; and others smote him with the palms of their hands,
texts.mat.26.68: Saying, Prophesy to us, thou Christ, Who is he that smote thee?
texts.mat.26.69: Now Peter sat without in the palace: and a damsel came to him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galilee.
texts.mat.26.70: But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what thou sayest.
texts.mat.26.71: And when he had gone out into the porch, another maid saw him, and said to them that were there, This man was also with Jesus of Nazareth.
texts.mat.26.72: And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.
texts.mat.26.73: And after a while came to him they that stood by, and said to Peter, Surely thou also art one of them; for thy speech betrayeth thee.
texts.mat.26.74: Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crowed.
texts.mat.26.75: And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, who said to him, Before the cock shall crow, thou wilt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.
texts.mat.27.1: When the morning was come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death.
texts.mat.27.2: And when they had bound him, they led him away, and delivered him to Pontius Pilate the governor.
texts.mat.27.3: Then Judas, who had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
texts.mat.27.4: Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that.
texts.mat.27.5: And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.
texts.mat.27.6: And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.
texts.mat.27.7: And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in.
texts.mat.27.8: Wherefore that field has been called, The field of blood, to this day.
texts.mat.27.9: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued, whom they of the children of Israel did value;
texts.mat.27.10: And gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord appointed me.
texts.mat.27.11: And Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And Jesus said to him, Thou sayest.
texts.mat.27.12: And when he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.
texts.mat.27.13: Then saith Pilate to him, Hearest thou not how many things they testify against thee?
texts.mat.27.14: And he answered him to not a word; so that the governor marveled greatly.
texts.mat.27.15: Now at that feast, the governor was wont to release to the people a prisoner, whom they would.
texts.mat.27.16: And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.
texts.mat.27.17: Therefore when they were assembled, Pilate said to them, Whom will ye that I release to you? Barabbas, or Jesus, who is called Christ?
texts.mat.27.18: (For he knew that for envy they had delivered him.)
texts.mat.27.19: When he was sitting on the judgment-seat, his wife sent to him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream, because of him.
texts.mat.27.20: But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude that they should ask Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.
texts.mat.27.21: The governor answered and said to them, Which of the two will ye that I release to you? They said, Barabbas.
texts.mat.27.22: Pilate saith to them, What shall I do then with Jesus, who is called Christ? They all say to him, Let him be crucified.
texts.mat.27.23: And the governor said, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out the more, saying, Let him be crucified.
texts.mat.27.24: When Pilate saw that he could not prevail at all, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.
texts.mat.27.25: Then answered all the people, and said, His blood be on us, and on our children.
texts.mat.27.26: Then he released Barabbas to them: and when he had scourged Jesus, he delivered him to be crucified.
texts.mat.27.27: Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the common hall, and gathered to him the whole band of soldiers.
texts.mat.27.28: And they stripped him, and put on him a scarlet robe.
texts.mat.27.29: And when they had platted a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews?
texts.mat.27.30: And they spit upon him, and took the reed, and struck him on the head.
texts.mat.27.31: And after that they had mocked him, they took the robe off from him, and put his own raiment on him, and led him away to crucify him.
texts.mat.27.32: And as they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name: him they constrained to bear his cross.
texts.mat.27.33: And when they had come to a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,
texts.mat.27.34: They gave him vinegar to drink, mingled with gall: and when he had tasted of it, he would not drink.
texts.mat.27.35: And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture they cast lots.
texts.mat.27.36: And sitting down, they watched him there:
texts.mat.27.37: And set up over his head his accusation written, THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
texts.mat.27.38: Then were there two thieves crucified with him: one on the right hand, and another on the left.
texts.mat.27.39: And they that passed by, reviled him, wagging their heads,
texts.mat.27.40: And saying, Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself. If thou art the Son of God, come down from the cross.
texts.mat.27.41: Likewise also the chief priests mocking him, with the scribes and elders, said,
texts.mat.27.42: He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he is King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him.
texts.mat.27.43: He trusted in God; let him deliver him now if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of God.
texts.mat.27.44: The thieves also who were crucified with him, cast the same in his teeth.
texts.mat.27.45: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land to the ninth hour.
texts.mat.27.46: And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
texts.mat.27.47: Some of them that stood there, when they heard that, said, This man calleth for Elijah.
texts.mat.27.48: And immediately one of them ran, and took a spunge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.
texts.mat.27.49: The rest said, Forbear, let us see whether Elijah will come to save him.
texts.mat.27.50: Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, expired.
texts.mat.27.51: And behold, the vail of the temple was rent in two, from the top to the bottom: and the earth shook, and the rocks rent;
texts.mat.27.52: And the graves were opened, and many bodies of saints who slept, arose,
texts.mat.27.53: And came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared to many.
texts.mat.27.54: Now when the centurion, and they that were with him, watching Jesus, saw the earthquake, and those things that were done, they feared greatly, saying, Truly this was the Son of God.
texts.mat.27.55: And many women were there (beholding at a distance) who followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering to him:
texts.mat.27.56: Among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee's children.
texts.mat.27.57: When the evening was come, there came a rich man of Arimathea, named Joseph, who also himself was a disciple of Jesus.
texts.mat.27.58: He went to Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded the body to be delivered.
texts.mat.27.59: And when Joseph had taken the body, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
texts.mat.27.60: And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock; and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulcher, and departed.
texts.mat.27.61: And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulcher.
texts.mat.27.62: Now the next day that followed the day of the preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees came together to Pilate,
texts.mat.27.63: Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again.
texts.mat.27.64: Command therefore that the sepulcher be made secure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away, and say to the people, He is risen from the dead: so the last error will be worse than the first.
texts.mat.27.65: Pilate said to them, Ye have a watch: go, make it as secure as ye can.
texts.mat.27.66: So they went, and having sealed the stone, made the sepulcher secure with a watch.
texts.mat.28.1: In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn towards the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary to see the sepulcher.
texts.mat.28.2: And behold, there was a great earthquake: for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it.
texts.mat.28.3: His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow.
texts.mat.28.4: And for fear of him the keepers trembled and became as dead men.
texts.mat.28.5: And the angel answered and said to the women, Fear ye not: for I know that ye seek Jesus, who was crucified.
texts.mat.28.6: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
texts.mat.28.7: And go quickly, and tell his disciples, that he is risen from the dead, and behold, he goeth before you into Galilee; there shall ye see him: lo, I have told you.
texts.mat.28.8: And they departed quickly from the sepulcher, with fear and great joy; and ran to bring word to his disciples.
texts.mat.28.9: And as they were going to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, All hail. And they came, and held him by the feet, and worshiped him.
texts.mat.28.10: Then said Jesus to them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren, that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.
texts.mat.28.11: Now when they were going, behold, some of the watch came into the city, and showed to the chief priests all the things that had been done.
texts.mat.28.12: And when they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave a large sum of money to the soldiers,
texts.mat.28.13: Saying, Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.
texts.mat.28.14: And if this shall come to the governor's ears, we will persuade him, and secure you.
texts.mat.28.15: So they took the money, and did as they were instructed: and this saying is commonly reported among the Jews until this day.
texts.mat.28.16: Then the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, to a mountain where Jesus had appointed them.
texts.mat.28.17: And when they saw him, they worshiped him: but some doubted.
texts.mat.28.18: And Jesus came, and spoke to them, saying, All power is given to me in heaven and upon earth.
texts.mat.28.19: Go ye therefore and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
texts.mat.28.20: Teaching them to observe all things whatever I have commanded you: and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the world. Amen.

texts.mat.1.1: Book of the generation of Jesus Christ, Son of David, Son of Abraham.
texts.mat.1.2: Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob begat Juda and his brethren;
texts.mat.1.3: and Juda begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom, and Esrom begat Aram,
texts.mat.1.4: and Aram begat Aminadab, and Aminadab begat Naasson, and Naasson begat Salmon,
texts.mat.1.5: and Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse,
texts.mat.1.6: and Jesse begat David the king. And David begat Solomon, of her [that had been the wife] of Urias;
texts.mat.1.7: and Solomon begat Roboam, and Roboam begat Abia, and Abia begat Asa,
texts.mat.1.8: and Asa begat Josaphat, and Josaphat begat Joram, and Joram begat Ozias,
texts.mat.1.9: and Ozias begat Joatham, and Joatham begat Achaz, and Achaz begat Ezekias,
texts.mat.1.10: and Ezekias begat Manasses, and Manasses begat Amon, and Amon begat Josias,
texts.mat.1.11: and Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren, at the time of the carrying away of Babylon.
texts.mat.1.12: And after the carrying away of Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel, and Salathiel begat Zorobabel,
texts.mat.1.13: and Zorobabel begat Abiud, and Abiud begat Eliakim, and Eliakim begat Azor,
texts.mat.1.14: and Azor begat Sadoc, and Sadoc begat Achim, and Achim begat Eliud,
texts.mat.1.15: and Eliud begat Eliazar, and Eliazar begat Matthan, and Matthan begat Jacob,
texts.mat.1.16: and Jacob begat Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
texts.mat.1.17: All the generations, therefore, from Abraham to David [were] fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away of Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the carrying away of Babylon unto the Christ, fourteen generations.
texts.mat.1.18: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was thus: His mother, Mary, that is, having been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be with child of [the] Holy Spirit.
texts.mat.1.19: But Joseph, her husband, being [a] righteous [man], and unwilling to expose her publicly, purposed to have put her away secretly;
texts.mat.1.20: but while he pondered on these things, behold, an angel of [the] Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, Joseph, son of David, fear not to take to [thee] Mary, thy wife, for that which is begotten in her is of [the] Holy Spirit.
texts.mat.1.21: And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name Jesus, for *he* shall save his people from their sins.
texts.mat.1.22: Now all this came to pass that that might be fulfilled which was spoken by [the] Lord, through the prophet, saying,
texts.mat.1.23: Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which is, being interpreted, 'God with us.'
texts.mat.1.24: But Joseph, having awoke up from his sleep, did as the angel of [the] Lord had enjoined him, and took to [him] his wife,
texts.mat.1.25: and knew her not until she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name Jesus.
texts.mat.2.1: Now Jesus having been born in Bethlehem of Judaea, in the days of Herod the king, behold magi from the east arrived at Jerusalem, saying,
texts.mat.2.2: Where is the king of the Jews that has been born? for we have seen his star in the east, and have come to do him homage.
texts.mat.2.3: But Herod the king having heard [of it], was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him;
texts.mat.2.4: and, assembling all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired of them where the Christ should be born.
texts.mat.2.5: And they said to him, In Bethlehem of Judaea; for thus it is written through the prophet:
texts.mat.2.6: And *thou* Bethlehem, land of Juda, art in no wise the least among the governors of Juda; for out of thee shall go forth a leader who shall shepherd my people Israel.
texts.mat.2.7: Then Herod, having secretly called the magi, inquired of them accurately the time of the star that was appearing;
texts.mat.2.8: and having sent them to Bethlehem, said, Go, search out accurately concerning the child, and when ye shall have found [him] bring me back word, so that *I* also may come and do him homage.
texts.mat.2.9: And they having heard the king went their way; and lo, the star, which they had seen in the east, went before them until it came and stood over the place where the little child was.
texts.mat.2.10: And when they saw the star they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.
texts.mat.2.11: And having come into the house they saw the little child with Mary his mother, and falling down did him homage. And having opened their treasures, they offered to him gifts, gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
texts.mat.2.12: And being divinely instructed in a dream not to return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way.
texts.mat.2.13: Now, they having departed, behold, an angel of [the] Lord appears in a dream to Joseph, saying, Arise, take to [thee] the little child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be there until I shall tell thee; for Herod will seek the little child to destroy it.
texts.mat.2.14: And, having arisen, he took to [him] the little child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt.
texts.mat.2.15: And he was there until the death of Herod, that that might be fulfilled which was spoken by [the] Lord through the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son.
