texts.mat.19.21: Jesus said to him, If thou wouldest be perfect, go, sell what thou hast and give to [the] poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.
texts.mat.19.22: But the young man, having heard the word, went away grieved, for he had large possessions.
texts.mat.19.23: And Jesus said to his disciples, Verily I say unto you, A rich man shall with difficulty enter into the kingdom of the heavens;
texts.mat.19.24: and again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to enter a needle's eye than a rich man into the kingdom of God.
texts.mat.19.25: And when the disciples heard [it] they were exceedingly astonished, saying, Who then can be saved?
texts.mat.19.26: But Jesus, looking on [them], said to them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
texts.mat.19.27: Then Peter answering said to him, Behold, *we* have left all things and have followed thee; what then shall happen to us?
texts.mat.19.28: And Jesus said to them, Verily I say unto you, That *ye* who have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit down upon his throne of glory, *ye* also shall sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
texts.mat.19.29: And every one who has left houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name's sake, shall receive a hundredfold, and shall inherit life eternal.
texts.mat.19.30: But many first shall be last, and last first.
texts.mat.20.1: For the kingdom of the heavens is like a householder who went out with the early morn to hire workmen for his vineyard.
texts.mat.20.2: And having agreed with the workmen for a denarius the day, he sent them into his vineyard.
texts.mat.20.3: And having gone out about [the] third hour, he saw others standing in the market-place idle;
texts.mat.20.4: and to them he said, Go also ye into the vineyard, and whatsoever may be just I will give you. And they went their way.
texts.mat.20.5: Again, having gone out about the sixth and ninth hour, he did likewise.
texts.mat.20.6: But about the eleventh [hour], having gone out, he found others standing, and says to them, Why stand ye here all the day idle?
texts.mat.20.7: They say to him, Because no man has hired us. He says to them, Go also ye into the vineyard [and whatsoever may be just ye shall receive].
texts.mat.20.8: But when the evening was come, the lord of the vineyard says to his steward, Call the workmen and pay [them] their wages, beginning from the last even to the first.
texts.mat.20.9: And when they [who came to work] about the eleventh hour came, they received each a denarius.
texts.mat.20.10: And when the first came, they supposed that they would receive more, and they received also themselves each a denarius.
texts.mat.20.11: And on receiving it they murmured against the master of the house,
texts.mat.20.12: saying, These last have worked one hour, and thou hast made them equal to us, who have borne the burden of the day and the heat.
texts.mat.20.13: But he answering said to one of them, [My] friend, I do not wrong thee. Didst thou not agree with me for a denarius?
texts.mat.20.14: Take what is thine and go. But it is my will to give to this last even as to thee:
texts.mat.20.15: is it not lawful for me to do what I will in my own affairs? Is thine eye evil because *I* am good?
texts.mat.20.16: Thus shall the last be first, and the first last; for many are called ones, but few chosen ones.
texts.mat.20.17: And Jesus, going up to Jerusalem, took the twelve disciples with [him] apart in the way, and said to them,
texts.mat.20.18: Behold we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of man will be delivered up to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death;
texts.mat.20.19: and they will deliver him up to the nations to mock and to scourge and to crucify, and the third day he shall rise again.
texts.mat.20.20: Then came to him the mother of the sons of Zebedee, with her sons, doing homage, and asking something of him.
texts.mat.20.21: And he said to her, What wilt thou? She says to him, Speak [the word] that these my two sons may sit, one on thy right hand and one on thy left in thy kingdom.
texts.mat.20.22: And Jesus answering said, Ye know not what ye ask. Can ye drink the cup which *I* am about to drink? They say to him, We are able.
texts.mat.20.23: [And] he says to them, Ye shall drink indeed my cup, but to sit on my right hand and on [my] left, is not mine to give, but to those for whom it is prepared of my Father.
texts.mat.20.24: And the ten, having heard [of it], were indignant about the two brothers.
texts.mat.20.25: But Jesus having called them to [him], said, Ye know that the rulers of the nations exercise lordship over them, and the great exercise authority over them.
texts.mat.20.26: It shall not be thus amongst you, but whosoever will be great among you, shall be your servant;
texts.mat.20.27: and whosoever will be first among you, let him be your bondman;
texts.mat.20.28: as indeed the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.
texts.mat.20.29: And as they went out from Jericho a great crowd followed him.
texts.mat.20.30: And lo, two blind men, sitting by the wayside, having heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out saying, Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David.
texts.mat.20.31: But the crowd rebuked them, that they might be silent. But they cried out the more, saying, Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David.
texts.mat.20.32: And Jesus, having stopped, called them and said, What will ye that I shall do to you?
texts.mat.20.33: They say to him, Lord, that our eyes may be opened.
texts.mat.20.34: And Jesus, moved with compassion, touched their eyes; and immediately their eyes had sight restored to them, and they followed him.
texts.mat.21.1: And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, at the mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
texts.mat.21.2: saying to them, Go into the village over against you, and immediately ye will find an ass tied, and a colt with it; loose [them] and lead [them] to me.
texts.mat.21.3: And if any one say anything to you, ye shall say, The Lord has need of them, and straightway he will send them.
texts.mat.21.4: But all this came to pass, that that might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying,
texts.mat.21.5: Say to the daughter of Zion, Behold thy King cometh to thee, meek, and mounted upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.
texts.mat.21.6: But the disciples, having gone and done as Jesus had ordered them,
texts.mat.21.7: brought the ass and the colt and put their garments upon them, and he sat on them.
texts.mat.21.8: But a very great crowd strewed their own garments on the way, and others kept cutting down branches from the trees and strewing them on the way.
texts.mat.21.9: And the crowds who went before him and who followed cried, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David; blessed [be] he who comes in the name of [the] Lord; hosanna in the highest.
texts.mat.21.10: And as he entered into Jerusalem, the whole city was moved, saying, Who is this?
texts.mat.21.11: And the crowds said, This is Jesus the prophet who is from Nazareth of Galilee.
texts.mat.21.12: And Jesus entered into the temple [of God], and cast out all that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those that sold the doves.
texts.mat.21.13: And he says to them, It is written, My house shall be called a house of prayer, but *ye* have made it a den of robbers.
texts.mat.21.14: And blind and lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
texts.mat.21.15: And when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonders which he wrought, and the children crying in the temple and saying, Hosanna to the Son of David, they were indignant,
texts.mat.21.16: and said to him, Hearest thou what these say? And Jesus says to them, Yea; have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise?
texts.mat.21.17: And leaving them he went forth out of the city to Bethany, and there he passed the night.
texts.mat.21.18: But early in the morning, as he came back into the city, he hungered.
texts.mat.21.19: And seeing one fig-tree in the way, he came to it and found on it nothing but leaves only. And he says to it, Let there be never more fruit of thee for ever. And the fig-tree was immediately dried up.
texts.mat.21.20: And when the disciples saw [it], they wondered, saying, How immediately is the fig-tree dried up!
texts.mat.21.21: And Jesus answering said to them, Verily I say unto you, If ye have faith, and do not doubt, not only shall ye do what [is done] to the fig-tree, but even if ye should say to this mountain, Be thou taken away and be thou cast into the sea, it shall come to pass.
texts.mat.21.22: And all things whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.
texts.mat.21.23: And when he came into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him [as he was] teaching, saying, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority?
texts.mat.21.24: And Jesus answering said to them, *I* also will ask you one thing, which if ye tell me, *I* also will tell you by what authority I do these things:
texts.mat.21.25: The baptism of John, whence was it? of heaven or of men? And they reasoned among themselves, saying, If we should say, Of heaven, he will say to us, Why then have ye not believed him?
texts.mat.21.26: but if we should say, Of men, we fear the crowd, for all hold John for a prophet.
texts.mat.21.27: And answering Jesus they said, We do not know. *He* also said to them, Neither do *I* tell you by what authority I do these things.
texts.mat.21.28: But what think ye? A man had two children, and coming to the first he said, Child, go to-day, work in [my] vineyard.
texts.mat.21.29: And he answering said, I will not; but afterwards repenting himself he went.
texts.mat.21.30: And coming to the second he said likewise; and he answering said, *I* [go], sir, and went not.
texts.mat.21.31: Which of the two did the will of the father? They say [to him], The first. Jesus says to them, Verily I say unto you that the tax-gatherers and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.
texts.mat.21.32: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not; but the tax-gatherers and the harlots believed him; but *ye* when ye saw [it] repented not yourselves afterwards to believe him.
texts.mat.21.33: Hear another parable: There was a householder who planted a vineyard, and made a fence round it, and dug a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and left the country.
texts.mat.21.34: But when the time of fruit drew near, he sent his bondmen to the husbandmen to receive his fruits.
texts.mat.21.35: And the husbandmen took his bondmen, and beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
texts.mat.21.36: Again he sent other bondmen more than the first, and they did to them in like manner.
texts.mat.21.37: And at last he sent to them his son, saying, They will have respect for my son.
texts.mat.21.38: But the husbandmen, seeing the son, said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him and possess his inheritance.
texts.mat.21.39: And they took him, and cast him forth out of the vineyard, and killed him.
texts.mat.21.40: When therefore the lord of the vineyard comes, what shall he do to those husbandmen?
texts.mat.21.41: They say to him, He will miserably destroy those evil [men], and let out the vineyard to other husbandmen, who shall render him the fruits in their seasons.
texts.mat.21.42: Jesus says to them, Have ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which they that builded rejected, this has become the corner-stone: this is of [the] Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes?
texts.mat.21.43: Therefore I say to you, that the kingdom of God shall be taken from you and shall be given to a nation producing the fruits of it.
texts.mat.21.44: And he that falls on this stone shall be broken, but on whomsoever it shall fall, it shall grind him to powder.
texts.mat.21.45: And the chief priests and the Pharisees, having heard his parables, knew that he spoke about them.
texts.mat.21.46: And seeking to lay hold of him, they were afraid of the crowds, because they held him for a prophet.
texts.mat.22.1: And Jesus answering spoke to them again in parables, saying,
texts.mat.22.2: The kingdom of the heavens has become like a king who made a wedding feast for his son,
texts.mat.22.3: and sent his bondmen to call the persons invited to the wedding feast, and they would not come.
texts.mat.22.4: Again he sent other bondmen, saying, Say to the persons invited, Behold, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and my fatted beasts are killed, and all things ready; come to the wedding feast.
texts.mat.22.5: But they made light of it, and went, one to his own land, and another to his commerce.
texts.mat.22.6: And the rest, laying hold of his bondmen, ill-treated and slew [them].
texts.mat.22.7: And [when] the king [heard of it he] was wroth, and having sent his forces, destroyed those murderers and burned their city.
texts.mat.22.8: Then he says to his bondmen, The wedding feast is ready, but those invited were not worthy;
texts.mat.22.9: go therefore into the thoroughfares of the highways, and as many as ye shall find invite to the wedding feast.
texts.mat.22.10: And those bondmen went out into the highways, and brought together all as many as they found, both evil and good; and the wedding feast was furnished with guests.
texts.mat.22.11: And the king, having gone in to see the guests, beheld there a man not clothed with a wedding garment.
texts.mat.22.12: And he says to him, [My] friend, how camest thou in here not having on a wedding garment? But he was speechless.
texts.mat.22.13: Then said the king to the servants, Bind him feet and hands, and take him away, and cast him out into the outer darkness: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.22.14: For many are called ones, but few chosen ones.
texts.mat.22.15: Then went the Pharisees and held a council how they might ensnare him in speaking.
texts.mat.22.16: And they send out to him their disciples with the Herodians, saying, Teacher, we know that thou art true and teachest the way of God in truth, and carest not for any one, for thou regardest not men's person;
texts.mat.22.17: tell us therefore what thou thinkest: Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?
texts.mat.22.18: But Jesus, knowing their wickedness, said, Why tempt ye me, hypocrites?
texts.mat.22.19: Shew me the money of the tribute. And they presented to him a denarius.
texts.mat.22.20: And he says to them, Whose [is] this image and superscription?
texts.mat.22.21: They say to him, Caesar's. Then he says to them, Pay then what is Caesar's to Caesar, and what is God's to God.
texts.mat.22.22: And when they heard [him], they wondered, and left him, and went away.
texts.mat.22.23: On that day came to him Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection; and they demanded of him,
texts.mat.22.24: saying, Teacher, Moses said, If any one die, not having children, his brother shall marry his wife and shall raise up seed to his brother.
texts.mat.22.25: Now there were with us seven brethren; and the first having married died, and not having seed, left his wife to his brother.
texts.mat.22.26: In like manner also the second and the third, unto the seven.
texts.mat.22.27: And last of all the woman also died.
texts.mat.22.28: In the resurrection therefore of which of the seven shall she be wife, for all had her?
texts.mat.22.29: And Jesus answering said to them, Ye err, not knowing the scriptures nor the power of God.
texts.mat.22.30: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are as angels of God in heaven.
texts.mat.22.31: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read what was spoken to you by God, saying,
texts.mat.22.32: *I* am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not God of [the] dead, but of [the] living.
texts.mat.22.33: And when the crowds heard [it] they were astonished at his doctrine.
texts.mat.22.34: But the Pharisees, having heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, were gathered together.
texts.mat.22.35: And one of them, a lawyer, demanded, tempting him, and saying,
texts.mat.22.36: Teacher, which is the great commandment in the law?
texts.mat.22.37: And he said to him, Thou shalt love [the] Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy understanding.
texts.mat.22.38: This is [the] great and first commandment.
texts.mat.22.39: And [the] second is like it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
texts.mat.22.40: On these two commandments the whole law and the prophets hang.
texts.mat.22.41: And the Pharisees being gathered together, Jesus demanded of them,
texts.mat.22.42: saying, What think ye concerning the Christ? whose son is he? They say to him, David's.
texts.mat.22.43: He says to them, How then does David in Spirit call him Lord, saying,
texts.mat.22.44: The Lord said to my Lord, Sit on my right hand until I put thine enemies under thy feet?
texts.mat.22.45: If therefore David call him Lord, how is he his son?
texts.mat.22.46: And no one was able to answer him a word, nor did any one dare from that day to question him any more.
texts.mat.23.1: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples,
texts.mat.23.2: saying, The scribes and the Pharisees have set themselves down in Moses' seat:
texts.mat.23.3: all things therefore, whatever they may tell you, do and keep. But do not after their works, for they say and do not,
texts.mat.23.4: but bind burdens heavy and hard to bear, and lay them on the shoulders of men, but will not move them with their finger.
texts.mat.23.5: And all their works they do to be seen of men: for they make broad their phylacteries and enlarge the borders [of their garments],
texts.mat.23.6: and love the chief place in feasts and the first seats in the synagogues,
texts.mat.23.7: and salutations in the market-places, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi.
texts.mat.23.8: But *ye*, be not ye called Rabbi; for one is your instructor, and all *ye* are brethren.
texts.mat.23.9: And call not [any one] your father upon the earth; for one is your Father, he who is in the heavens.
texts.mat.23.10: Neither be called instructors, for one is your instructor, the Christ.
texts.mat.23.11: But the greatest of you shall be your servant.
texts.mat.23.12: And whoever shall exalt himself shall be humbled, and whoever shall humble himself shall be exalted.
texts.mat.23.13: But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for ye shut up the kingdom of the heavens before men; for *ye* do not enter, nor do ye suffer those that are entering to go in.
texts.mat.23.15: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for ye compass the sea and the dry [land] to make one proselyte, and when he is become [such], ye make him twofold more [the] son of hell than yourselves.
texts.mat.23.16: Woe to you, blind guides, who say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor.
texts.mat.23.17: Fools and blind, for which is greater, the gold, or the temple which sanctifies the gold?
texts.mat.23.18: And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gift that is upon it is a debtor.
texts.mat.23.19: [Fools and] blind ones, for which is greater, the gift, or the altar which sanctifies the gift?
texts.mat.23.20: He therefore that swears by the altar swears by it and by all things that are upon it.
texts.mat.23.21: And he that swears by the temple swears by it and by him that dwells in it.
texts.mat.23.22: And he that swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by him that sits upon it.
texts.mat.23.23: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for ye pay tithes of mint and anise and cummin, and ye have left aside the weightier matters of the law, judgment and mercy and faith: these ye ought to have done and not have left those aside.
texts.mat.23.24: Blind guides, who strain out the gnat, but drink down the camel.
texts.mat.23.25: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the dish, but within they are full of rapine and intemperance.
texts.mat.23.26: Blind Pharisee, make clean first the inside of the cup and of the dish, that their outside also may become clean.
texts.mat.23.27: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for ye are like whited sepulchres, which appear beautiful outwardly, but within are full of dead men's bones and all uncleanness.
texts.mat.23.28: Thus also *ye*, outwardly ye appear righteous to men, but within are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
texts.mat.23.29: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for ye build the sepulchres of the prophets and adorn the tombs of the just,
texts.mat.23.30: and ye say, If we had been in the days of our fathers we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.
texts.mat.23.31: So that ye bear witness of yourselves that ye are sons of those who slew the prophets:
texts.mat.23.32: and *ye*, fill ye up the measure of your fathers.
texts.mat.23.33: Serpents, offspring of vipers, how should ye escape the judgment of hell?
texts.mat.23.34: Therefore, behold, *I* send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes; and [some] of them ye will kill and crucify, and [some] of them ye will scourge in your synagogues, and will persecute from city to city;
texts.mat.23.35: so that all righteous blood shed upon the earth should come upon *you*, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.
texts.mat.23.36: Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.
texts.mat.23.37: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, [the city] that kills the prophets and stones those that are sent unto her, how often would I have gathered thy children as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
texts.mat.23.38: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate;
texts.mat.23.39: for I say unto you, Ye shall in no wise see me henceforth until ye say, Blessed [be] he that comes in the name of [the] Lord.
texts.mat.24.1: And Jesus went forth and went away from the temple, and his disciples came to [him] to point out to him the buildings of the temple.
texts.mat.24.2: And he answering said to them, Do ye not see all these things? Verily I say to you, Not a stone shall be left here upon a stone which shall not be thrown down.
texts.mat.24.3: And as he was sitting upon the mount of Olives the disciples came to him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be, and what is the sign of thy coming and [the] completion of the age?
texts.mat.24.4: And Jesus answering said to them, See that no one mislead you.
texts.mat.24.5: For many shall come in my name, saying, *I* am the Christ, and they shall mislead many.
texts.mat.24.6: But ye will hear of wars and rumours of wars. See that ye be not disturbed; for all [these things] must take place, but it is not yet the end.
texts.mat.24.7: For nation shall rise up against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and there shall be famines and pestilences, and earthquakes in divers places.
texts.mat.24.8: But all these [are the] beginning of throes.
texts.mat.24.9: Then shall they deliver you up to tribulation, and shall kill you; and ye will be hated of all the nations for my name's sake.
texts.mat.24.10: And then will many be offended, and will deliver one another up, and hate one another;
texts.mat.24.11: and many false prophets shall arise and shall mislead many;
texts.mat.24.12: and because lawlessness shall prevail, the love of the most shall grow cold;
texts.mat.24.13: but he that has endured to the end, *he* shall be saved.
texts.mat.24.14: And these glad tidings of the kingdom shall be preached in the whole habitable earth, for a witness to all the nations, and then shall come the end.
texts.mat.24.15: When therefore ye shall see the abomination of desolation, which is spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in [what is a] holy place, (he that reads let him understand,)
texts.mat.24.16: then let those who are in Judaea flee to the mountains;
texts.mat.24.17: let not him that is on the house come down to take the things out of his house;
texts.mat.24.18: and let not him that is in the field turn back to take his garment.
texts.mat.24.19: But woe to those that are with child, and those that give suck in those days.
texts.mat.24.20: But pray that your flight may not be in winter time nor on sabbath:
texts.mat.24.21: for then shall there be great tribulation, such as has not been from [the] beginning of [the] world until now, nor ever shall be;
texts.mat.24.22: and if those days had not been cut short, no flesh had been saved; but on account of the elect those days shall be cut short.
texts.mat.24.23: Then if any one say to you, Behold, here is the Christ, or here, believe [it] not.
texts.mat.24.24: For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall give great signs and wonders, so as to mislead, if possible, even the elect.
texts.mat.24.25: Behold, I have told you beforehand.
texts.mat.24.26: If therefore they say to you, Behold, he is in the desert, go not forth; behold, [he is] in the inner chambers, do not believe [it].
texts.mat.24.27: For as the lightning goes forth from the east and shines to the west, so shall be the coming of the Son of man.
texts.mat.24.28: [For] wherever the carcase is, there will be gathered the eagles.
texts.mat.24.29: But immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun shall be darkened, and the moon not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken.
texts.mat.24.30: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven; and then shall all the tribes of the land lament, and they shall see the Son of man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
texts.mat.24.31: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from [the one] extremity of [the] heavens to [the other] extremity of them.
texts.mat.24.32: But learn the parable from the fig-tree: When already its branch becomes tender and produces leaves, ye know that the summer is near.
texts.mat.24.33: Thus also *ye*, when ye see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors.
texts.mat.24.34: Verily I say to you, This generation will not have passed away until all these things shall have taken place.
texts.mat.24.35: The heaven and the earth shall pass away, but my words shall in no wise pass away.
texts.mat.24.36: But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of the heavens, but [my] Father alone.
texts.mat.24.37: But as the days of Noe, so also shall be the coming of the Son of man.
texts.mat.24.38: For as they were in the days which were before the flood, eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day on which Noe entered into the ark,
texts.mat.24.39: and they knew not till the flood came and took all away; thus also shall be the coming of the Son of man.
texts.mat.24.40: Then two shall be in the field, one is taken and one is left;
texts.mat.24.41: two [women] grinding at the mill, one is taken and one is left.
texts.mat.24.42: Watch therefore, for ye know not in what hour your Lord comes.
texts.mat.24.43: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have watched and not have suffered his house to be dug through [into].
texts.mat.24.44: Wherefore *ye* also, be ye ready, for in that hour that ye think not the Son of man comes.
texts.mat.24.45: Who then is the faithful and prudent bondman whom his lord has set over his household, to give them food in season?
texts.mat.24.46: Blessed is that bondman whom his lord on coming shall find doing thus.
texts.mat.24.47: Verily I say unto you, that he will set him over all his substance.
texts.mat.24.48: But if that evil bondman should say in his heart, My lord delays to come,
texts.mat.24.49: and begin to beat his fellow-bondmen, and eat and drink with the drunken;
texts.mat.24.50: the lord of that bondman shall come in a day when he does not expect it, and in an hour he knows not of,
texts.mat.24.51: and shall cut him in two and appoint his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.25.1: Then shall the kingdom of the heavens be made like to ten virgins that having taken their torches, went forth to meet the bridegroom.
texts.mat.25.2: And five of them were prudent and five foolish.
texts.mat.25.3: They that were foolish took their torches and did not take oil with them;
texts.mat.25.4: but the prudent took oil in their vessels with their torches.
texts.mat.25.5: Now the bridegroom tarrying, they all grew heavy and slept.
texts.mat.25.6: But in [the] middle of [the] night there was a cry, Behold, the bridegroom; go forth to meet him.
texts.mat.25.7: Then all those virgins arose and trimmed their torches.
texts.mat.25.8: And the foolish said to the prudent, Give us of your oil, for our torches are going out.
texts.mat.25.9: But the prudent answered saying, [We cannot,] lest it might not suffice for us and for you. Go rather to those that sell, and buy for yourselves.
texts.mat.25.10: But as they went away to buy, the bridegroom came, and the [ones that were] ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
texts.mat.25.11: Afterwards come also the rest of the virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us;
texts.mat.25.12: but he answering said, Verily I say unto you, I do not know you.
texts.mat.25.13: Watch therefore, for ye know not the day nor the hour.
texts.mat.25.14: For [it is] as [if] a man going away out of a country called his own bondmen and delivered to them his substance.
texts.mat.25.15: And to one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to each according to his particular ability, and immediately went away out of the country.
texts.mat.25.16: And he that had received the five talents went and trafficked with them, and made five other talents.
texts.mat.25.17: In like manner also he that [had received] the two, [he also] gained two others.
texts.mat.25.18: But he that had received the one went and dug in the earth, and hid the money of his lord.
texts.mat.25.19: And after a long time the lord of those bondmen comes and reckons with them.
texts.mat.25.20: And he that had received the five talents came to [him] and brought five other talents, saying, [My] lord, thou deliveredst me five talents; behold, I have gained five other talents besides them.
texts.mat.25.21: His lord said to him, Well, good and faithful bondman, thou wast faithful over a few things, I will set thee over many things: enter into the joy of thy lord.
texts.mat.25.22: And he also that had received the two talents came to [him] and said, [My] lord, thou deliveredst me two talents; behold, I have gained two other talents besides them.
texts.mat.25.23: His lord said to him, Well, good and faithful bondman, thou wast faithful over a few things, I will set thee over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
texts.mat.25.24: And he also that had received the one talent coming to [him] said, [My] lord, I knew thee that thou art a hard man, reaping where thou hadst not sowed, and gathering from where thou hadst not scattered,
texts.mat.25.25: and being afraid I went away and hid thy talent in the earth; behold, thou hast that which is thine.
texts.mat.25.26: And his lord answering said to him, Wicked and slothful bondman, thou knewest that I reap where I had not sowed, and gather from where I had not scattered;
texts.mat.25.27: thou oughtest then to have put my money to the money-changers, and when I came I should have got what is mine with interest.
texts.mat.25.28: Take therefore the talent from him, and give it to him that has the ten talents:
texts.mat.25.29: for to every one that has shall be given, and he shall be in abundance; but from him that has not, that even which he has shall be taken from him.
texts.mat.25.30: And cast out the useless bondman into the outer darkness; there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.25.31: But when the Son of man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then shall he sit down upon his throne of glory,
texts.mat.25.32: and all the nations shall be gathered before him; and he shall separate them from one another, as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats;
texts.mat.25.33: and he will set the sheep on his right hand, and the goats on [his] left.
texts.mat.25.34: Then shall the King say to those on his right hand, Come, blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from [the] world's foundation:
texts.mat.25.35: for I hungered, and ye gave me to eat; I thirsted, and ye gave me to drink; I was a stranger, and ye took me in;
texts.mat.25.36: naked, and ye clothed me; I was ill, and ye visited me; I was in prison, and ye came to me.
texts.mat.25.37: Then shall the righteous answer him saying, Lord, when saw we thee hungering, and nourished thee; or thirsting, and gave thee to drink?
texts.mat.25.38: and when saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in; or naked, and clothed thee?
texts.mat.25.39: and when saw we thee ill, or in prison, and came to thee?
texts.mat.25.40: And the King answering shall say to them, Verily, I say to you, Inasmuch as ye have done it to one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it to me.
texts.mat.25.41: Then shall he say also to those on the left, Go from me, cursed, into eternal fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:
texts.mat.25.42: for I hungered, and ye gave me not to eat; I thirsted, and ye gave me not to drink;
texts.mat.25.43: I was a stranger, and ye took me not in; naked, and ye did not clothe me; ill, and in prison, and ye did not visit me.
texts.mat.25.44: Then shall *they* also answer saying, Lord, when saw we thee hungering, or thirsting, or a stranger, or naked, or ill, or in prison, and have not ministered to thee?
texts.mat.25.45: Then shall he answer them saying, Verily I say to you, Inasmuch as ye have not done it to one of these least, neither have ye done it to me.
texts.mat.25.46: And these shall go away into eternal punishment, and the righteous into life eternal.
texts.mat.26.1: And it came to pass when Jesus had finished all these sayings, he said to his disciples,
texts.mat.26.2: Ye know that after two days the passover takes place, and the Son of man is delivered up to be crucified.
texts.mat.26.3: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people were gathered together to the palace of the high priest who was called Caiaphas,
texts.mat.26.4: and took counsel together in order that they might seize Jesus by subtlety and kill him;
texts.mat.26.5: but they said, Not in the feast, that there be not a tumult among the people.
texts.mat.26.6: But Jesus being in Bethany, in Simon the leper's house,
texts.mat.26.7: a woman, having an alabaster flask of very precious ointment, came to him and poured it out upon his head as he lay at table.
texts.mat.26.8: But the disciples seeing it became indignant, saying, To what end [was] this waste?
texts.mat.26.9: for this might have been sold for much and been given to the poor.
texts.mat.26.10: But Jesus knowing [it] said to them, Why do ye trouble the woman? for she has wrought a good work toward me.
texts.mat.26.11: For ye have the poor always with you, but me ye have not always.
texts.mat.26.12: For in pouring out this ointment on my body, she has done it for my burying.
texts.mat.26.13: Verily I say to you, Wheresoever these glad tidings may be preached in the whole world, that also which this [woman] has done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.
texts.mat.26.14: Then one of the twelve, he who was called Judas Iscariote, went to the chief priests
texts.mat.26.15: and said, What are ye willing to give me, and *I* will deliver him up to you? And they appointed to him thirty pieces of silver.
texts.mat.26.16: And from that time he sought a good opportunity that he might deliver him up.
texts.mat.26.17: Now on the first [day] of [the feast of] unleavened bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying, Where wilt thou that we prepare for thee to eat the passover?
texts.mat.26.18: And he said, Go into the city unto such a one, and say to him, The Teacher says, My time is near, I will keep the passover in thy house with my disciples.
texts.mat.26.19: And the disciples did as Jesus had directed them, and they prepared the passover.
texts.mat.26.20: And when the evening was come he lay down at table with the twelve.
texts.mat.26.21: And as they were eating he said, Verily I say to you, that one of you shall deliver me up.
texts.mat.26.22: And being exceedingly grieved they began to say to him, each of them, Is it *I*, Lord?
texts.mat.26.23: But he answering said, He that dips his hand with me in the dish, *he* it is who shall deliver me up.
texts.mat.26.24: The Son of man goes indeed, according as it is written concerning him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of man is delivered up; it were good for that man if he had not been born.
texts.mat.26.25: And Judas, who delivered him up, answering said, Is it *I*, Rabbi? He says to him, *Thou* hast said.
texts.mat.26.26: And as they were eating, Jesus, having taken [the] bread and blessed, broke [it] and gave [it] to the disciples, and said, Take, eat: this is my body.
texts.mat.26.27: And having taken [the] cup and given thanks, he gave [it] to them, saying, Drink ye all of it.
texts.mat.26.28: For this is my blood, that of the [new] covenant, that shed for many for remission of sins.
texts.mat.26.29: But I say to you, that I will not at all drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father.
texts.mat.26.30: And having sung a hymn, they went out to the mount of Olives.
texts.mat.26.31: Then saith Jesus to them, All *ye* shall be offended in me during this night. For it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad.
texts.mat.26.32: But after that I shall be risen, I will go before you to Galilee.
texts.mat.26.33: And Peter answering said to him, If all shall be offended in thee, *I* will never be offended.
texts.mat.26.34: Jesus said to him, Verily I say to thee, that during this night, before [the] cock shall crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
texts.mat.26.35: Peter says to him, If I should needs die with thee, I will in no wise deny thee. Likewise said all the disciples also.
texts.mat.26.36: Then Jesus comes with them to a place called Gethsemane, and says to the disciples, Sit here until I go away and pray yonder.
texts.mat.26.37: And taking with [him] Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be sorrowful and deeply depressed.
texts.mat.26.38: Then he says to them, My soul is very sorrowful even unto death; remain here and watch with me.
texts.mat.26.39: And going forward a little he fell upon his face, praying and saying, My Father, if it be possible let this cup pass from me; but not as *I* will, but as *thou* [wilt].
texts.mat.26.40: And he comes to the disciples and finds them sleeping, and says to Peter, Thus ye have not been able to watch one hour with me?
texts.mat.26.41: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed [is] ready, but the flesh weak.
texts.mat.26.42: Again going away a second time he prayed saying, My Father, if this cannot pass [from me] unless I drink it, thy will be done.
texts.mat.26.43: And coming he found them again sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
texts.mat.26.44: And leaving them, he went away again and prayed the third time, saying the same thing.
texts.mat.26.45: Then he comes to the disciples and says to them, Sleep on now and take your rest; behold, the hour has drawn nigh, and the Son of man is delivered up into the hands of sinners.
texts.mat.26.46: Arise, let us go; behold, he that delivers me up has drawn nigh.
texts.mat.26.47: And while he was yet speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great crowd with swords and sticks from the chief priests and elders of the people.
texts.mat.26.48: Now he that delivered him up had given them a sign, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, he it is: seize him.
texts.mat.26.49: And immediately coming up to Jesus he said, Hail, Rabbi, and covered him with kisses.
texts.mat.26.50: But Jesus said to him, [My] friend, for what purpose art thou come? Then coming up they laid hands upon Jesus and seized him.
texts.mat.26.51: And behold, one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand and drew his sword, and smiting the bondman of the high priest took off his ear.
texts.mat.26.52: Then saith Jesus to him, Return thy sword to its place; for all who take the sword shall perish by the sword.
texts.mat.26.53: Or thinkest thou that I cannot now call upon my Father, and he will furnish me more than twelve legions of angels?
texts.mat.26.54: How then should the scriptures be fulfilled that thus it must be?
texts.mat.26.55: In that hour Jesus said to the crowds, Are ye come out as against a robber with swords and sticks to take me? I sat daily [with you] teaching in the temple, and ye did not seize me.
texts.mat.26.56: But all this is come to pass that the scriptures of the prophets may be fulfilled. Then all the disciples left him and fled.
texts.mat.26.57: Now they that had seized Jesus led [him] away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were assembled.
texts.mat.26.58: And Peter followed him at a distance, even to the palace of the high priest, and entering in sat with the officers to see the end.
texts.mat.26.59: And the chief priests and the elders and the whole sanhedrim sought false witness against Jesus, so that they might put him to death.
texts.mat.26.60: And they found none, though many false witnesses came forward. But at the last two false witnesses came forward
texts.mat.26.61: and said, *He* said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and in three days build it.
texts.mat.26.62: And the high priest standing up said to him, Answerest thou nothing? What do these witness against thee?
texts.mat.26.63: But Jesus was silent. And the high priest answering said to him, I adjure thee by the living God that thou tell us if *thou* art the Christ the Son of God.
texts.mat.26.64: Jesus says to him, *Thou* hast said. Moreover, I say to you, From henceforth ye shall see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of power, and coming on the clouds of heaven.
texts.mat.26.65: Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He has blasphemed: what need have we any more of witnesses? behold, now ye have heard the blasphemy.
texts.mat.26.66: What think ye? And they answering said, He is liable to the penalty of death.
texts.mat.26.67: Then they spit in his face, and buffeted him, and some struck him with the palms of their hand,
texts.mat.26.68: saying, Prophesy to us, Christ, Who is it who struck thee?
texts.mat.26.69: But Peter sat without in the palace-court; and a maid came to him, saying, And *thou* wast with Jesus the Galilaean.
texts.mat.26.70: But he denied before all, saying, I do not know what thou sayest.
texts.mat.26.71: And when he had gone out into the entrance, another [maid] saw him, and says to those there, This [man] also was with Jesus the Nazaraean.
texts.mat.26.72: And again he denied with an oath: I do not know the man.
texts.mat.26.73: And after a little, those who stood [there], coming to [him], said to Peter, Truly *thou* too art of them, for also thy speech makes thee manifest.
texts.mat.26.74: Then he began to curse and to swear, I know not the man. And immediately [the] cock crew.
texts.mat.26.75: And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, who had said [to him], Before [the] cock crow thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went forth without, and wept bitterly.
texts.mat.27.1: And when it was morning all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus so that they might put him to death.
texts.mat.27.2: And having bound him they led him away, and delivered him up to Pontius Pilate, the governor.
texts.mat.27.3: Then Judas, who delivered him up, seeing that he had been condemned, filled with remorse, returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and the elders,
texts.mat.27.4: saying, I have sinned [in] having delivered up guiltless blood. But they said, What is that to us? see *thou* [to that].
texts.mat.27.5: And having cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, he left the place, and went away and hanged himself.
texts.mat.27.6: And the chief priests took the pieces of silver and said, It is not lawful to cast them into the Corban, since it is [the] price of blood.
texts.mat.27.7: And having taken counsel, they bought with them the field of the potter for a burying-ground for strangers.
texts.mat.27.8: Wherefore that field has been called Blood-field unto this day.
texts.mat.27.9: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken through Jeremias the prophet, saying, And I took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was set a price on, whom [they who were] of the sons of Israel had set a price on,
texts.mat.27.10: and they gave them for the field of the potter, according as [the] Lord commanded me.
texts.mat.27.11: But Jesus stood before the governor. And the governor questioned him, saying, Art *thou* the King of the Jews? And Jesus said to him, Thou sayest.
texts.mat.27.12: And when he was accused of the chief priests and the elders, he answered nothing.
texts.mat.27.13: Then says Pilate to him, Hearest thou not how many things they witness against thee?
texts.mat.27.14: And he answered him not so much as one word, so that the governor wondered exceedingly.
texts.mat.27.15: Now at [the] feast the governor was accustomed to release one prisoner to the crowd, whom they would.
texts.mat.27.16: And they had then a notable prisoner, named Barabbas.
texts.mat.27.17: They therefore being gathered together, Pilate said to them, Whom will ye that I release to you, Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?
texts.mat.27.18: For he knew that they had delivered him up through envy.
texts.mat.27.19: But, as he was sitting on the judgment-seat, his wife sent to him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that righteous [man]; for I have suffered to-day many things in a dream because of him.
texts.mat.27.20: But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds that they should beg for Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.
texts.mat.27.21: And the governor answering said to them, Which of the two will ye that I release unto you? And they said, Barabbas.
texts.mat.27.22: Pilate says to them, What then shall I do with Jesus, who is called Christ? They all say, Let him be crucified.
texts.mat.27.23: And the governor said, What evil then has he done? But they cried more than ever, saying, Let him be crucified.
texts.mat.27.24: And Pilate, seeing that it availed nothing, but that rather a tumult was arising, having taken water, washed his hands before the crowd, saying, I am guiltless of the blood of this righteous one: see *ye* [to it].
texts.mat.27.25: And all the people answering said, His blood [be] on us and on our children.
texts.mat.27.26: Then he released to them Barabbas; but Jesus, having scourged [him], he delivered up that he might be crucified.
texts.mat.27.27: Then the soldiers of the governor, having taken Jesus with [them] to the praetorium, gathered against him the whole band,
texts.mat.27.28: and having taken off his garment, put on him a scarlet cloak;
texts.mat.27.29: and having woven a crown out of thorns, they put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand; and, bowing the knee before him, they mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!
texts.mat.27.30: And having spit upon him, they took the reed and beat [him] on his head.
texts.mat.27.31: And when they had mocked him, they took the cloak off him, and put his own clothes on him, and led him away to crucify.
texts.mat.27.32: And as they went forth they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name; him they compelled to go [with them] that he might bear his cross.
texts.mat.27.33: And having come to a place called Golgotha, which means Place of a skull,
texts.mat.27.34: they gave to him to drink vinegar mingled with gall; and having tasted [it], he would not drink.
texts.mat.27.35: And having crucified him, they parted his clothes amongst [themselves], casting lots.
texts.mat.27.36: And sitting down, they kept guard over him there.
texts.mat.27.37: And they set up over his head his accusation written: This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.
texts.mat.27.38: Then are crucified with him two robbers, one on the right hand and one on the left.
texts.mat.27.39: But the passers-by reviled him, shaking their heads
texts.mat.27.40: and saying, Thou that destroyest the temple and buildest it in three days, save thyself. If thou art Son of God, descend from the cross.
texts.mat.27.41: [And] in like manner the chief priests also, mocking, with the scribes and elders, said,
texts.mat.27.42: He saved others, himself he cannot save. He is King of Israel: let him descend now from the cross, and we will believe on him.
texts.mat.27.43: He trusted upon God; let him save him now if he will [have] him. For he said, I am Son of God.
texts.mat.27.44: And the robbers also who had been crucified with him cast the same reproaches on him.
texts.mat.27.45: Now from [the] sixth hour there was darkness over the whole land until [the] ninth hour;
texts.mat.27.46: but about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
texts.mat.27.47: And some of those who stood there, when they heard [it], said, This [man] calls for Elias.
texts.mat.27.48: And immediately one of them running and getting a sponge, having filled [it] with vinegar and fixed [it] on a reed, gave him to drink.
texts.mat.27.49: But the rest said, Let be; let us see if Elias comes to save him.
texts.mat.27.50: And Jesus, having again cried with a loud voice, gave up the ghost.
texts.mat.27.51: And lo, the veil of the temple was rent in two from the top to the bottom, and the earth was shaken, and the rocks were rent,
texts.mat.27.52: and the tombs were opened; and many bodies of the saints fallen asleep arose,
texts.mat.27.53: and going out of the tombs after his arising, entered into the holy city and appeared unto many.
texts.mat.27.54: But the centurion, and they who were with him on guard over Jesus, seeing the earthquake and the things that took place, feared greatly, saying, Truly this [man] was Son of God.
texts.mat.27.55: And there were there many women beholding from afar off, who had followed Jesus from Galilee ministering to him,
texts.mat.27.56: among whom was Mary of Magdala, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
texts.mat.27.57: Now when even was come there came a rich man of Arimathaea, his name Joseph, who also himself was a disciple to Jesus.
texts.mat.27.58: *He*, going to Pilate, begged the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded the body to be given up.
texts.mat.27.59: And Joseph having got the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
texts.mat.27.60: and laid it in his new tomb which he had hewn in the rock; and having rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb, went away.
texts.mat.27.61: But Mary of Magdala was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the sepulchre.
texts.mat.27.62: Now on the morrow, which is after the preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees came together to Pilate,
texts.mat.27.63: saying, Sir, we have called to mind that that deceiver said when he was still alive, After three days I arise.
texts.mat.27.64: Command therefore that the sepulchre be secured until the third day, lest his disciples should come and steal him away, and say to the people, He is risen from the dead; and the last error shall be worse than the first.
texts.mat.27.65: And Pilate said to them, Ye have a watch: go, secure it as well as ye know how.
texts.mat.27.66: And they went and secured the sepulchre, having sealed the stone, with the watch [besides].
texts.mat.28.1: Now late on sabbath, as it was the dusk of the next day after sabbath, came Mary of Magdala and the other Mary to look at the sepulchre.
texts.mat.28.2: And behold, there was a great earthquake; for an angel of [the] Lord, descending out of heaven, came and rolled away the stone and sat upon it.
texts.mat.28.3: And his look was as lightning, and his clothing white as snow.
texts.mat.28.4: And for fear of him the guards trembled and became as dead men.
texts.mat.28.5: And the angel answering said to the women, Fear not *ye*, for I know that ye seek Jesus the crucified one.
texts.mat.28.6: He is not here, for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
texts.mat.28.7: And go quickly and say to his disciples that he is risen from the dead; and behold, he goes before you into Galilee, there shall ye see him. Behold, I have told you.
texts.mat.28.8: And going out quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, they ran to bring his disciples word.
texts.mat.28.9: And as they went to bring his disciples word, behold also, Jesus met them, saying, Hail! And they coming up took him by the feet, and did him homage.
texts.mat.28.10: Then Jesus says to them, Fear not; go, bring word to my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there they shall see me.
texts.mat.28.11: And as they went, behold, some of the watch went into the city, and brought word to the chief priests of all that had taken place.
texts.mat.28.12: And having assembled with the elders, and having taken counsel, they gave a large sum of money to the soldiers,
texts.mat.28.13: saying, Say that his disciples coming by night stole him [while] we [were] sleeping.
texts.mat.28.14: And if this should come to the hearing of the governor, *we* will persuade him, and save *you* from all anxiety.
texts.mat.28.15: And they took the money and did as they had been taught. And this report is current among the Jews until this day.
texts.mat.28.16: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee to the mountain which Jesus had appointed them.
texts.mat.28.17: And when they saw him, they did homage to him: but some doubted.
texts.mat.28.18: And Jesus coming up spoke to them, saying, All power has been given me in heaven and upon earth.
texts.mat.28.19: Go [therefore] and make disciples of all the nations, baptising them to the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit;
texts.mat.28.20: teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have enjoined you. And behold, *I* am with you all the days, until the completion of the age.

texts.mat.1.1: A roll of the birth of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
texts.mat.1.2: Abraham begat Isaac, and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob begat Judah and his brethren,
texts.mat.1.3: and Judah begat Pharez and Zarah of Tamar, and Pharez begat Hezron, and Hezron begat Ram,
texts.mat.1.4: and Ram begat Amminadab, and Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon,
texts.mat.1.5: and Salmon begat Boaz of Rahab, and Boaz begat Obed of Ruth, and Obed begat Jesse,
texts.mat.1.6: and Jesse begat David the king. And David the king begat Solomon, of her [who had been] Uriah's,
texts.mat.1.7: and Solomon begat Rehoboam, and Rehoboam begat Abijah, and Abijah begat Asa,
texts.mat.1.8: and Asa begat Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat begat Joram, and Joram begat Uzziah,
texts.mat.1.9: and Uzziah begat Jotham, and Jotham begat Ahaz, and Ahaz begat Hezekiah,
texts.mat.1.10: and Hezekiah begat Manasseh, and Manasseh begat Amon, and Amon begat Josiah,
texts.mat.1.11: and Josiah begat Jeconiah and his brethren, at the Babylonian removal.
texts.mat.1.12: And after the Babylonian removal, Jeconiah begat Shealtiel, and Shealtiel begat Zerubbabel,
texts.mat.1.13: and Zerubbabel begat Abiud, and Abiud begat Eliakim, and Eliakim begat Azor,
texts.mat.1.14: and Azor begat Sadok, and Sadok begat Achim, and Achim begat Eliud,
texts.mat.1.15: and Eliud begat Eleazar, and Eleazar begat Matthan, and Matthan begat Jacob,
texts.mat.1.16: and Jacob begat Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was begotten Jesus, who is named Christ.
texts.mat.1.17: All the generations, therefore, from Abraham unto David [are] fourteen generations, and from David unto the Babylonian removal fourteen generations, and from the Babylonian removal unto the Christ, fourteen generations.
texts.mat.1.18: And of Jesus Christ, the birth was thus: For his mother Mary having been betrothed to Joseph, before their coming together she was found to have conceived from the Holy Spirit,
texts.mat.1.19: and Joseph her husband being righteous, and not willing to make her an example, did wish privately to send her away.
texts.mat.1.20: And on his thinking of these things, lo, a messenger of the Lord in a dream appeared to him, saying, `Joseph, son of David, thou mayest not fear to receive Mary thy wife, for that which in her was begotten [is] of the Holy Spirit,
texts.mat.1.21: and she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name Jesus, for he shall save his people from their sins.'
texts.mat.1.22: And all this hath come to pass, that it may be fulfilled that was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,
texts.mat.1.23: `Lo, the virgin shall conceive, and she shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel,' which is, being interpreted `With us [he is] God.'
texts.mat.1.24: And Joseph, having risen from the sleep, did as the messenger of the Lord directed him, and received his wife,
texts.mat.1.25: and did not know her till she brought forth her son -- the first-born, and he called his name Jesus.
texts.mat.2.1: And Jesus having been born in Beth-Lehem of Judea, in the days of Herod the king, lo, mages from the east came to Jerusalem,
texts.mat.2.2: saying, `Where is he who was born king of the Jews? for we saw his star in the east, and we came to bow to him.'
texts.mat.2.3: And Herod the king having heard, was stirred, and all Jerusalem with him,
texts.mat.2.4: and having gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he was inquiring from them where the Christ is born.
texts.mat.2.5: And they said to him, `In Beth-Lehem of Judea, for thus it hath been written through the prophet,
texts.mat.2.6: And thou, Beth-Lehem, the land of Judah, thou art by no means the least among the leaders of Judah, for out of thee shall come one leading, who shall feed My people Israel.'
texts.mat.2.7: Then Herod, privately having called the mages, did inquire exactly from them the time of the appearing star,
texts.mat.2.8: and having sent them to Beth-Lehem, he said, `Having gone -- inquire ye exactly for the child, and whenever ye may have found, bring me back word, that I also having come may bow to him.'
texts.mat.2.9: And they, having heard the king, departed, and lo, the star, that they did see in the east, did go before them, till, having come, it stood over where the child was.
texts.mat.2.10: And having seen the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy,
texts.mat.2.11: and having come to the house, they found the child with Mary his mother, and having fallen down they bowed to him, and having opened their treasures, they presented to him gifts, gold, and frankincense, and myrrh,
texts.mat.2.12: and having been divinely warned in a dream not to turn back unto Herod, through another way they withdrew to their own region.
texts.mat.2.13: And on their having withdrawn, lo, a messenger of the Lord doth appear in a dream to Joseph, saying, `Having risen, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and be thou there till I may speak to thee, for Herod is about to seek the child to destroy him.'
texts.mat.2.14: And he, having risen, took the child and his mother by night, and withdrew to Egypt,
texts.mat.2.15: and he was there till the death of Herod, that it might be fulfilled that was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying, `Out of Egypt I did call My Son.'
texts.mat.2.16: Then Herod, having seen that he was deceived by the mages, was very wroth, and having sent forth, he slew all the male children in Beth-Lehem, and in all its borders, from two years and under, according to the time that he inquired exactly from the mages.
texts.mat.2.17: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, saying,
texts.mat.2.18: `A voice in Ramah was heard -- lamentation and weeping and much mourning -- Rachel weeping [for] her children, and she would not be comforted because they are not.'
texts.mat.2.19: And Herod having died, lo, a messenger of the Lord in a dream doth appear to Joseph in Egypt,
texts.mat.2.20: saying, `Having risen, take the child and his mother, and be going to the land of Israel, for they have died -- those seeking the life of the child.'
texts.mat.2.21: And he, having risen, took the child and his mother, and came to the land of Israel,
texts.mat.2.22: and having heard that Archelaus doth reign over Judea instead of Herod his father, he was afraid to go thither, and having been divinely warned in a dream, he withdrew to the parts of Galilee,
texts.mat.2.23: and coming, he dwelt in a city named Nazareth, that it might be fulfilled that was spoken through the prophets, that `A Nazarene he shall be called.'
texts.mat.3.1: And in those days cometh John the Baptist, proclaiming in the wilderness of Judea,
texts.mat.3.2: and saying, `Reform, for come nigh hath the reign of the heavens,'
texts.mat.3.3: for this is he who was spoken of by Isaiah the prophet, saying, `A voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, straight make ye His paths.'
texts.mat.3.4: And this John had his clothing of camel's hair, and a girdle of skin round his loins, and his nourishment was locusts and honey of the field.
texts.mat.3.5: Then were going forth unto him Jerusalem, and all Judea, and all the region round about the Jordan,
texts.mat.3.6: and they were baptized in the Jordan by him, confessing their sins.
texts.mat.3.7: And having seen many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming about his baptism, he said to them, `Brood of vipers! who did shew you to flee from the coming wrath?
texts.mat.3.8: bear, therefore, fruits worthy of the reformation,
texts.mat.3.9: and do not think to say in yourselves, A father we have -- Abraham, for I say to you, that God is able out of these stones to raise children to Abraham,
texts.mat.3.10: and now also, the axe unto the root of the trees is laid, every tree therefore not bearing good fruit is hewn down, and to fire is cast.
texts.mat.3.11: `I indeed do baptize you with water to reformation, but he who after me is coming is mightier than I, of whom I am not worthy to bear the sandals, he shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire,
texts.mat.3.12: whose fan [is] in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his floor, and will gather his wheat to the storehouse, but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.'
texts.mat.3.13: Then cometh Jesus from Galilee upon the Jordan, unto John to be baptized by him,
texts.mat.3.14: but John was forbidding him, saying, `I have need by thee to be baptized -- and thou dost come unto me!'
texts.mat.3.15: But Jesus answering said to him, `Suffer now, for thus it is becoming to us to fulfill all righteousness,' then he doth suffer him.
texts.mat.3.16: And having been baptized, Jesus went up immediately from the water, and lo, opened to him were the heavens, and he saw the Spirit of God descending as a dove, and coming upon him,
texts.mat.3.17: and lo, a voice out of the heavens, saying, `This is My Son -- the Beloved, in whom I did delight.'
texts.mat.4.1: Then Jesus was led up to the wilderness by the Spirit, to be tempted by the Devil,
texts.mat.4.2: and having fasted forty days and forty nights, afterwards he did hunger.
texts.mat.4.3: And the Tempter having come to him said, `If Son thou art of God -- speak that these stones may become loaves.'
texts.mat.4.4: But he answering said, `It hath been written, Not upon bread alone doth man live, but upon every word coming forth from the mouth of God.'
texts.mat.4.5: Then doth the Devil take him to the [holy] city, and doth set him on the pinnacle of the temple,
texts.mat.4.6: and saith to him, `If Son thou art of God -- cast thyself down, for it hath been written, that, His messengers He shall charge concerning thee, and on hands they shall bear thee up, that thou mayest not dash on a stone thy foot.'
texts.mat.4.7: Jesus said to him again, `It hath been written, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.'
texts.mat.4.8: Again doth the Devil take him to a very high mount, and doth shew to him all the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them,
texts.mat.4.9: and saith to him, `All these to thee I will give, if falling down thou mayest bow to me.'
texts.mat.4.10: Then saith Jesus to him, `Go -- Adversary, for it hath been written, The Lord thy God thou shalt bow to, and Him only thou shalt serve.'
texts.mat.4.11: Then doth the Devil leave him, and lo, messengers came and were ministering to him.
texts.mat.4.12: And Jesus having heard that John was delivered up, did withdraw to Galilee,
texts.mat.4.13: and having left Nazareth, having come, he dwelt at Capernaum that is by the sea, in the borders of Zebulun and Naphtalim,
texts.mat.4.14: that it might be fulfilled that was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,
texts.mat.4.15: `Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations! --
texts.mat.4.16: the people that is sitting in darkness saw a great light, and to those sitting in a region and shadow of death -- light arose to them.'
texts.mat.4.17: From that time began Jesus to proclaim and to say, `Reform ye, for come nigh hath the reign of the heavens.'
texts.mat.4.18: And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brothers, Simon named Peter and Andrew his brother, casting a drag into the sea -- for they were fishers --
texts.mat.4.19: and he saith to them, `Come ye after me, and I will make you fishers of men,'
texts.mat.4.20: and they, immediately, having left the nets, did follow him.
texts.mat.4.21: And having advanced thence, he saw other two brothers, James of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, refitting their nets, and he called them,
texts.mat.4.22: and they, immediately, having left the boat and their father, did follow him.
texts.mat.4.23: And Jesus was going about all Galilee teaching in their synagogues, and proclaiming the good news of the reign, and healing every disease, and every malady among the people,
texts.mat.4.24: and his fame went forth to all Syria, and they brought to him all having ailments, pressed with manifold sicknesses and pains, and demoniacs, and lunatics, and paralytics, and he healed them.
texts.mat.4.25: And there followed him many multitudes from Galilee, and Decapolis, and Jerusalem, and Judea, and beyond the Jordan.
texts.mat.5.1: And having seen the multitudes, he went up to the mount, and he having sat down, his disciples came to him,
texts.mat.5.2: and having opened his mouth, he was teaching them, saying:
texts.mat.5.3: `Happy the poor in spirit -- because theirs is the reign of the heavens.
texts.mat.5.4: `Happy the mourning -- because they shall be comforted.
texts.mat.5.5: `Happy the meek -- because they shall inherit the land.
texts.mat.5.6: `Happy those hungering and thirsting for righteousness -- because they shall be filled.
texts.mat.5.7: `Happy the kind -- because they shall find kindness.
texts.mat.5.8: `Happy the clean in heart -- because they shall see God.
texts.mat.5.9: `Happy the peacemakers -- because they shall be called Sons of God.
texts.mat.5.10: `Happy those persecuted for righteousness' sake -- because theirs is the reign of the heavens.
texts.mat.5.11: `Happy are ye whenever they may reproach you, and may persecute, and may say any evil thing against you falsely for my sake --
texts.mat.5.12: rejoice ye and be glad, because your reward [is] great in the heavens, for thus did they persecute the prophets who were before you.
texts.mat.5.13: `Ye are the salt of the land, but if the salt may lose savour, in what shall it be salted? for nothing is it good henceforth, except to be cast without, and to be trodden down by men.
texts.mat.5.14: `Ye are the light of the world, a city set upon a mount is not able to be hid;
texts.mat.5.15: nor do they light a lamp, and put it under the measure, but on the lamp-stand, and it shineth to all those in the house;
texts.mat.5.16: so let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works, and may glorify your Father who [is] in the heavens.
texts.mat.5.17: `Do not suppose that I came to throw down the law or the prophets -- I did not come to throw down, but to fulfill;
texts.mat.5.18: for, verily I say to you, till that the heaven and the earth may pass away, one iota or one tittle may not pass away from the law, till that all may come to pass.
texts.mat.5.19: `Whoever therefore may loose one of these commands -- the least -- and may teach men so, least he shall be called in the reign of the heavens, but whoever may do and may teach [them], he shall be called great in the reign of the heavens.
texts.mat.5.20: `For I say to you, that if your righteousness may not abound above that of the scribes and Pharisees, ye may not enter to the reign of the heavens.
texts.mat.5.21: `Ye heard that it was said to the ancients: Thou shalt not kill, and whoever may kill shall be in danger of the judgment;
texts.mat.5.22: but I -- I say to you, that every one who is angry at his brother without cause, shall be in danger of the judgment, and whoever may say to his brother, Empty fellow! shall be in danger of the sanhedrim, and whoever may say, Rebel! shall be in danger of the gehenna of the fire.
texts.mat.5.23: `If, therefore, thou mayest bring thy gift to the altar, and there mayest remember that thy brother hath anything against thee,
texts.mat.5.24: leave there thy gift before the altar, and go -- first be reconciled to thy brother, and then having come bring thy gift.
texts.mat.5.25: `Be agreeing with thy opponent quickly, while thou art in the way with him, that the opponent may not deliver thee to the judge, and the judge may deliver thee to the officer, and to prison thou mayest be cast,
texts.mat.5.26: verily I say to thee, thou mayest not come forth thence till that thou mayest pay the last farthing.
texts.mat.5.27: `Ye heard that it was said to the ancients: Thou shalt not commit adultery;
texts.mat.5.28: but I -- I say to you, that every one who is looking on a woman to desire her, did already commit adultery with her in his heart.
texts.mat.5.29: `But, if thy right eye doth cause thee to stumble, pluck it out and cast from thee, for it is good to thee that one of thy members may perish, and not thy whole body be cast to gehenna.
texts.mat.5.30: `And, if thy right hand doth cause thee to stumble, cut it off, and cast from thee, for it is good to thee that one of thy members may perish, and not thy whole body be cast to gehenna.
texts.mat.5.31: `And it was said, That whoever may put away his wife, let him give to her a writing of divorce;
texts.mat.5.32: but I -- I say to you, that whoever may put away his wife, save for the matter of whoredom, doth make her to commit adultery; and whoever may marry her who hath been put away doth commit adultery.
texts.mat.5.33: `Again, ye heard that it was said to the ancients: Thou shalt not swear falsely, but thou shalt pay to the Lord thine oaths;
texts.mat.5.34: but I -- I say to you, not to swear at all; neither by the heaven, because it is the throne of God,
texts.mat.5.35: nor by the earth, because it is His footstool, nor by Jerusalem, because it is a city of a great king,
texts.mat.5.36: nor by thy head mayest thou swear, because thou art not able one hair to make white or black;
texts.mat.5.37: but let your word be, Yes, Yes, No, No, and that which is more than these is of the evil.
texts.mat.5.38: `Ye heard that it was said: Eye for eye, and tooth for tooth;
texts.mat.5.39: but I -- I say to you, not to resist the evil, but whoever shall slap thee on thy right cheek, turn to him also the other;
texts.mat.5.40: and whoever is willing to take thee to law, and thy coat to take -- suffer to him also the cloak.
texts.mat.5.41: `And whoever shall impress thee one mile, go with him two,
texts.mat.5.42: to him who is asking of thee be giving, and him who is willing to borrow from thee thou mayest not turn away.
texts.mat.5.43: `Ye heard that it was said: Thou shalt love thy neighbor, and shalt hate thine enemy;
texts.mat.5.44: but I -- I say to you, Love your enemies, bless those cursing you, do good to those hating you, and pray for those accusing you falsely, and persecuting you,
texts.mat.5.45: that ye may be sons of your Father in the heavens, because His sun He doth cause to rise on evil and good, and He doth send rain on righteous and unrighteous.
texts.mat.5.46: `For, if ye may love those loving you, what reward have ye? do not also the tax-gatherers the same?
texts.mat.5.47: and if ye may salute your brethren only, what do ye abundant? do not also the tax-gatherers so?
texts.mat.5.48: ye shall therefore be perfect, as your Father who [is] in the heavens is perfect.
texts.mat.6.1: `Take heed your kindness not to do before men, to be seen by them, and if not -- reward ye have not from your Father who [is] in the heavens;
texts.mat.6.2: whenever, therefore, thou mayest do kindness, thou mayest not sound a trumpet before thee as the hypocrites do, in the synagogues, and in the streets, that they may have glory from men; verily I say to you -- they have their reward!
texts.mat.6.3: `But thou, doing kindness, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doth,
texts.mat.6.4: that thy kindness may be in secret, and thy Father who is seeing in secret Himself shall reward thee manifestly.
texts.mat.6.5: `And when thou mayest pray, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites, because they love in the synagogues, and in the corners of the broad places -- standing -- to pray, that they may be seen of men; verily I say to you, that they have their reward.
texts.mat.6.6: `But thou, when thou mayest pray, go into thy chamber, and having shut thy door, pray to thy Father who [is] in secret, and thy Father who is seeing in secret, shall reward thee manifestly.
texts.mat.6.7: `And -- praying -- ye may not use vain repetitions like the nations, for they think that in their much speaking they shall be heard,
texts.mat.6.8: be ye not therefore like to them, for your Father doth know those things that ye have need of before your asking him;
texts.mat.6.9: thus therefore pray ye: `Our Father who [art] in the heavens! hallowed be Thy name.
texts.mat.6.10: `Thy reign come: Thy will come to pass, as in heaven also on the earth.
texts.mat.6.12: `And forgive us our debts, as also we forgive our debtors.
texts.mat.6.13: `And mayest Thou not lead us to temptation, but deliver us from the evil, because Thine is the reign, and the power, and the glory -- to the ages. Amen.
texts.mat.6.14: `For, if ye may forgive men their trespasses He also will forgive you -- your Father who [is] in the heavens;
texts.mat.6.15: but if ye may not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
texts.mat.6.16: `And when ye may fast, be ye not as the hypocrites, of sour countenances, for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear to men fasting; verily I say to you, that they have their reward.
texts.mat.6.17: `But thou, fasting, anoint thy head, and wash thy face,
texts.mat.6.18: that thou mayest not appear to men fasting, but to thy Father who [is] in secret, and thy Father, who is seeing in secret, shall reward thee manifestly.
texts.mat.6.19: `Treasure not up to yourselves treasures on the earth, where moth and rust disfigure, and where thieves break through and steal,
texts.mat.6.20: but treasure up to yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth disfigure, and where thieves do not break through nor steal,
texts.mat.6.21: for where your treasure is, there will be also your heart.
texts.mat.6.22: `The lamp of the body is the eye, if, therefore, thine eye may be perfect, all thy body shall be enlightened,
texts.mat.6.23: but if thine eye may be evil, all thy body shall be dark; if, therefore, the light that [is] in thee is darkness -- the darkness, how great!
texts.mat.6.24: `None is able to serve two lords, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to the one, and despise the other; ye are not able to serve God and Mammon.
texts.mat.6.25: `Because of this I say to you, be not anxious for your life, what ye may eat, and what ye may drink, nor for your body, what ye may put on. Is not the life more than the nourishment, and the body than the clothing?
texts.mat.6.26: look to the fowls of the heaven, for they do not sow, nor reap, nor gather into storehouses, and your heavenly Father doth nourish them; are not ye much better than they?
texts.mat.6.27: `And who of you, being anxious, is able to add to his age one cubit?
texts.mat.6.28: and about clothing why are ye anxious? consider well the lilies of the field; how do they grow? they do not labour, nor do they spin;
texts.mat.6.29: and I say to you, that not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed as one of these.
texts.mat.6.30: `And if the herb of the field, that to-day is, and to-morrow is cast to the furnace, God doth so clothe -- not much more you, O ye of little faith?
texts.mat.6.31: therefore ye may not be anxious, saying, What may we eat? or, What may we drink? or, What may we put round?
texts.mat.6.32: for all these do the nations seek for, for your heavenly Father doth know that ye have need of all these;
texts.mat.6.33: but seek ye first the reign of God and His righteousness, and all these shall be added to you.
texts.mat.6.34: Be not therefore anxious for the morrow, for the morrow shall be anxious for its own things; sufficient for the day [is] the evil of it.
texts.mat.7.1: `Judge not, that ye may not be judged,
texts.mat.7.2: for in what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged, and in what measure ye measure, it shall be measured to you.
texts.mat.7.3: `And why dost thou behold the mote that [is] in thy brother's eye, and the beam that [is] in thine own eye dost not consider?
texts.mat.7.4: or, how wilt thou say to thy brother, Suffer I may cast out the mote from thine eye, and lo, the beam [is] in thine own eye?
texts.mat.7.5: Hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye, and then thou shalt see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye.
texts.mat.7.6: `Ye may not give that which is [holy] to the dogs, nor cast your pearls before the swine, that they may not trample them among their feet, and having turned -- may rend you.
texts.mat.7.7: `Ask, and it shall be given to you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you;
texts.mat.7.8: for every one who is asking doth receive, and he who is seeking doth find, and to him who is knocking it shall be opened.
texts.mat.7.9: `Or what man is of you, of whom, if his son may ask a loaf -- a stone will he present to him?
texts.mat.7.10: and if a fish he may ask -- a serpent will he present to him?
