texts.mat.26.47: ¶ Y hablando aun él, he aquí, Júdas, uno de los doce, vino, y con él una grande multitud, con espadas y palos, de parte de los príncipes de los sacerdotes, y de los ancianos del pueblo.
texts.mat.26.48: Y el que le entregaba les había dado señal, diciendo: Al que yo besare, aquel es: tenédle bien.
texts.mat.26.49: Y luego que llegó a Jesús, dijo: Tengas gozo, Maestro. Y le besó.
texts.mat.26.50: Y Jesús le dijo: ¿Amigo, a qué vienes? Entonces llegaron, y echaron mano a Jesús, y le prendieron.
texts.mat.26.51: Y, he aquí, uno de los que estaban con Jesús, extendiendo la mano, sacó su espada, e hiriendo a un siervo del sumo sacerdote, le quitó una oreja.
texts.mat.26.52: Entonces Jesús le dice: Vuelve tu espada a su lugar; porque todos los que tomaren espada, a espada perecerán.
texts.mat.26.53: O ¿piensas que no puedo ahora orar a mi Padre, y él me daría más de doce legiones de ángeles?
texts.mat.26.54: Mas ¿cómo se cumplirían entonces las Escrituras, de que así es menester que sea hecho?
texts.mat.26.55: En aquella hora dijo Jesús a la multitud: Como a ladrón habéis salido con espadas y con palos a prenderme: cada día me sentaba con vosotros enseñando en el templo, y no me prendisteis.
texts.mat.26.56: Mas todo esto se hace, para que se cumplan las Escrituras de los profetas. Entonces todos los discípulos huyeron, dejándole.
texts.mat.26.57: Y ellos, prendido Jesús, le trajeron a Caifás sumo sacerdote, donde los escribas y los ancianos estaban juntos.
texts.mat.26.58: Mas Pedro le seguía de lejos hasta el patio del sumo sacerdote; y entrado dentro, se estaba sentado con los criados, para ver el fin.
texts.mat.26.59: Y los príncipes de los sacerdotes, y los ancianos, y todo el concilio buscaban algún falso testimonio contra Jesús, para entregarle a la muerte;
texts.mat.26.60: Y no hallaban: y aunque muchos testigos falsos se llegaban, no lo hallaron. Mas a la postre vinieron dos testigos falsos,
texts.mat.26.61: Que dijeron: Este dijo: Puedo derribar el templo de Dios, y reedificarle en tres días.
texts.mat.26.62: Y levantándose el sumo sacerdote, le dijo: ¿No respondes nada? ¿Qué testifican estos contra ti?
texts.mat.26.63: Mas Jesús callaba. Y respondiendo el sumo sacerdote, le dijo: Te conjuro por el Dios viviente, que nos digas, si eres tú el Cristo, Hijo de Dios.
texts.mat.26.64: Jesús le dice: Tú lo has dicho. Y aun os digo, que de aquí a poco habéis de ver al Hijo del hombre asentado a la diestra del poder de Dios, y viniendo sobre las nubes del cielo.
texts.mat.26.65: Entonces el sumo sacerdote rasgó sus vestiduras, diciendo: Blasfemado ha: ¿qué más necesidad tenemos de testigos? He aquí, ahora habéis oído su blasfemia.
texts.mat.26.66: ¿Qué os parece? Y respondiendo ellos dijeron: Culpado es de muerte.
texts.mat.26.67: Entonces le escupieron en su rostro, y le dieron de bofetadas, y otros le herían a puñadas,
texts.mat.26.68: Diciendo: Profetízanos, oh Cristo, quién es el que te ha herido.
texts.mat.26.69: ¶ Y Pedro estaba sentado fuera en el patio; y se llegó a él una criada, diciendo: Y tú con Jesús el Galileo estabas.
texts.mat.26.70: Mas él negó delante de todos, diciendo: No sé lo que dices.
texts.mat.26.71: Y saliendo a la puerta, le vio otra, y dijo a los que estaban allí: También éste estaba con Jesús Nazareno.
texts.mat.26.72: Y negó otra vez con juramento, diciendo: No conozco a ese hombre.
texts.mat.26.73: Y después de un poco se allegaron los que por allí estaban, y dijeron a Pedro: Verdaderamente también tú eres uno de ellos; porque aun tu habla te hace manifiesto.
texts.mat.26.74: Entonces comenzó a echarse maldiciones, y a jurar, diciendo: No conozco a ese hombre. Y el gallo cantó luego.
texts.mat.26.75: Y se acordó Pedro de las palabras de Jesús, que le dijo: Antes que cante el gallo, me negarás tres veces. Y saliéndose fuera, lloró amargamente.
texts.mat.27.1: Y venida la mañana, entraron en consejo todos los príncipes de los sacerdotes, y los ancianos del pueblo, contra Jesús, para entregarle a muerte.
texts.mat.27.2: Y le llevaron atado, y le entregaron a Poncio Pilato presidente.
texts.mat.27.3: Entonces Júdas, el que le había entregado, viendo que era condenado, volvió arrepentido las treinta piezas de plata a los príncipes de los sacerdotes, y a los ancianos,
texts.mat.27.4: Diciendo: Yo he pecado entregando la sangre inocente. Mas ellos dijeron: ¿Qué se nos da a nosotros? Viéraslo tú.
texts.mat.27.5: Y arrojando las piezas de plata al templo, se partió, y fue, y se ahorcó.
texts.mat.27.6: Y los príncipes de los sacerdotes, tomando las piezas de plata, dijeron: No es lícito echarlas en el tesoro, porque es precio de sangre.
texts.mat.27.7: Mas habido consejo, compraron con ellas el campo del Ollero, por sepultura para los extranjeros.
texts.mat.27.8: Por lo cual fue llamado aquel campo: Campo de sangre, hasta el día de hoy.
texts.mat.27.9: Entonces se cumplió lo que fue dicho por el profeta Jeremías, que dijo: Y tomaron las treinta piezas de plata, precio del apreciado, que fue apreciado por los hijos de Israel;
texts.mat.27.10: Y las dieron para comprar el campo del Ollero, como me ordenó el Señor.
texts.mat.27.11: ¶ Y Jesús estuvo delante del presidente, y el presidente le preguntó, diciendo: ¿Eres tú el rey de los Judíos? Y Jesús le dijo: Tú lo dices.
texts.mat.27.12: Y siendo acusado por los príncipes de los sacerdotes, y por los ancianos, nada respondió.
texts.mat.27.13: Pilato entonces le dice: ¿No oyes cuántas cosas testifican contra ti?
texts.mat.27.14: Y no le respondió ni una palabra, de tal manera que el presidente se maravillaba mucho.
texts.mat.27.15: ¶ Y en el día de la fiesta acostumbraba el presidente soltar al pueblo un preso cual quisiesen.
texts.mat.27.16: Y tenían entonces un preso famoso, que se llamaba Barrabás.
texts.mat.27.17: Y juntos ellos, les dijo Pilato: ¿Cuál queréis que os suelte? ¿a Barrabás, o a Jesús, que es llamado el Cristo?
texts.mat.27.18: Porque sabía que por envidia le habían entregado.
texts.mat.27.19: Y estando él sentado en el tribunal, su mujer envió a él, diciendo: No tengas que ver con aquel justo; porque hoy he padecido muchas cosas en sueños por causa de él.
texts.mat.27.20: Mas los príncipes de los sacerdotes, y los ancianos, persuadieron al pueblo, que pidiese a Barrabás, y a Jesús matase.
texts.mat.27.21: Y respondiendo el presidente, les dijo: ¿Cuál de los dos queréis que os suelte? Y ellos dijeron: A Barrabás.
texts.mat.27.22: Pilato les dijo: ¿Qué pues haré de Jesús que es llamado el Cristo? Dícenle todos: Sea crucificado.
texts.mat.27.23: Y el presidente les dijo: Pues ¿qué mal ha hecho? Mas ellos alzaban más el grito, diciendo: Sea crucificado.
texts.mat.27.24: Y viendo Pilato que nada aprovechaba, antes se hacía más alboroto, tomando agua lavó sus manos delante del pueblo, diciendo: Inocente soy yo de la sangre de este justo: véd lo vosotros.
texts.mat.27.25: Y respondiendo todo el pueblo, dijo: Su sangre sea sobre nosotros, y sobre nuestros hijos.
texts.mat.27.26: Entonces les soltó a Barrabás; y habiendo azotado a Jesús, le entregó para ser crucificado.
texts.mat.27.27: ¶ Entonces los soldados del presidente llevando a Jesús al pretorio, juntaron a él toda la cuadrilla.
texts.mat.27.28: Y desnudándole, echáronle encima un manto de grana.
texts.mat.27.29: Y pusieron sobre su cabeza una corona tejida de espinas, y una caña en su mano derecha; e hincando la rodilla delante de él, burlaban de él, diciendo: Tengas gozo, rey de los Judíos.
texts.mat.27.30: Y escupiendo en él, tomaron la caña, y le herían en la cabeza.
texts.mat.27.31: Y después que le hubieron escarnecido, le desnudaron el manto, y le vistieron de sus vestidos, y le llevaron para crucificar le.
texts.mat.27.32: Y saliendo, hallaron a un Cireneo que se llamaba Simón: a éste cargaron para que llevase su cruz.
texts.mat.27.33: Y como llegaron al lugar que se llama Gólgota, que quiere decir, el lugar de la Calavera,
texts.mat.27.34: Le dieron a beber vinagre mezclado con hiel; y gustando, no quiso beberlo.
texts.mat.27.35: Y después que le hubieron crucificado, repartieron sus vestidos, echando suertes; para que se cumpliese lo que fue dicho por el profeta: Se repartieron mis vestidos, y sobre mi ropa echaron suertes.
texts.mat.27.37: Y pusieron sobre su cabeza su causa escrita: ESTE ES JESUS, EL REY DE LOS JUDÍOS.
texts.mat.27.38: Entonces crucificaron con él dos ladrones: uno a la derecha, y otro a la izquierda.
texts.mat.27.39: Y los que pasaban, le decían injurias, meneando sus cabezas,
texts.mat.27.40: Y diciendo: Tú, el que derribas el templo, y en tres días lo reedificas, sálvate a ti mismo. Si eres Hijo de Dios, desciende de la cruz.
texts.mat.27.41: De esta manera también los príncipes de los sacerdotes escarneciendo, con los escribas, y los Fariseos, y los ancianos, decían:
texts.mat.27.42: A otros salvó, a sí no se puede salvar. Si es el rey de Israel, descienda ahora de la cruz, y creeremos en él.
texts.mat.27.43: Confió en Dios: líbrele ahora, si le quiere; porque ha dicho: Soy Hijo de Dios.
texts.mat.27.44: Lo mismo también le zaherían los ladrones que estaban crucificados con él.
texts.mat.27.45: ¶ Y desde la hora de sexta fueron tinieblas sobre toda la tierra, hasta la hora de nona.
texts.mat.27.46: Y cerca de la hora de nona Jesús exclamó con gran voz, diciendo: Eli, Eli, ¿lamma sabachthani? esto es: Dios mío, Dios mío, ¿por qué me has desamparado?
texts.mat.27.47: Y algunos de los que estaban allí, oyéndo lo, decían: A Elías llama éste.
texts.mat.27.48: Y luego corriendo uno de ellos tomó una esponja, y la hinchió de vinagre, y poniéndo la en una caña, le daba para que bebiese.
texts.mat.27.49: Y los otros decían: Deja, veamos si vendrá Elías a librarle.
texts.mat.27.50: Mas Jesús habiendo otra vez exclamado con grande voz, dio el espíritu.
texts.mat.27.51: Y, he aquí, el velo del templo se rompió en dos, de alto a bajo; y la tierra se movió, y las piedras se hendieron;
texts.mat.27.52: Y los sepulcros se abrieron; y muchos cuerpos de santos, que habían dormido, se levantaron.
texts.mat.27.53: Y salidos de los sepulcros, después de su resurrección, vinieron a la santa ciudad, y aparecieron a muchos.
texts.mat.27.54: Y el centurión, y los que estaban con él guardando a Jesús, visto el terremoto, y las cosas que habían sido hechas, temieron en gran manera, diciendo: Verdaderamente Hijo de Dios era éste.
texts.mat.27.55: Y estaban allí muchas mujeres mirando de lejos, las cuales habían seguido de Galilea a Jesús, sirviéndole:
texts.mat.27.56: Entre las cuales era María Magdalena, y María madre de Santiago y de Joses, y la madre de los hijos de Zebedeo.
texts.mat.27.57: ¶ Y como fue la tarde del día, vino un hombre rico de Arimatea, llamado José, el cual también era discípulo de Jesús.
texts.mat.27.58: Este llegó a Pilato, y pidió el cuerpo de Jesús. Entonces Pilato mandó que el cuerpo se le diese.
texts.mat.27.59: Y tomando José el cuerpo, lo envolvió en una sábana limpia,
texts.mat.27.60: Y lo puso en un sepulcro suyo nuevo, que había labrado en la roca; y revuelta una grande piedra a la puerta del sepulcro, se fue.
texts.mat.27.61: Y estaban allí María Magdalena, y la otra María, sentadas delante del sepulcro.
texts.mat.27.62: Y el siguiente día, que era el día después de la preparación, se juntaron los príncipes de los sacerdotes y los Fariseos a Pilato,
texts.mat.27.63: Diciendo: Señor, nos acordamos que aquel engañador dijo, viviendo aun: Después del tercero día resucitaré.
texts.mat.27.64: Manda, pues, asegurar el sepulcro hasta el día tercero; porque no vengan sus discípulos de noche, y le hurten, y digan al pueblo: Resucitó de los muertos; y será el postrer error peor que el primero.
texts.mat.27.65: Díceles Pilato: La guardia tenéis: id, asegurád lo como sabéis.
texts.mat.27.66: Y yendo ellos, aseguraron el sepulcro con la guardia, sellando la piedra.
texts.mat.28.1: En el fin del sábado, así como iba amaneciendo el primer día de la semana, vino María Magdalena, y la otra María, a ver el sepulcro.
texts.mat.28.2: Y, he aquí, fue hecho un gran terremoto; porque el ángel del Señor descendiendo del cielo y llegando, había revuelto la piedra de la puerta del sepulcro, y estaba sentado sobre ella.
texts.mat.28.3: Y su aspecto era como un relámpago; y su vestido blanco como la nieve.
texts.mat.28.4: Y del miedo de él los guardas temblaron, y fueron vueltos como muertos.
texts.mat.28.5: Y respondiendo el ángel, dijo a las mujeres: No temáis vosotras; porque yo sé que buscáis a Jesús, el que fue crucificado.
texts.mat.28.6: No está aquí; porque ha resucitado, como dijo. Veníd, ved el lugar donde fue puesto el Señor;
texts.mat.28.7: Y presto id, decíd a sus discípulos, que ha resucitado de los muertos; y, he aquí, os espera en Galilea: allí le veréis: he aquí, os lo he dicho.
texts.mat.28.8: Entonces ellas saliendo del sepulcro con temor y gran gozo, fueron corriendo a dar las nuevas a sus discípulos. Y yendo a dar las nuevas a sus discípulos,
texts.mat.28.9: He aquí, Jesús les sale al encuentro, diciendo: Tengáis gozo. Y ellas se llegaron, y trabaron de sus pies, y le adoraron.
texts.mat.28.10: Entonces Jesús les dice: No temáis, id, dad las nuevas a mis hermanos, para que vayan a Galilea; y allá me verán.
texts.mat.28.11: ¶ Y yendo ellas, he aquí, unos de la guardia vinieron a la ciudad, y dieron aviso a los príncipes de los sacerdotes de todas las cosas que habían acontecido.
texts.mat.28.12: Y juntados con los ancianos, habido consejo, dieron mucho dinero a los soldados,
texts.mat.28.13: Diciendo: Decíd: Sus discípulos vinieron de noche, y le hurtaron, durmiendo nosotros.
texts.mat.28.14: Y si esto fuere oído del presidente, nosotros le persuadiremos, y os haremos seguros.
texts.mat.28.15: Y ellos, tomado el dinero, hicieron como estaban instruidos; y este dicho ha sido divulgado entre los Judíos hasta el día de hoy.
texts.mat.28.16: ¶ Mas los once discípulos se fueron a Galilea, al monte, donde Jesús les había ordenado.
texts.mat.28.17: Y como le vieron, le adoraron; mas algunos dudaban.
texts.mat.28.18: Y llegando Jesús, les habló, diciendo: Toda potestad me es dada en el cielo y en la tierra.
texts.mat.28.19: Por tanto id, enseñád a todas las naciones, bautizándoles en el nombre del Padre, y del Hijo, y del Espíritu Santo:
texts.mat.28.20: Enseñándoles que guarden todas las cosas que os he mandado; y, he aquí, yo estoy con vosotros todos los días, hasta el fin del siglo. Amén.

texts.mat.1.1: The Lineage Roll of Jesus Christ,—Son of David, Son of Abraham.
texts.mat.1.2: Abraham begat Isaac, and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob, begat Judah and his brethren;
texts.mat.1.3: And Judah begat Perez and Zarah of Tamah, and Perez begat Hezron, and Hezron begat Ram;
texts.mat.1.4: And Ram begat Amminadab, and Amminadab begat Nashon, and Nashon begat Salmon;
texts.mat.1.5: And Salmon begat Boaz of Rahab, and Boaz begat Obed of Ruth, and Obed begat Jesse;
texts.mat.1.6: And Jesse begat David the King. And David begat Solomon of her [that had been the wife] of Uriah;
texts.mat.1.7: And Solomon begat Rehoboam, and Rehoboam begat Abijah, and Abijah begat Asa;
texts.mat.1.8: And Asa begat Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat begat Joram, and Joram begat Uzziah;
texts.mat.1.9: And Uzziah begat Jotham, and Jotham begat Ahaz, and Ahaz begat Hezekiah:
texts.mat.1.10: And Hezekiah begat Manasseh, and Manasseh begat Amon, and Amon begat Josiah;
texts.mat.1.11: And Josiah begat Jechoniah, and his brethren,—upon the removal to Babylon.
texts.mat.1.12: And, after the removal to Babylon, Jechoniah begat Shealtiel, and Shealtiel begat Zerubbabel;
texts.mat.1.13: And Zerubbabel begat Abiud, and Abiud begat Eliakim, and Eliakim begat Azor;
texts.mat.1.14: And Azor begat Sadoc, and Sadoc begat Achim, and Achim begat Eliud;
texts.mat.1.15: And Eliud begat Eleazar, and Eleazar begat Matthan, and Matthan begat Jacob;—
texts.mat.1.16: And Jacob begat Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus,—who is called Christ.
texts.mat.1.17: So then, all the generations from Abraham unto David, are, fourteen, generations, and, from David unto the removal to Babylon, fourteen, generations; and, from the removal to Babylon unto the Christ, fourteen, generations.
texts.mat.1.18: Now the birth, of [Jesus] Christ, was, thus: His mother Mary having been betrothed to Joseph,—before they came together, she was found with child by [the] Holy Spirit.
texts.mat.1.19: Moreover, Joseph her husband, being, righteous, and yet unwilling to expose her,—intended, privately, to divorce her.
texts.mat.1.20: But, when, these things, he had pondered, lo! a messenger of the Lord, by dream, appeared to him, saying,—Joseph, son of David! do not fear to take unto thee Mary thy wife, for, that which, in her, hath been begotten, is of [the], Holy, Spirit.
texts.mat.1.21: Moreover she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name Jesus,—for, he, will save his people from their sins.
texts.mat.1.22: But, all this, hath come to pass, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord, through the prophet, saying:
texts.mat.1.23: Lo! a Virgin, shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son,—and they shall call his name Emmanuel; which is, being translated, God with us.
texts.mat.1.24: And Joseph, awaking, from his sleep, did as the messenger of the Lord directed him,—and took unto him his wife;
texts.mat.1.25: and knew her not, until she had brought forth a son,—and he called his name Jesus.
texts.mat.2.1: Now, when, Jesus, was born in Bethlehem of Judaea, in the days of Herod the king, lo! wise men from eastern parts, came into Jerusalem:
texts.mat.2.2: saying—Where is he that hath been born king of the Jews? for we saw his star in the east, and have come to bow down to him.
texts.mat.2.3: But, when King Herod heard, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him;
texts.mat.2.4: and, assembling all the high-priests and scribes of the people, he was enquiring of them—Where is, the Christ, to be born?
texts.mat.2.5: And, they, said to him, In Bethlehem of Judaea,—for, so, is it written through the prophet:
texts.mat.2.6: And, thou, Bethlehem, land of Judah, by no means least, art thou, among the governors of Judah,—For, out of thee, shall one come forth to govern, Who shall shepherd my people Israel.
texts.mat.2.7: Then Herod, privately, calling the wise men, ascertained from them the time of the appearing star;
texts.mat.2.8: and sending them to Bethlehem, said—Go search out accurately concerning the child,—and, as soon as ye find it, bring report unto me, that, I also, may come and bow myself down to it.
texts.mat.2.9: Now, they, hearing the king, went, and lo! the star which they had seen in the east, was going before them, until it went and stood over where the child was;
texts.mat.2.10: and, seeing the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy;
texts.mat.2.11: and, coming into the house, they saw the child, with Mary its mother,—and, falling down, prostrated themselves unto it, and, opening their treasures, offered unto it gifts—gold and frankincense and myrrh;
texts.mat.2.12: and, being instructed by dream, not to return unto Herod, by another way, retired they unto their own country.
texts.mat.2.13: Now, when they had retired, lo! a messenger of the Lord, appeareth by dream unto Joseph, saying, Arise, take unto thee the child and its mother, and flee into Egypt, and be there, until I tell thee,—for Herod is about to seek the child, to destroy it.
texts.mat.2.14: And, he, arising, took unto him the child and its mother, by night, and retired into Egypt;
texts.mat.2.15: and was there, until the death of Herod,—that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt, called I my son.
texts.mat.2.16: Then Herod, seeing that he had been mocked by the wise men, was exceedingly enraged,—and sent and slew all the male children that were in Bethlehem, and in all its bounds, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had ascertained from the wise men.
texts.mat.2.17: Then was fulfilled, that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying:
texts.mat.2.18: A voice, in Ramah, was heard, weeping and great mourning,—Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted,—because they are not.
texts.mat.2.19: But, when Herod was, dead, lo! a messenger of the Lord, appeareth by dream unto Joseph in Egypt;
texts.mat.2.20: saying—Arise! and take unto thee the child and its mother, and be journeying into the land of Israel,—for they are dead, who were seeking the life of the child.
texts.mat.2.21: And, he, arising, took unto him the child and its mother, and entered into the land of Israel.
texts.mat.2.22: Hearing, however, that, Archelaus, was reigning over Judaea instead of his father Herod, he was afraid, thither, to go,—and so, being instructed by dream, he retired into the parts of Galilee;
texts.mat.2.23: and came and fixed his dwelling in a city called Nazareth,—that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophets—A Nazarene, shall he be called.
texts.mat.3.1: Now, in those days, came John the Immerser, proclaiming in the wilderness of Judaea;
texts.mat.3.2: saying, Repent ye,—for the kingdom of the heavens hath drawn near.
texts.mat.3.3: For, this, is he who was spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying, A voice, of one crying aloud! In the wilderness, prepare ye the way of the Lord, straight, be making his paths.
texts.mat.3.4: But John, himself, had his raiment of camel’s hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins,—while, his food, was locusts and wild honey.
texts.mat.3.5: Then, were going forth unto him—Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the country round about the Jordan:
texts.mat.3.6: and were being immersed in the Jordan river, by him, openly confessing their sins.
texts.mat.3.7: But, seeing, many of the Pharisees and Sadducees, coming unto his immersion, he said to them,—Broods of vipers! who suggested to you, to be fleeing from the coming wrath?
texts.mat.3.8: Bring forth, therefore, fruit worthy of repentance;
texts.mat.3.9: and think not to be saying within yourselves,—As our father, we have, Abraham; for, I say unto you, that God is able, out of these stones, to raise up children unto Abraham.
texts.mat.3.10: Already also, the axe, unto the root of the trees, is being laid,—every tree, therefore, not bringing forth good fruit, is to be hewn down, and, into fire, to be cast.
texts.mat.3.11: I, indeed, am immersing you, in water, unto repentance,—but, he who, after me, cometh is, mightier than I, whose, sandals, I am not worthy to bear, he, will immerse you, in Holy Spirit and fire:
texts.mat.3.12: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will clear out his threshing-floor,—and will gather his wheat into the granary, but, the chaff, will he burn up with fire unquenchable.
texts.mat.3.13: Then, cometh Jesus, from Galilee to the Jordan, unto John,—to be immersed by him.
texts.mat.3.14: But, he, would have hindered him, saying—I, have, need, by thee, to be immersed,—and dost, thou, come unto me?
texts.mat.3.15: But Jesus answering, said unto him, Suffer [me] even now,—for, thus, it becometh us, to fulfil, all righteousness; then, he suffered him.
texts.mat.3.16: And Jesus, having been immersed, straightway, went up from the water,—and lo! the heavens were opened and he saw the Spirit of God, descending like a dove coming upon him;
texts.mat.3.17: and lo! a voice out of the heavens,—saying, This, is my Son, the Beloved, in whom I delight.
texts.mat.4.1: Then, Jesus was led up into the wilderness, by the Spirit, to be tempted by the adversary;
texts.mat.4.2: and, fasting forty days and forty nights,—afterwards, he hungered.
texts.mat.4.3: And, coming near, the tempter said to him,—If thou art God’s, Son, speak! that, these stones, may become, loaves.
texts.mat.4.4: But, he, answering, said, It is written,—Not on bread alone, shall man live, but on every declaration coming forth through the mouth of God.
texts.mat.4.5: Then, the adversary taketh him with him, unto the holy city,—and he set him upon the pinnacle of the temple;
texts.mat.4.6: and saith to him—If thou art God’s, Son, cast thyself down,—for it is written, To his messengers, will he give charge concerning thee; and, on hands, will they bear thee up, lest once thou strike, against a stone, thy foot.
texts.mat.4.7: Jesus said to him, Again, it is written,—Thou shalt not put to the test, the Lord thy God.
texts.mat.4.8: Again, the adversary taketh him with him, into an exceeding high mountain,—and pointeth out to him all the kingdoms of the world, and their glory;
texts.mat.4.9: and said to him, All these things, will I give thee,—if thou wilt fall down and worship me.
texts.mat.4.10: Then saith Jesus unto him, Withdraw, Satan! for it is written,—The Lord thy God, shalt thou worship, and, to him alone, render divine service.
texts.mat.4.11: Then, the adversary leaveth him,—and lo! messengers came near, and began ministering unto him.
texts.mat.4.12: And, hearing that, John, had been delivered up, he retired into Galilee;
texts.mat.4.13: and, forsaking Nazareth, he came and fixed his dwelling in Capernaum, which was by the lake,—within the bounds of Zebulun and Naphtali:
texts.mat.4.14: that it might be fulfilled, which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying:
texts.mat.4.15: Land of Zebulun, and land of Naphtali, the lake-way across the Jordan,—Galilee of the nations,
texts.mat.4.16: The people that was sitting in darkness, a great light, beheld,—and, on them who were sitting in land and shade of death, Light rose on them.
texts.mat.4.17: From that time, began Jesus to be making proclamation, and saying,—Repent ye, for the kingdom of the heavens hath drawn near.
texts.mat.4.18: And, walking round beside the sea of Galilee, he saw two brethren—Simon who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother,—casting a large fishing-net into the sea, for they were fishers;
texts.mat.4.19: and he saith unto them, Come after me,—and I will make you fishers, of men.
texts.mat.4.20: And, they, straightway, leaving the nets, followed him.
texts.mat.4.21: And, going forward from thence, he saw other two brethren—James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother—in the boat with Zebedee their father, putting in order their nets,—and he called them.
texts.mat.4.22: And, they, straightway, leaving the boat and their father, followed him.
texts.mat.4.23: And Jesus was going round throughout all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and proclaiming the glad-message of the kingdom,—and curing every disease, and every infirmity, among the people.
texts.mat.4.24: And forth went the report of him into all Syria; and they brought unto him all who were sick, with divers diseases and tortures, distressed, demonized and lunatic and paralyzed,—and he cured them.
texts.mat.4.25: And there followed him large multitudes—from Galilee, and Decapolis, and Jerusalem, and Judaea, and across the Jordan.
texts.mat.5.1: But, seeing the multitudes, he went up into a mountain,—and, when he had taken a seat, his disciples came unto him;
texts.mat.5.2: and, opening his mouth, he began teaching them, saying:—
texts.mat.5.3: Happy, the destitute, in spirit; for, theirs, is the kingdom of the heavens;
texts.mat.5.4: Happy, they who mourn; for, they, shall be comforted:
texts.mat.5.5: Happy, the meek; for, they, shall inherit the earth:
texts.mat.5.6: Happy, they who hunger and thirst for righteousness; for, they, shall be filled:
texts.mat.5.7: Happy, the merciful; for, they, shall receive mercy:
texts.mat.5.8: Happy, the pure, in heart; for, they, shall, see God:
texts.mat.5.9: Happy, the peacemakers; for, they, shall be, called sons of God:
texts.mat.5.10: Happy, they who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake; for, theirs, is the kingdom of the heavens.
texts.mat.5.11: Happy, are ye, whensoever they may reproach you and persecute you, and say every evil thing against you, falsely, for my sake:
texts.mat.5.12: Rejoice and exult, because, your reward, is great in the heavens; for, so, persecuted they the prophets who were before you.
texts.mat.5.13: Ye, are the salt of the earth; but, if the salt become tasteless, wherewith shall it be salted? it is good, for nothing, any more, save, being cast out, to be trampled on by men.
texts.mat.5.14: Ye, are the light of the world: it is impossible for a city to be hid, on the top of a mountain, lying.
texts.mat.5.15: Neither light they a lamp, and place it under the measure; but upon the lampstand, and it giveth light to all that are in the house.
texts.mat.5.16: In like manner, let your light shine before men,—that they may see your good works,—and glorify your Father who is in the heavens.
texts.mat.5.17: Do not think, that I came to pull down the law, or the prophets,—I came not to pull down, but to fulfil.
texts.mat.5.18: For, verily, I say unto you, until the heaven and the earth shall pass away, one least letter, or one point, may in nowise pass away from the law, till all be accomplished.
texts.mat.5.19: Whosoever, therefore, shall relax one of these commandments, the least, and teach men so, shall be called, least, in the kingdom of the heavens; but, whosoever shall do and teach, the same, shall be called, great, in the kingdom of the heavens.
texts.mat.5.20: For I say unto you, that, unless your righteousness exceed that of the Scribes and Pharisees, in nowise, may ye enter into the kingdom of the heavens.
texts.mat.5.21: Ye have heard, that it was said, to them of olden time,—Thou shalt not commit murder, and, whosoever shall commit murder, shall be, liable, to judgment.
texts.mat.5.22: But, I, say unto you, that, every one who is angry with his brother, shall be, liable, to judgment,—and, whosoever shall say to his brother, Worthless one!, shall be, liable, to the high council; and, whosoever shall say, Rebel!, shall be, liable, unto the fiery gehenna.
texts.mat.5.23: If, therefore, thou be bearing thy gift towards the altar, and, there, shouldst remember that, thy brother, hath aught against thee,
texts.mat.5.24: leave, there, thy gift before the altar, and withdraw,—first, be reconciled unto thy brother, and, then, coming, be offering thy gift.
texts.mat.5.25: Be making agreement with thine adversary, quickly, while thou art with him, in the way,—lest once thine adversary deliver thee up unto the judge, and the judge, unto the officer, and, into prison, thou be cast.
texts.mat.5.26: Verily, I say unto thee, In nowise, mayest thou come out from thence, until thou pay the last halfpenny.
texts.mat.5.27: Ye have heard, that it was said, Thou shalt not commit adultery:
texts.mat.5.28: But, I, say unto you, that, Every one who looketh on a woman so as to covet her, already, hath committed adultery with her, in his heart.
texts.mat.5.29: And, if, thy right eye, is causing thee to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from thee,—for it profiteth thee, that, one of thy members, should perish, and not, thy whole body, be cast into gehenna.
texts.mat.5.30: And, if, thy right hand, is causing thee to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from thee,—for it profiteth thee, that, one of thy members, should perish, and not, thy whole body, into gehenna, depart.
texts.mat.5.31: It was said, moreover, Whosoever shall divorce his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement;
texts.mat.5.32: But, I, say unto you, that, Everyone who divorceth his wife—saving for unfaithfulness, causeth her to be made an adulteress,— [and, whosoever shall marry a divorced woman, committeth adultery].
texts.mat.5.33: Again, ye have heard that it was said, to them of olden time, Thou shalt not swear falsely,—but shalt render unto the Lord, thine oaths.
texts.mat.5.34: But, I, tell you—not to swear, at all: Neither by heaven, because it is the, throne of God,—
texts.mat.5.35: Nor by the earth, because it is his, footstool; nor by Jerusalem, because, it is the, city, of the Great King;
texts.mat.5.36: Nor, by thine own head, mayest thou swear, because thou art not able to make, one hair, white or black.
texts.mat.5.37: But let your word be, Yea, yea,—Nay, nay; and, what goeth beyond these, is, of evil.
texts.mat.5.38: Ye have heard, that it was said,—Eye for eye, and tooth for tooth.
texts.mat.5.39: But, I, tell you, not to resist evil,—Nay, whoever is smiting thee on the right cheek, turn to him, the other also;
texts.mat.5.40: And, him who is desiring thee to be judged, and to take, thy tunic, let him have, thy mantle also.
texts.mat.5.41: And, whoever shall impress thee one mile, go with him two:
texts.mat.5.42: To him who is asking thee, give; and, him who is desiring from thee to borrow, do not thou turn away.
texts.mat.5.43: Ye have heard, that it was said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy.
texts.mat.5.44: But, I, say unto you, Be loving your enemies, and praying for them who are persecuting you:
texts.mat.5.45: That ye may become sons of your Father who is in the heavens: because, his sun, he maketh arise on evil and good, and sendeth rain, on just and unjust.
texts.mat.5.46: For, if ye love them that love you, what reward have ye? are not, even the tax-collectors, the same thing, doing?
texts.mat.5.47: And, if ye salute your brethren only, what, more than common, are ye doing? are not, even the nations, the same thing, doing?
texts.mat.5.48: Ye, therefore, shall become, perfect: as, your heavenly Father, is perfect.
texts.mat.6.1: [But] take heed, that ye do not, your righteousness, before men, to be gazed at by them,—otherwise at least, reward, have ye none, with your Father who is in the heavens.
texts.mat.6.2: When, therefore, thou mayest be doing an alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, just as, the hypocrites, do in the synagogues and in the streets—that they may be glorified by men,—Verily, I say unto you, they are getting back their reward.
texts.mat.6.3: But, thou, when doing an alms, let not, thy left hand, know what thy right hand is doing;
texts.mat.6.4: that thine alms may be in secret,—and, thy Father, who seeth in secret, will give it back to thee.
texts.mat.6.5: And, when ye may be praying, ye shall not be as the hypocrites, because they love, in the synagogues, and at the corners of the broad ways, to take their stand and pray, that they may shine before men; Verily, I say unto you, they are getting back their reward.
texts.mat.6.6: But, thou, when thou wouldest pray, enter into thy closet, and, fastening thy door, pray unto thy Father who is in secret,—and, thy Father who seeth in secret, will reward thee.
texts.mat.6.7: And, being at prayer, use not vain repetitions, just like the nations,—for they think, that, in their much speaking, they shall be hoard;
texts.mat.6.8: do not, therefore, make yourselves like them, for [God] your Father knoweth of what things ye have, need, before ye ask him.
texts.mat.6.9: Thus, therefore pray, ye: Our Father, who art in the heavens,—Hallowed be thy name,
texts.mat.6.10: Come may thy kingdom,—Accomplished be thy will, as in heaven, also on earth:
texts.mat.6.11: Our needful bread, give us, this day;
texts.mat.6.12: And forgive us our debts, as, we also, have forgiven our debtors;
texts.mat.6.13: And bring us not into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one.
texts.mat.6.14: For, if ye forgive men their faults, Your Father who is in the heavens, will forgive, even you;
texts.mat.6.15: But, if ye forgive not men [their faults], neither will your Father forgive, your faults.
texts.mat.6.16: And, when ye may he fasting, become not ye, as the hypocrites, of sullen countenance,—for they darken their looks, that they may appear, unto men, to be fasting: Verily, I say unto you, they are getting back their reward.
texts.mat.6.17: But, when, thou, art fasting, anoint thy head, and, thy face, wash,—
texts.mat.6.18: that thou do not appear, unto men, to be fasting, but to thy Father who is in secret,—and, thy Father who seeth in secret, will reward thee.
texts.mat.6.19: Be not laying up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, where, moth and rust, do tarnish, and where, thieves, dig through and steal;
texts.mat.6.20: but be laying up or yourselves treasures in heaven, where, neither moth nor rust, doth tarnish, and where, thieves, dig not through nor steal:
texts.mat.6.21: for, where, thy treasure, is, there, will be, thy heart [also].
texts.mat.6.22: The lamp of the body, is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body, shall be, lighted up;
texts.mat.6.23: But, if thine eye be, evil, thy whole body, shall be, in the dark;—if therefore, the light which is in thee, is, darkness, the darkness, how great!
texts.mat.6.24: No one, unto two masters, can be in service; for either, the one, he will hate, and, the other,love, or, one, he will hold to, and, the other, despise: Ye cannot be in service, unto God, and, unto Riches.
texts.mat.6.25: For this cause, I say unto you: Be not anxious for your life, what ye shall eat [or what ye shall drink],—or for your body, what ye shall put on: Is not, the life, more than, the food? And, the body, than, the raiment?
texts.mat.6.26: Observe intently, the birds of the heaven,—that they neither sow, nor reap, nor gather into barns, and yet, your heavenly Father, feedeth, them: Are no, ye, much better than, they?
texts.mat.6.27: But who from among you, being anxious, can add to his stature one cubit?
texts.mat.6.28: And, about clothing, why are ye anxious? Consider well the lilies of the field, how they grow,—they toil not neither do they spin;
texts.mat.6.29: And yet, I say unto you, not even Solomon, in all his glory, was arrayed like, one of these!
texts.mat.6.30: Now, if the grass of the field—which to-day, is, and, to-morrow, into an oven, is cast—God thus adorneth, not much rather, you, little of faith?
texts.mat.6.31: Do not then be anxious saying, What shall we eat? or What shall we drink? or Wherewithal shall we be arrayed?
texts.mat.6.32: For, all these things, the nations, seek after,—for your heavenly Father, knoweth, that ye are needing, all these things.
texts.mat.6.33: But be seeking first, the kingdom and its righteousness,—and, all these things, shall be added unto you.
texts.mat.6.34: Do not, then, be anxious for the morrow; for the morrow, will be anxious, for itself: Sufficient for the day, is the evil thereof.
texts.mat.7.1: Judge not, that ye be not judged;—
texts.mat.7.2: For, with what judgment ye judge, shall ye be judged,—and, with what measure ye mete, shall it be measured unto you.
texts.mat.7.3: Why, moreover, beholdest thou the mote, in the eye of thy brother,—while, the beam in thine own eye, thou dost not consider?
texts.mat.7.4: Or how wilt thou say unto thy brother, Let me cast the mote out of thine eye,—when lo! a beam, is in thine own eye?
texts.mat.7.5: Hypocrite! cast first, out of thine own eye, the beam,—and, then, shalt thou see clearly to cast the mote, out of the eye of thy brother.
texts.mat.7.6: Do not give what is holy unto dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine,—lest once they trample, them, down with their feet, and, turning, tear, you.
texts.mat.7.7: Be asking, and it shall be given you, Be seeking, and ye shall find,—Be knocking, and it shall be opened unto you.
texts.mat.7.8: For, whosoever asketh, receiveth, and, he that seeketh, findeth,—and, to him that knocketh, shall it be opened.
texts.mat.7.9: Or what man, from among yourselves, whom his son shall ask for a loaf,—a stone, will give him?
texts.mat.7.10: Or, a fish also, shall ask,—a serpent, will give him?
texts.mat.7.11: If then, ye, being, evil, know how, good gifts, to be giving unto your children, how much more, will, your Father who is in the heavens, give good things to them that ask, him?
texts.mat.7.12: Whatsoever things, therefore, ye would, that men be doing unto you, so, be, ye also, doing, unto them,—for, this, is the law and the prophets.
texts.mat.7.13: Enter ye in at, the narrow gate; because broad and roomy is the way that leadeth unto destruction,—and, many, are they who enter thereby:
texts.mat.7.14: Because, narrow, is the gate, and, confined, the way, that leadeth unto life,—and, few, are they who find, it.
texts.mat.7.15: Beware of false prophets, who come unto you in clothing of sheep,—while, within, they are ravening wolves.
texts.mat.7.16: By their fruits, shall ye find, them, out,—unless perhaps men gather—from thorns, grapes! or, from thistles, figs!
texts.mat.7.17: So, every good tree, fine fruit, produceth,—whereas, the worthless tree, evil fruit, produceth:
texts.mat.7.18: It is, impossible, for a, good tree, to be bearing, evil fruit, neither doth, a worthless tree, produce, fine fruit.
texts.mat.7.19: Every tree that beareth not fine fruit, is hewn down, and, into fire, is cast.
texts.mat.7.20: After all then, by their fruits, shall ye find, them, out.
texts.mat.7.21: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord! Lord! shall enter into the kingdom of the heavens,—but he that doeth the will of my Father who is in the heavens.
texts.mat.7.22: Many, will say unto me, in, that, day, Lord! Lord! did we not, in thy name, prophesy, and, in thy name, cast, demons, out,—and, in thy name, many works of power, perform?
texts.mat.7.23: And, then, will I confess unto them, Never, have I acknowledged you,—Depart from me, ye workers of lawlessness!
texts.mat.7.24: Every one, therefore, who heareth [these] my words, and doeth them, shall be likened to a prudent man, who built his house upon the rock;
texts.mat.7.25: And the rain descended, and the streams came, and the winds blew, and rushed against that house, and it fell not; for it had been founded upon the rock.
texts.mat.7.26: And every one who heareth these my words, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, who built his house upon the sand;
texts.mat.7.27: And the rain descended, and the streams came, and the winds blew, and dashed against that house, and it fell; and, the fall thereof, was, great.
texts.mat.7.28: And it came to pass, when Jesus ended these words, with astonishment were the multitudes being struck at his teaching;
texts.mat.7.29: for he was teaching them as one having, authority, and not as their Scribes.
texts.mat.8.1: And when he came down from the mountain, there followed him large multitudes.
texts.mat.8.2: And lo! a leper, coming near, began to bow down to him saying,—Lord! if thou be willing, thou canst cleanse me.
texts.mat.8.3: And, stretching forth the hand, he touched him, saying,—I am willing, be cleansed! And, straightway, cleansed was his leprosy.
texts.mat.8.4: And Jesus saith unto him, Mind! tell, no one,—but withdraw, thyself, shew to the priest, and offer the gift which Moses directed, for a witness unto them.
texts.mat.8.5: And, when he entered into Capernaum, there came near unto him a centurion, beseeching him,
texts.mat.8.6: and saying, Lord! my servant, is laid prostrate in the house, a paralytic, fearfully tortured.
texts.mat.8.7: He saith unto him, I, will come and cure him.
texts.mat.8.8: But the centurion, answering, said, Lord! I am of no consideration, that, under my roof, thou shouldest enter,—but, only say with a word, and healed shall be my servant.
texts.mat.8.9: For, I also, am a man [set] under authority, having under myself, soldiers,—and I say to this one, Go! and he goeth, and to another, Come! and he cometh, and, to my servant, Do this! and he doeth it.
texts.mat.8.10: Now Jesus, hearing, marveled, and said to them that followed,—Verily, I say unto you, With no one in Israel, such faith as this, have I found.
texts.mat.8.11: But I say unto you, Many from east and west, will have come, and shall recline with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, in the kingdom of the heavens;
texts.mat.8.12: Whereas, the sons of the kingdom, shall be cast forth into the darkness outside,—There, will be wailing and gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.8.13: And Jesus said unto the centurion, Withdraw! and, as thou hast believed, be it done for thee. And healed was the servant in that hour.
texts.mat.8.14: And Jesus, coming into the house of Peter, saw his mother-in-law laid prostrate and in a fever,
texts.mat.8.15: and he touched her hand, and the fever left her,—and she arose, and began ministering unto him.
texts.mat.8.16: But, when, evening, came, they brought unto him many demonized,—and he cast out the spirits with a word, and, all who were sick, he cured:
texts.mat.8.17: that it might be fulfilled, which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,—Himself, our weaknesses, took, and, diseases, bare.
texts.mat.8.18: Now Jesus, seeing a multitude about him, gave orders to depart unto the other side.
texts.mat.8.19: And a certain scribe, coming near, said unto him,—Teacher; I will follow thee, whithersoever Thou goest.
texts.mat.8.20: And Jesus saith unto him: The foxes, have, dens, and, the birds of the heavens, nests,—but, the Son of Man, hath not where, his head he may recline.
texts.mat.8.21: And, another of the disciples, saith unto him,—Lord! suffer me, first, to depart, and bury my father.
texts.mat.8.22: But, Jesus, saith unto him,—Be following me, and leave, the dead, to bury, their own dead.
texts.mat.8.23: And, when he, entered, into a boat, his disciples followed him.
texts.mat.8.24: And lo! a great squall, arose in the sea, so that, the boat, was being covered, by the waves,—but, he, was sleeping.
texts.mat.8.25: And, coming near, they aroused him, saying, Master! save, we perish!
texts.mat.8.26: And he saith unto them, Why, are ye, fearful, little of faith? Then, aroused, he rebuked the winds and the sea,—and it became a great calm.
texts.mat.8.27: But, the men, marveled, saying, Whence is this one,—that, both the winds and the sea, unto him, give ear?
texts.mat.8.28: And, when he, came, unto the other side, into the country of the Gadarenes, there met him, two men demonized, out of the tombs, coming forth,—fierce exceedingly, so that no one could pass that way;
texts.mat.8.29: and lo! they cried aloud, saying, What have we in common with thee, O Son of God? Hast thou come hither, before the right time, to torment us?
texts.mat.8.30: Now there was, far from them, a herd of many swine, feeding;
texts.mat.8.31: and, the demons, began to beseech him, saying, If thou dost cast us out, send us away, into the herd of swine.
texts.mat.8.32: And he said unto them, Withdraw! So, they, going out, departed into the swine,—and lo! all the herd rushed down the cliff, into the sea, and died in the waters.
texts.mat.8.33: And, they who were feeding them, fled,—and, departing into the city, reported all things, and what concerned them who had been demonized.
texts.mat.8.34: And lo! all the city, came out to meet Jesus,—and, seeing him, they besought that he would pass on from their bounds.
texts.mat.9.1: And, entering into a boat, he crossed over, and came into his own city.
texts.mat.9.2: And lo! they were bringing unto him a paralytic, on a couch, laid prostrate; and Jesus, seeing, their faith, said to the paralytic,—Take courage! child, forgiven are thy sins.
texts.mat.9.3: And lo! certain of the scribes, said within themselves,—This man, speaketh profanely!
texts.mat.9.4: And Jesus, knowing, their inward thoughts, said,—To what end are ye cherishing evil thoughts within your hearts?
texts.mat.9.5: For which is easier—To say, Forgiven are thy sins,—or to say, Rise and be walking!
texts.mat.9.6: But, that ye may know, that the Son of Man hath, authority, upon the earth, to be forgiving sins, then, saith he to the paralytic,—Rise! take up thy couch, and withdraw unto thy house.
texts.mat.9.7: And, rising, he departed unto his house.
texts.mat.9.8: Now the multitudes, seeing, were struck with fear, and glorified the God who had given authority, such as this, unto men.
texts.mat.9.9: And Jesus, passing aside from thence, saw a man presiding over the tax-office, called, Matthew, and saith unto him,—Be following me. And, arising, he followed him.
texts.mat.9.10: And it came to pass, as he was reclining in the house, that lo! many tax-collectors and sinners, came, and were reclining together with Jesus and his disciples.
texts.mat.9.11: And, the Pharisees, observing it, began to say unto his disciples,—Wherefore, with tax-collectors and sinners, doth your Teacher eat?
texts.mat.9.12: And, he, hearing it, said,—No need have the strong, of a physician, but they who are sick.
texts.mat.9.13: But go ye, and learn what this meaneth,—Mercy, I desire, and not, sacrifice; For I came, not to call the righteous, but sinners.
texts.mat.9.14: Then come near unto him the disciples of John, saying,—Wherefore do, we, and the Pharisees, fast, whereas, thy disciples, fast not?
texts.mat.9.15: And Jesus said unto them,—Can, the sons of the bridechamber, mourn, so long as, the bridegroom, is, with them? But days will come, when the bridegroom, shall be taken from them, and, then, will they fast.
texts.mat.9.16: Howbeit, no one, layeth on a patch of unshrunk cloth, upon an old garment,—for the shrinking of it teareth away from the garment, and, a worse rent, is made.
texts.mat.9.17: Neither pour they new wine into old skins: otherwise at least, the skins are burst, and, the wine, runneth out, and, the skins, are spoiled,—but they pour new wine into unused skins, and, both, are together preserved.
texts.mat.9.18: While, these things, he was speaking unto them, lo! a [certain] ruler, came, and began bowing down to him, saying,—My daughter, just now died! But come, and lay thy hand upon, her, and she shall live.
texts.mat.9.19: And Jesus, arising, was following him, also his disciples.
texts.mat.9.20: And lo! a woman, having a flow of blood twelve years, coming near behind, touched the fringe of his mantle.
texts.mat.9.21: For she kept saying within herself,—If only I touch his mantle, I shall be made well!
texts.mat.9.22: And, Jesus, turning and seeing her, said,—Take courage! daughter, Thy faith, hath made thee well. And the woman was made well, from that hour.
texts.mat.9.23: And, Jesus, coming, into the house of the ruler, and seeing the flute-players and the multitude in confusion, was saying:
texts.mat.9.24: Give place! for the maiden died not, but is sleeping. And they began to deride him.
texts.mat.9.25: But, when the multitude had been put forth, he went in, and grasped her hand,—and the maiden arose.
texts.mat.9.26: And forth went this report, into the whole of that land.
texts.mat.9.27: And, as Jesus, was passing aside from thence, there followed him, two blind men, crying aloud and saying,—Have mercy on us, O Son of David!
texts.mat.9.28: And, when he entered the house, the blind men came unto him,—and Jesus saith unto them, Believe ye, that I can, do this? They say unto him, Yea, Lord!
texts.mat.9.29: Then touched he their eyes, saying, According to your faith, be it done unto you.
texts.mat.9.30: And their eyes were opened. And Jesus, sternly charged them, saying, Mind! let no one know!
texts.mat.9.31: They, however, going forth, made him known throughout the whole of that land.
texts.mat.9.32: And, as, they, were going forth, lo! there was brought to him, a dumb man, demonized.
texts.mat.9.33: And, the demon being cast out, the dumb man spoke; and the multitudes marvelled, saying,—Never, was it seen thus, in Israel.
texts.mat.9.34: [But, the Pharisees, beg to say, In the ruler of the demons, is he casting out the demons.]
texts.mat.9.35: And Jesus was going round all the cities and the villages, teaching in their synagogues, and proclaiming the glad-message of the kingdom,—and curing every disease, and every infirmity.
texts.mat.9.36: But, seeing the multitudes, he was moved with compassion concerning them, because they were torn and thrown down, like sheep hating no shepherd.
texts.mat.9.37: Then, saith he unto his disciples, The harvest, indeed, is great, but, the labourers, few;
texts.mat.9.38: Beg ye, therefore, of the Lord of the harvest,—That he would thrust forth labourers, into his harvest.
texts.mat.10.1: And, calling near his twelve disciples, he gave them authority over impure spirits,—so as to be casting them out, and curing every disease and every infirmity.
texts.mat.10.2: Now, the twelve apostles’ names, are these:—first Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother,—and James, the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother;
texts.mat.10.3: Philip, and Bartholomew,—Thomas, and Matthew, the tax-collector; James, the son of Alphaeus, and Thadaeus;
texts.mat.10.4: Simon, the zealot, and Judas Iscariot, who also delivered him up.
texts.mat.10.5: These twelve, Jesus sent forth, charging them, saying:—Into any way to the nations, do not depart,—and, into any city of Samaritans, do not enter;
texts.mat.10.6: But be going, rather, unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
texts.mat.10.7: And, as ye go, proclaim, saying, The kingdom of the heavens hath drawn near!
texts.mat.10.8: Be curing, the sick, raising, the dead,—cleansing, lepers, casting out, demons: freely, ye have, received, freely, give.
texts.mat.10.9: Ye may procure—neither gold, nor silver, nor copper, for your belts,—
texts.mat.10.10: neither satchel for journey, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor staff; for, worthy, is the labourer, of his maintenance.
texts.mat.10.11: And, into whatsoever city or village ye enter, search out who in it is, worthy, and, there, abide, till ye go forth.
texts.mat.10.12: And, as ye enter the house, salute it;
texts.mat.10.13: And, if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it, but, if it be not worthy, let your peace, unto you, return.
texts.mat.10.14: And, whosoever shall neither welcome you, nor hear your words, as ye go forth outside that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet:
texts.mat.10.15: Verily, I say unto you,—More tolerable, will it be, for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for, that, city!
texts.mat.10.16: Lo! I, send you forth as sheep amidst wolves; become ye therefore—prudent, as serpents, and simple, as doves.
texts.mat.10.17: But beware of men; for they will deliver you up into high-councils, and, in their synagogues, will they scourge you,—
texts.mat.10.18: And, before both governor and kings, shall ye be brought, for my sake—for a witness to them and the nations.
texts.mat.10.19: And, when they deliver you up, be not anxious how or what ye shall speak,—for it shall be given you in that hour what ye shall speak;
texts.mat.10.20: For it is not, ye, who are speaking, but, the Spirit of your Father, that is speaking in you.
texts.mat.10.21: And, brother, will deliver up, brother, unto death, and, father, child,—and, children, will rise up, against parents, and will put them to death.
texts.mat.10.22: And ye will be hated by all, because of my name,—but, he that endureth throughout, the same, shall be saved.
texts.mat.10.23: And, when they persecute you in this city, flee into another,—for, verily, I say unto you, in nowise shall ye finish the cities of Israel, till, he Son of Man, come.
texts.mat.10.24: A, disciple, is not above, the teacher, nor, a servant, above, his lord:
texts.mat.10.25: Sufficient for the disciple, that he become, as his teacher, and, the servant, as, his lord. If, the master of the house, Beelzebul, they called, how much more, the men of his house!
texts.mat.10.26: Then do not fear them,—for, nothing hath been covered, which shall not be, uncovered, and, hidden, which shall not be, made known.
texts.mat.10.27: What I am saying to you in the darkness, tell ye in the light,—and, what [whispered] into the ear ye are hearing, proclaim ye on the housetops.
texts.mat.10.28: And be not in fear, by reason of them that are killing the body,—and, the soul, are not able to kill. But fear, rather, him who is able, both soul and body, to destroy in gehenna!
texts.mat.10.29: Are not, two sparrows, for a farthing, sold? And, one from among them, shall not fall upon the ground, without your Father;
texts.mat.10.30: But, even the hairs of, your, head, have all been numbered.
texts.mat.10.31: Then be not in fear—than many sparrows, better are, ye!
texts.mat.10.32: Every one therefore who shall confess me before men, I also, will confess, him, before my Father who is in the heavens;
texts.mat.10.33: But, whoever shall deny me before men, I also, will deny, him, before my Father who is in the heavens.
texts.mat.10.34: Do not think, that I came to thrust peace upon the earth,—I came not to thrust, peace, but, a sword;
texts.mat.10.35: For I came to set at variance—a man, against, his father, and, a daughter, against, her mother, and, a bride, against, her mother-in-law;
texts.mat.10.36: And, a man foes, are, they of his own house.
texts.mat.10.37: He that loveth father or mother above me, is not, worthy, of me,—and, he that loveth son or daughter above me, is not, worthy, of me;
texts.mat.10.38: And, he that doth not take his cross and follow after me, is not, worthy, of me.
texts.mat.10.39: He that hath found his life, shall lose it,—and, he that hath lost his life, for my sake, shall find it.
texts.mat.10.40: He that giveth welcome unto you, unto me, giveth welcome, and, he that, unto me, giveth welcome, giveth welcome—unto him that sent me forth.
texts.mat.10.41: He that giveth welcome unto a prophet, in the name of a prophet, the reward of a prophet, shall receive; and, he that giveth welcome unto a righteous man, in the name of a righteous man, the reward of a righteous man, shall receive;—
texts.mat.10.42: And, whosoever shall give to drink—unto one of these little ones—a cup of cold water only, in the name of a disciple, Verily, I say unto you, in nowise, shall lose his reward!
texts.mat.11.1: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished giving instructions to his twelve disciples, he passed on from thence, to be teaching and proclaiming in their cities.
texts.mat.11.2: Now, John, hearing in the prison the works of the Christ, sending through his disciples,
texts.mat.11.3: said unto him, Art, thou, the coming one? or, a different one, are we to expect?
texts.mat.11.4: And, answering, Jesus said unto them—Go report unto John what ye do hear and see:—
texts.mat.11.5: The, blind, recover sight, and, the lame, walk, lepers, are cleansed, and, the deaf, hear,—and, the dead, are raised, and, the destitute, are told the joyful tidings;
texts.mat.11.6: And, happy, is he, whosoever shall not find cause of stumbling, in me.
texts.mat.11.7: But, as these were going their way, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes, concerning John,—What went ye forth into the wilderness to gaze at? A reed, by a wind, shaken?
texts.mat.11.8: But what went ye forth to see? A man, in soft clothing, arrayed? Lo! they who soft clothing do wear, are in the houses of kings.
texts.mat.11.9: But why went ye forth? A prophet, to see? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.
texts.mat.11.10: This, is he, concerning whom it is written,—Lo! I, send my messenger before thy face, who shall make ready thy way before thee!
texts.mat.11.11: Verily, I say unto you—There hath not arisen, among such as are born of women, a greater than John the Immerser,—yet, he that is less in the kingdom of the heavens, is, greater than he.
texts.mat.11.12: But, from the days of John the Immerser, until even now, the kingdom of the heavens, is being invaded, and, invaders, are, seizing upon it.
texts.mat.11.13: For, all the prophets and the law, until John, did prophesy;
texts.mat.11.14: And, if ye are willing to accept it, he, is Elijah—the one destined to come.
texts.mat.11.15: He that hath ears, let him hear!
texts.mat.11.16: But, unto what, shall I liken this generation? It is, like, unto children, sitting the market-places, who, calling unto the others,
texts.mat.11.17: say, We played the flute to you, and ye danced not,—we sang a lament, and ye beat not the breast.
texts.mat.11.18: For, John, came, neither eating nor drinking, and they say—A demon, he hath!
texts.mat.11.19: The Son of Man, came, eating and drinking, and they say, Lo! a gluttonous man and a wine-drinker! a friend of, tax-collectors, and sinners! And yet wisdom hath been justified by her works.
texts.mat.11.20: Then, began he to upbraid the cities, in which had been done his noblest mighty works; because they repented not:—
texts.mat.11.21: Alas for thee, Chorazin! Alas for thee, Bethsaida! Because, if, in Tyre and Zidon, had been done the works of power, which were done in you, of old, in sackcloth and ashes, had they repented.
texts.mat.11.22: Moreover, I say unto you, For Tyre and Zidon, more tolerable, will it be, in the day of judgment, than for you.
texts.mat.11.23: And, thou, Capernaum! Unto heaven, shalt thou be uplifted? Unto hades, thou shall be brought down; because, if, in Sodom, had been done the works of power, which were done in thee, it would, in that case, have remained until this day.
texts.mat.11.24: Moreover, I say unto you—For the land of Sodom, more tolerable, will it be in a day of judgment, than, for thee.
texts.mat.11.25: In that season, answered Jesus, and said—I openly give praise unto thee, Father, Lord of heaven and earth,—in that thou hast hid these things from the wise and discerning, and hast revealed them unto babes;
texts.mat.11.26: Yea, O Father! That, so, it hath become, a delight, before thee.
texts.mat.11.27: All things, unto me, have been delivered up by my Father; and, no one, fully knoweth the Son, save the rather, neither doth any one fully know, the Father, save, the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son, may be minded, to reveal, him.
texts.mat.11.28: Come unto me! all ye that toil and are burdened, and, I, will give you rest:
texts.mat.11.29: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me,—because, meek, am I and lowly, in heart, and ye shall find rest unto your souls;
texts.mat.11.30: For, my yoke, is easy, and, my burden, light.
texts.mat.12.1: In that season, went Jesus, on, the sabbath, through the cornfields,—and, his disciples, hungered, and began to pluck ears of corn, and to eat.
texts.mat.12.2: But, the Pharisees, observing it, said unto him, Lo! thy disciples, are doing what is not allowed to do, on sabbath.
texts.mat.12.3: And he said unto them, have ye never read what, David, did, when he hungered, and they who were with him? how
texts.mat.12.4: he entered into the house of God and, the presence-bread, did eat, which it was not, allowable, for him to eat, nor for them who were with him,—save for the priests, alone?
texts.mat.12.5: Or have ye not read, in the law, that, on the sabbaths, the priests, in the temple, the sabbath, profane, and are, blameless?
texts.mat.12.6: But I say unto you,—Something greater than the Temple, is here!
texts.mat.12.7: If, however, ye had known what this meaneth—Mercy, I desire, and not, sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the blameless;
texts.mat.12.8: For, the Son of Man, is, Lord of the Sabbath.
texts.mat.12.9: And, passing on from thence, he came into their synagogue;
texts.mat.12.10: and lo! a man having, a withered hand, and they questioned him, saying, Is it allowable, on the sabbath, to heal? that they might accuse him.
texts.mat.12.11: And said unto them, What man, from among yourselves, [shall there be],—Who shall have one sheep, and, if this should fall, on the sabbath, into a pit, will not lay hold of it, and raise it?
texts.mat.12.12: How much better, then, a man, than, a sheep? So that it is allowable, on the sabbath, nobly, to act.
texts.mat.12.13: Then saith he unto the man, Stretch forth thy hand! And he stretched it forth,—and it was restored, whole, as the other.
texts.mat.12.14: And the Pharisees, going forth, took, counsel, against him, to the end that, him, they might destroy.
texts.mat.12.15: But, Jesus, taking note, retired from thence,—and many followed him, and he cured them all;
texts.mat.12.16: and straitly charged them, lest they should make him, manifest:
texts.mat.12.17: that it might be fulfilled, which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying:—
texts.mat.12.18: Lo! my servant, whom I have chosen, My beloved, in whom, my soul, delighteth,—I will put my Spirit upon him, and, justice, unto the nations, will he report:
texts.mat.12.19: He will not strive, nor will he cry out, nor shall any hear, in the broadways, his voice:
texts.mat.12.20: A bruised cane, will he not break, and, a smoking wick, will he not quench,—until he urge on, justice, to victory,
texts.mat.12.21: And, in his name, shall nations hope.
texts.mat.12.22: Then they brought unto him, one demonized, blind and dumb,—and he cured him, so that the dumb did speak and see.
texts.mat.12.23: And all the multitudes were beside themselves, and were saying, Can, this one, be, the Son of David?
texts.mat.12.24: But, the Pharisees, hearing it, said, This one, doth not cast out the demons, save in Beelzebul ruler of the demons.
texts.mat.12.25: And, knowing their inward thoughts, he said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself, is laid waste,—and, no city or house divided against itself, will stand;
texts.mat.12.26: And, if, Satan, is casting, Satan, out, against himself, hath he become divided,—How then shall, his kingdom, stand?
texts.mat.12.27: And, if, I, in Beelzebul, am casting out the demons, In whom are, your sons, casting them out? Wherefore, they, shall be, judges of you.
texts.mat.12.28: But, if, in God’s Spirit, I, am casting out the demons, then doubtless hath come upon you unawares, the kingdom of God!
texts.mat.12.29: Or how can one enter the house of the mighty and, seize his goods, unless, first, he bind the mighty one? and, then, his house, he will plunder.
texts.mat.12.30: He that is no with me, is, against me,—and, he that gathereth not with me, scattereth
texts.mat.12.31: Wherefore, I say unto you, All sin and profane speaking, shall be forgiven unto men,—but, the speaking profanely of the Spirit, shall not be forgiven;
texts.mat.12.32: And, whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven him,—but, whosoever shall speak against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, either in this age, or the coming.
texts.mat.12.33: Either make the tree good, and its fruit good, or make the tree worthless, and its fruit worthless; for, from the fruit, the tree is known.
texts.mat.12.34: Broods of vipers! How can ye speak, good things, being, evil? For, out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaketh.
texts.mat.12.35: The good man, out of the good treasure, putteth forth, good things; and, the evil man, out of the evil treasure, putteth forth, evil things.
texts.mat.12.36: But I say unto you, That, every useless expression that men shall utter, they shall render, concerning it, an account, in a day of judgment;
texts.mat.12.37: For, by thy words, shalt thou be, justified, and, by thy words, shalt thou be condemned.
texts.mat.12.38: Then, answered him, certain of the Scribes and Pharisees, saying, Teacher! we desire of thee, a sign, to behold.
texts.mat.12.39: But, he, answering, said unto them, A wicked and adulterous generation, a sign, doth seek, and, a sign, will not be, given, it, save the sign of Jonah the prophet.
texts.mat.12.40: For, just as was Jonah in the belly of the sea-monster three days and three nights, so, will be the Son of Man, in the heart of the earth, three days and three nights.
texts.mat.12.41: Men of Nineveh, will rise up in the judgment, with this generation, and will condemn it,—because they repented into the proclamation of Jonah; and lo! something greater than Jonah, here.
texts.mat.12.42: The queen of the south, will arise in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it—because she came out of the ends of the earth, to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and lo! something greater than Solomon, here.
texts.mat.12.43: But, when the impure spirit goeth out of the man, it passeth through waterless places, seeking rest,—and findeth it not.
texts.mat.12.44: Then, it saith, Into my house, will I return whence I came out,—and, coming, findeth it empty [and] swept and adorned.
texts.mat.12.45: Then, it goeth, and taketh along with itself, seven diverse spirits, more wicked than itself,—and, entering, abideth there; and, the last state of that man, becometh, worse than the first. So, shall it be, with this, wicked, generation.
texts.mat.12.46: While yet he was speaking unto the multitudes, lo! his mother and brethren, were standing without, seeking to speak with him.
texts.mat.12.47: [And one said to him, Lo! thy mother and thy brethren, without, are standing, seeking, to speak, with thee.]
texts.mat.12.48: But, he, answering, said unto him that was telling him, Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?
texts.mat.12.49: And, stretching forth his hand towards his disciples, he said, Lo! my mother and my brethren!
texts.mat.12.50: For, whosoever shall do the will of my Father who is in the heavens, he, is my, brother, and sister, and mother.
texts.mat.13.1: On that day, Jesus, going out of the house, was sitting near the sea:
texts.mat.13.2: and there were gathered unto him, large multitudes, so that, he, into a boat, entered, and was sitting, and, all the multitude, on the beach was standing.
texts.mat.13.3: And he spake unto them many things, in parables, saying: Lo! the sower went forth to sow,—
texts.mat.13.4: and, as he sowed, some, indeed, fell by the pathway, and, the birds, came, and devoured it;
texts.mat.13.5: And, some, fell on the rocky places, where it had not much earth,—and, straightway, it sprang up, because if had no depth of earth;
texts.mat.13.6: and, the sun arising, it was scorched, and, because it had no root, it withered away;
texts.mat.13.7: And, some, fell upon the thorns, and the thorns came up, and choked it;
texts.mat.13.8: But, some, fell upon the good ground, and did yield fruit,—this, indeed a hundred fold, and, that, sixty, and, the other, thirty.
texts.mat.13.9: He that hath ears, let him hear.
texts.mat.13.10: And the disciples, coming near, said to him, Wherefore, in parables, art thou speaking to them?
texts.mat.13.11: And, he, answering, said, Because, unto you, hath it been given, to get to know the sacred secrets of the kingdom of the heavens,—whereas, unto them, hath it not been given.
texts.mat.13.12: For, whosoever hath, it shall be given, to him, and he shall be made to abound,—but, whoever hath not, even what he hath, shall be taken from him?
texts.mat.13.13: For this reason, in parables, unto them, do I speak,—because, seeing, they see not, and, hearing, they hear not,—neither do they understand.
texts.mat.13.14: And, again is being fulfilled in them, the prophecy of Isaiah, which saith,—They shall, surely hear, and yet will not understand, and, surely see, and yet not perceive;
texts.mat.13.15: For the heart of this people hath become dense, and, with their ears, heavily have they heard, and, their eyes, have they closed,—lest, once they should see with their eyes, and, with their ears, should hear, and, with their hearts, should understand, and return; when I would certainly heal them.
texts.mat.13.16: But happy are, your, eyes, that they see, and your ears, that they hear;
texts.mat.13.17: For, verily, I say unto you—Many prophets and righteous men, have coveted to see what ye see, and have not seen, and to hear what ye hear, and have not heard.
texts.mat.13.18: Hear, ye, then, the parable of him that sowed:—
texts.mat.13.19: When anyone heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, the wicked one cometh, and catcheth up that which hath been sown in his heart,—this, is he, by the pathway, sown.
texts.mat.13.20: And, he on the rocky places sown, the same, is he that, heareth the word, and, straightway, with joy, receiveth it;
texts.mat.13.21: yet hath he no root in himself, but is, only for a season,—and, there arising, tribulation or persecution because of the word, straightway, he findeth cause of stumbling.
texts.mat.13.22: And, he among the thorns sown, the same, is he that, heareth the word,—and, the anxiety of the age and the deceit of riches, choke up the word, and, unfruitful, it becometh.
texts.mat.13.23: But, he on the good ground sown, the same, is he who doth hear and understand the word, who, indeed, beareth fruit and produceth,—this, a hundred, and, that, sixty, and, the other, thirty.
texts.mat.13.24: Another parable, put he before them, saying—The kingdom of the heavens hath become like a man sowing good seed in his field;
texts.mat.13.25: and, while men were sleeping, his enemy came, and sowed over darnel, in among the wheat,—and away he went.
texts.mat.13.26: And, when the blade shot up, and brought forth, fruit, then, appeared, the darnel also.
texts.mat.13.27: And the servants of the householder, coming near, said to him,—Sir! was it not, good seed, thou didst sow in thy field? Whence then hath it, darnel?
texts.mat.13.28: And he said unto them—An enemy, hath, done this. And they say, unto him—Wilt thou, then, that we go and collect it?
texts.mat.13.29: And, he, saith—Nay! lest, at any time, while collecting the darnel, ye uproot, along with it, the wheat:
texts.mat.13.30: Suffer both to grow together until the harvest, and at, harvest time, I will say unto the reapers,—Collect ye first, the darnel, and bind it into bundles, with a view to the burning it up; but, the wheat, be gathering it into my barn.
texts.mat.13.31: Another parable, put he before them, saying—The kingdom of the heavens is like unto, a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field;
texts.mat.13.32: which, indeed, is, less, than all seeds, but, when grown, is greater than garden-plants, and becometh a tree,—so that the birds of heaven come, and lodge among its branches.
texts.mat.13.33: Another parable, [spake he unto them]:—The kingdom of the heavens is like, unto leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until, the whole, was leavened.
texts.mat.13.34: All these things, spake Jesus in parables, unto the multitudes, and, without a parable, was he speaking, nothing, unto them:
texts.mat.13.35: that it might be fulfilled, which was spoken through the prophet, saying—I will open, in parables, my mouth, I will bring up things hidden from the foundation!
texts.mat.13.36: Then, dismissing the multitudes, he went into the house, and his disciples came near to him, saying—Make quite plain to us the parable of the darnel of the field.
texts.mat.13.37: And, he, answering, said—He that soweth the good seed, is the Son of Man;
texts.mat.13.38: And, the field, is the world, and, the good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom,—and, the darnel seeds, are the sons of the evil one;
texts.mat.13.39: And, the enemy that sowed them, is the adversary, and, the harvest, is, the conclusion of an age, and, the reapers, are, messengers.
texts.mat.13.40: Just, therefore, as collected is the darnel, and, with fire is burned, so, will it be in the conclusion of the age:—
texts.mat.13.41: The Son of Man will send forth his messengers, and they will collect, out of his kingdom, all the causes of stumbling, and the doers of lawlessness,
texts.mat.13.42: and will cast them into the furnace of fire: there, will be wailing and gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.13.43: Then, the righteous, will shine forth as the sun, in the kingdom of their Father. He that hath ears, let him hear!
texts.mat.13.44: The kingdom of the heavens is like unto, a treasure hid in the field, which a man, finding, hid,—and, by reason of his joy, withdraweth and selleth whatsoever he hath, and buyeth that field.
texts.mat.13.45: Again, the kingdom of the heavens is, like, unto, a merchant, seeking beautiful pearls,—
texts.mat.13.46: and, finding one very precious pearl, departing, he at once sold all things, whatsoever he had, and bought it.
texts.mat.13.47: Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like unto, a large drag-net, cast into the sea and gathering of every kind,—
texts.mat.13.48: which, when it was filled, they dragged up on the beach, and, sitting down, collected the good into vessels, but, the worthless, forth they cast.
texts.mat.13.49: So, will it be in the conclusion of the age: The messengers will come forth, and separate the wicked from among the righteous;
texts.mat.13.50: and will cast them into the furnace of fire: there, will be wailing and gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.13.51: Have ye understood all these things? They say unto him, Yea!
texts.mat.13.52: And, he, said unto them—Wherefore, every scribe, discipled unto the kingdom of the heavens, is like unto a householder, who putteth forth out of his treasure, things new and old.
texts.mat.13.53: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these parables, he removed from thence;
texts.mat.13.54: and, coming into his own city, began teaching them in their synagogue, so that with astonishment were they being struck, and were saying—Whence, hath, this one, this wisdom, and the mighty works?
texts.mat.13.55: Is not, this one, the carpenter’s, son? Is not, his mother, called Mary, and are not his brethren—James and Joseph, and Simon, and Judas?
texts.mat.13.56: and, his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence, then hath, this one, all these things?
texts.mat.13.57: And they began to find cause of stumbling in him. But, Jesus, said unto them—A prophet is not without honour, save in his city, and in his house.
texts.mat.13.58: And he did not, there, many mighty works, because of their unbelief.
texts.mat.14.1: In that season, heard Herod the tetrarch, the fame of Jesus:
texts.mat.14.2: and he said unto his servants—This, is John the Immerser,—he hath arisen from the dead, for this cause, are the powers working mightily within him.
texts.mat.14.3: For, Herod, seizing John, had bound him, and, in prison, put him away,—because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother;
texts.mat.14.4: for John had been saying to him, It is not allowed thee, to have her.
texts.mat.14.5: And desiring, to kill, him, he feared the multitude, because, as a prophet, they held him.
texts.mat.14.6: But, a birthday feast of Herod taking place, the daughter of Herodias danced in the midst, and pleased Herod;
texts.mat.14.7: wherefore, with an oath, he promised to give her, whatsoever she should ask for herself;
texts.mat.14.8: and, she, being led on by her mother,—Give me (saith she) here, upon a charger, the head of John the Immerser.
texts.mat.14.9: And the king, though grieved, yet, because of the oaths and the guests, ordered it to be given;
texts.mat.14.10: and sent and beheaded John in the prison.
texts.mat.14.11: And his head was brought upon a charger, and given unto the maiden, and she brought it to her mother.
texts.mat.14.12: And his disciples, going near, bare away the corpse, and buried him, and came and brought tidings unto Jesus.
texts.mat.14.13: And Jesus, hearing it, retired from thence in a boat, into a desert place, apart,—and the multitudes, hearing of it, followed him on foot from the cities.
texts.mat.14.14: And, coming forth, he saw a great multitude,—and was moved with compassion over them, and cured their sick.
texts.mat.14.15: And, evening, arriving, the disciples came unto him, saying—The place is, a desert, and, the hour, hath already passed,—dismiss the multitudes, that they may go away into the villages, and buy themselves food.
texts.mat.14.16: But, Jesus, said unto them, No need, have they to go away,—give, ye, them to eat.
texts.mat.14.17: But, they, say unto him—We have nothing here, save five loaves and two fishes.
texts.mat.14.18: But, he, said—Bring, them, to me, here.
texts.mat.14.19: And, giving orders that the multitudes should recline upon the grass,—taking the five loaves and the two fishes,—looking up into the heaven, he blessed; and, breaking, gave, the disciples, the loaves, and the disciples unto the multitude.
texts.mat.14.20: And they did all eat, and were filled,—and they took up the remainder of the broken pieces, twelve baskets, full.
texts.mat.14.21: And, they who did eat, were about five thousand, men, besides women and children.
