texts.mat.14.22: And [straightway] constrained he the disciples to enter into a boat, and be going before him unto the other side, while he dismissed the multitudes.
texts.mat.14.23: And, dismissing the multitudes, he went up into the mountain, apart, to pray,—and when, evening, came, alone, was he, there.
texts.mat.14.24: Now, the boat, still many furlongs from the land, was holding off, being distressed by the waves,—for, the wind, was, contrary.
texts.mat.14.25: And, in the fourth watch of the night, he came unto them, walking upon the sea.
texts.mat.14.26: And, the disciples, seeing him, upon the lake walking, were troubled,—saying—It is, a ghost; and, by reason of their fear, they cried out.
texts.mat.14.27: And, straightway, Jesus spake unto them, saying—Take courage! it is, I,—be not afraid.
texts.mat.14.28: And, making answer, Peter said unto him,—Lord! if it is, thou, bid me come unto thee, upon the waters.
texts.mat.14.29: And, he, said—Come! And, descending from the boat, Peter walked upon the waters, and came unto Jesus.
texts.mat.14.30: But, seeing the wind, he was affrighted, and, beginning to sink, cried out, saying—Lord! save me!
texts.mat.14.31: And, straightway, Jesus, stretching forth his hand, laid hold upon him and saith unto him—O little-of-faith! why didst thou doubt?
texts.mat.14.32: And, when they came up into the boat, the wind abated.
texts.mat.14.33: And, they in the boat, bowed down to him, saying—Truly, God’s Son, thou art!
texts.mat.14.34: And, going across, they came up the land, into Gennesaret.
texts.mat.14.35: And, recognizing him, the men of that place, sent out into all that region, and they brought unto him all who were sick;
texts.mat.14.36: and were beseeching [him], that they might, only, touch the border of his mantle, and, as many as touched, were made quite well.
texts.mat.15.1: Then, there come unto Jesus from Jerusalem Pharisees and Scribes, saying—
texts.mat.15.2: Wherefore do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands, when they eat bread!
texts.mat.15.3: But, he, answering, said unto them—Wherefore do, ye also, transgress the commandment of God for the sake of your tradition?
texts.mat.15.4: For, God, said—Honour thy father and thy mother, and—He that revileth father or mother, let him, surely die!
texts.mat.15.5: But, ye, say—Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother—A gift! Whatsoever, out of me, thou mightest be profited,
texts.mat.15.6: in nowise, shall honour his father or his mother—and so ye have cancelled, the word of God, for the sake of your, tradition.
texts.mat.15.7: Hypocrites! well prophesied concerning you, Isaiah, saying—
texts.mat.15.8: This people, with the lips, do, honour, me, while, their heart, far off, holdeth from me;
texts.mat.15.9: But, in vain, do they pay devotions unto me, teaching, for teachings, the commandments of men.
texts.mat.15.10: And, calling near the multitude, he said to them—Hear and understand!
texts.mat.15.11: Not that which entereth into the mouth, defileth the man, but, that which proceedeth out of the mouth, the same, defileth the man,
texts.mat.15.12: Then, coming near, his disciples say unto him—Knowest thou, that the Pharisees, hearing the word, were caused to stumble?
texts.mat.15.13: And, he, answering, said—Every plant which my heavenly Father hath not planted, will be uprooted:
texts.mat.15.14: Let them alone! they are, blind leaders; and, if the, blind, lead the, blind, both, into a ditch, will fall.
texts.mat.15.15: And Peter, answering, said unto him, Declare to us the parable.
texts.mat.15.16: And, he, said, To this moment, are, ye also, without discernment?
texts.mat.15.17: Perceive ye not that, every thing which entereth into the mouth, into the stomach, findeth way, and, into the draught, is passed;
texts.mat.15.18: while, the things which proceed out of the mouth, out of the heart, come forth, and, they, defile the man.
texts.mat.15.19: For, out of the heart, come forth wicked designs,—murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, profane speakings:
texts.mat.15.20: these, are the things which defile the man, but, the eating with unwashed hands, doth not defile the man.
texts.mat.15.21: And, going forth from thence, Jesus retired into the parts of Tyre and Zidon.
texts.mat.15.22: And lo! a Canaanite woman, from those bounds, coming forth, began crying out, saying, Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter, is miserably demonized.
texts.mat.15.23: But, he, answered her no a word. And his disciples, coming forward began requesting him, saying—Dismiss her, because she is crying out after us.
texts.mat.15.24: But, he, answering, said, I was not sent forth, save unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
texts.mat.15.25: And, she, coming, began bowing down to him, saying, Lord! help me.
texts.mat.15.26: But, he, answering, said, It is, not seemly, to take the loaf of, the children, and cast, to the little dogs.
texts.mat.15.27: And, she, said, True, Lord! [for], even the little dogs, eat of the crumbs which are falling from the table of, their masters.
texts.mat.15.28: Then, answering, Jesus said to her—O woman! great, is, thy faith! Be it, done, for thee, as thou desirest. And her daughter was healed, from that hour.
texts.mat.15.29: And, passing on from thence, Jesus came near the sea of Galilee, and, going up into the mountain, was sitting there.
texts.mat.15.30: And there came unto him large multitudes, having with themselves the lame, the maimed, the blind, the dumb, and many others,—and they cast them near his feet, and he cured them;
texts.mat.15.31: so that the multitude marvelled, seeing the dumb speaking, the lame walking, and the blind seeing,—and they glorified the God of Israel.
texts.mat.15.32: But, Jesus, calling near his disciples, said—My compassions are moved towards the multitude, because [even now], three days, abide they with me, and they have nothing to eat,—and, to dismiss them fasting, I am not willing, lest by any means they faint in the way.
texts.mat.15.33: And his disciples say unto him—Whence, to us, in a wilderness, loaves in such numbers as to fill a multitude, so great?
texts.mat.15.34: And Jesus saith unto them—How many, loaves have ye? And, they, said,—Seven, and a few small fishes.
texts.mat.15.35: And, sending word to the multitude to recline upon the ground,
texts.mat.15.36: he took the seven loaves, and the fishes, and, giving thanks, brake,—and began giving to his disciples, and, the disciples, to the multitudes.
texts.mat.15.37: And they all did eat and were filled,—and, the remainder of the broken pieces, took they up, seven hampers, full.
texts.mat.15.38: And, they who did eat, were four thousand men, besides women and children.
texts.mat.15.39: And, dismissing the multitudes, he went up into the boat,—and came into the bounds of Magadan.
texts.mat.16.1: And, the Pharisees and Sadducees coming near, putting him to the test, requested him, a sign out of the heaven, to shew unto them.
texts.mat.16.2: But, he, answering said unto them— [[When evening cometh ye say, Fair! for fiery is the heaven;
texts.mat.16.3: And at morn, To-day, a storm! for fiery, and yet sad, is the heaven. The face of the heaven indeed, ye learn to distinguish,—but, the signs of the times, ye cannot.]]
texts.mat.16.4: A wicked and adulterous generation, a sign, doth seek after, and, a sign, will not be given it,—save the sign of Jonah. And, leaving them behind, he departed.
texts.mat.16.5: And the disciples coming, to the other side, had forgotten to take loaves.
texts.mat.16.6: And, Jesus, said unto them—Mind! and beware, of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
texts.mat.16.7: And, they, began to deliberate among themselves, saying—Because, loaves, we took not.
texts.mat.16.8: And, observing it, Jesus said—Why are ye deliberating among yourselves, ye little-of-faith! because, loaves, ye have not?
texts.mat.16.9: Not yet, perceive ye, neither remember,—The five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets ye received?
texts.mat.16.10: Nor the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many hampers ye received?
texts.mat.16.11: How is it ye perceive not, that, not concerning loaves, spake I unto you,—but beware of the leaven, of the Pharisees and Sadducees?
texts.mat.16.12: Then, understood they that he did not bid them beware of [the] leaven [of loaves] but of, the teaching, of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
texts.mat.16.13: And, Jesus coming into the parts of Caesarea of Philip, began questioning his disciples, saying—Who are men saying that, the Son of Man, is?
texts.mat.16.14: And, they, said—Some, indeed, John the Immerser, and, others, Elijah,—but, others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.
texts.mat.16.15: He saith unto them—But who say, ye, that I am?
texts.mat.16.16: And, Simon Peter, answering, said—Thou, art the Christ, the Son of the Living God.
texts.mat.16.17: And Jesus, answering, said to him—Happy, art thou, Simon Bar-yona,—because, flesh and blood, revealed it not unto thee, but my Father who is in the heavens.
texts.mat.16.18: And, I also, unto thee, say—Thou, art Peter,—and, upon this rock, will I build my assembly, and, the gates of hades, shall not prevail against it.
texts.mat.16.19: I will give thee, the keys of the kingdom of the heavens,—and, whatsoever thou shalt bind upon the earth, shall be bound in the heavens, and, whatsoever thou shalt loose upon the earth, shall be loosed in the heavens.
texts.mat.16.20: Then, straitly charged he the disciples, lest, to any man, they should say—He, is, the Christ.
texts.mat.16.21: From that time, began Jesus Christ to be pointing out to his disciples that he must needs, into Jerusalem, go away, and, many things, suffer, from the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain,—and on, the third day, arise.
texts.mat.16.22: And, taking him aside, Peter began to rebuke him, saying—Mercy on thee Lord! In nowise, shall, this, befall thee.
texts.mat.16.23: But, he, turning, said to Peter—Withdraw behind me, Satan! A snare, art thou of mine, because thou art not regarding the things of God, but the things of men.
texts.mat.16.24: Then, Jesus said unto his disciples—If any one intendeth, after me, to come, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and be following me;
texts.mat.16.25: For, whosoever intendeth, his life, to save, shall lose it,—but, whosoever shall lose his life, for my sake, shall find it.
texts.mat.16.26: For what shall a man be profited, though, the whole world, he gain, and, his life, he forfeit? Or what shall a man give, in exchange for his life?
texts.mat.16.27: For the Son of Man is destined to be coming, in the glory of his Father, with his messengers,—and, then, will he give back unto each one, according to his practice.
texts.mat.16.28: Verily, I say unto you—There are some of those, here standing, who, indeed, shall in nowise taste of death, until they see the Son of Man, coming in his kingdom.
texts.mat.17.1: And, after six days, Jesus taketh with him, Peter and James and John his brother, and bringeth them up into a high mountain, apart;
texts.mat.17.2: and was transformed before them,—and his face shone as the sun, and, his garments, became white as the light.
texts.mat.17.3: And lo! there appeared to them Moses and Elijah, conversing with him.
texts.mat.17.4: And Peter, answering, said unto Jesus—Lord! it is, delightful, for us, to be here,—If thou wilt, I will make here three tents, for thee, one, and, for Moses, one, and, for Elijah, one.
texts.mat.17.5: While yet he was speaking, lo! a brightly shining cloud, overshadowed them, and lo! a voice, out of the cloud, saying—This, is, my Son, the Beloved, in whom I delight,—Be hearkening to him.
texts.mat.17.6: And, hearing it, the disciples fell upon their face, and were caused to fear exceedingly.
texts.mat.17.7: And Jesus came near, and, touching them, said—Arise! and be not afraid.
texts.mat.17.8: And, lifting up their eyes, no one, saw they, save Jesus, himself, alone.
texts.mat.17.9: And, as they were coming down out of the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying—Unto no one, may ye tell the vision, until the Son of Man, from among the dead shall arise.
texts.mat.17.10: And the disciples questioned him, saying—Why then do, the Scribes, say, that, Elijah, must needs come, first?
texts.mat.17.11: And, he, answering, said—Elijah, indeed, cometh, and will restored all things;
texts.mat.17.12: But, I say unto you—that, Elijah, just now, came,—and they recognised him not, but did with him, whatsoever they pleased: Thus, the Son of Man also, is destined to suffer by them.
texts.mat.17.13: Then, perceived the disciples, that, concerning John the Immerser, he spake to them.
texts.mat.17.14: And, when they came unto the multitude, there approached him a man, falling on his knees to him,
texts.mat.17.15: and saying—Lord! have mercy upon my son,—because he is lunatic, and in a grievous condition; For, many times, falleth he into the fire, and, many times, into the water.
texts.mat.17.16: And I brought him unto thy disciples, and they could not cure, him.
texts.mat.17.17: And Jesus, answering, said—O faithless and perverted generation! How long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to me, here.
texts.mat.17.18: And Jesus rebuked it; and the demon came out of him,—and cured was the boy, from that hour.
texts.mat.17.19: Then, the disciples, coming near, to Jesus, privately, said—Wherefore could, we, not cast it out?
texts.mat.17.20: And, he, saith unto them—Because of your little faith. For, verily, I say unto you—If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say to this mountain, remove hence yonder; and it shall be removed, and, nothing, shall be impossible to you.
texts.mat.17.22: And, as they were being gathered together in Galilee, Jesus said unto them—The Son of Man is about to be delivered up into the hands of men;
texts.mat.17.23: And they will slay him, and, on the third day, will he, arise. And they were grieved exceedingly.
texts.mat.17.24: And, when they came into Capernaum, they who, the half shekel, were receiving, came near unto Peter, and said, Your teacher, doth he not pay the half shekel?
texts.mat.17.25: He saith—Yea. And, coming into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying, How, to thee, doth it seem, Simon? The kings of the earth, of whom receive they dues or tax? from their sons, or from the aliens?
texts.mat.17.26: And, when he said, From the aliens, Jesus said unto him, Well then, free, are the sons!
texts.mat.17.27: But, that we may not cause them to stumble, go unto the sea, and cast in a hook, and, the first fish that cometh up, take, and, opening its mouth, thou shalt find a shekel,—that, take, and give to them for me and thee.
texts.mat.18.1: In that hour came, the disciples unto Jesus, saying—Who then is, greatest, in the kingdom of the heavens?
texts.mat.18.2: And, calling near a child, he set it in the midst of them,
texts.mat.18.3: and said—Verily, I say unto you, Except ye turn and become as the children, in nowise, shall ye enter into the kingdom of the heavens.
texts.mat.18.4: Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this child, the same, is the greatest, in the kingdom of the heavens;
texts.mat.18.5: And, whosoever shall give welcome unto one such child as this, upon my name, unto me, giveth welcome.
texts.mat.18.6: And, whosoever shall cause to stumble one of these little ones who believe in me, it profiteth him, that there be hung a large mill-stone about his neck, and he be sunk in the wide main of the sea.
texts.mat.18.7: Alas for the world! by reason of the causes of stumbling; for it is, necessary, that the causes of stumbling come,—nevertheless, alas for the man through whom the cause of stumbling cometh!
texts.mat.18.8: But, if, thy hand or thy foot, be causing thee to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from thee: It is, seemly for thee, to enter into life, maimed or lame, rather than, having two hands or two feet, to be cast into the age-abiding fire.
texts.mat.18.9: And, if, thine eye, causeth thee to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: It is, seemly, for thee, one-eyed, into life, to enter, rather than, having two eyes, to be cast into the fiery gehenna.
texts.mat.18.10: Beware! do not despise one of these little ones; For I say unto you—that, their messengers in the heavens, do, continually, behold the face of my Father in the heavens.
texts.mat.18.12: How, to you, doth it seem? If a certain man come to have a hundred sheep and one from among them go astray, Will he not leave the ninety-nine upon the mountains, and going, seek the straying one?
texts.mat.18.13: And, if it should be that he find it, Verily, I say unto you—He rejoiceth over it, more than over the ninety-nine that have not gone astray.
texts.mat.18.14: Thus, there is no desire, in the presence of my Father who is in the heavens, that, one of these little ones, should be lost.
texts.mat.18.15: But, if thy brother sin, withdraw, convince him, betwixt thee and him, alone,—If unto thee he hearken, thou hast gained thy brother;
texts.mat.18.16: But, if he do not hearken, take with thee, yet one or two, that, at the mouth of two witnesses or three, every declaration, maybe established;
texts.mat.18.17: But, if he hear them amiss, tell it to the assembly,—And, if, even the assembly, he hear amiss, Let him be unto thee, just as the man of the nations and the tax-collector.
texts.mat.18.18: Verily, I say unto you—Whatsoever things ye shall bind on the earth, shall be bound in heaven; and, whatsoever things ye shall loose on the earth, shall be loosed in heaven.
texts.mat.18.19: Again, [verily] I say unto you—If two from among you shall agree upon the earth concerning any matter, whatsoever they shall ask, it shall be brought to pass for them, from my Father who is in the heavens;
texts.mat.18.20: For, where there are two or three, gathered together into my name, there, am I, in their midst.
texts.mat.18.21: Then, coming near, Peter said [to him] —Lord! how many times, shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until, seven, times?
texts.mat.18.22: Jesus saith to him—I say not unto thee, unto, seven, times, but, until seventy times seven.
texts.mat.18.23: For this cause, hath the kingdom of the heavens become like unto a man, a king, who wished to settle an account with his servants;
texts.mat.18.24: And, when he, began, to settle, there was brought unto him a, certain, debtor, of a thousand talents;
texts.mat.18.25: and, he, not having, wherewith to pay, the master ordered him to be sold, and the wife, and the children, and whatsoever he had,—and payment to be made.
texts.mat.18.26: The servant therefore, falling down, began to do homage unto him, saying—Have patience with me, and, all, will I pay thee.
texts.mat.18.27: And, moved with compassion, the master of that servant released him, and, the loan, he, forgave, him.
texts.mat.18.28: But that servant, going out, found one of his fellow-servants, who owed him, a hundred denaries, and, laying hold of him, he began seizing him by the throat, saying, Pay! if anything thou owest.
texts.mat.18.29: His fellow servant, therefore, falling down, began beseeching him, saying, Have patience with me! And I will pay thee.
texts.mat.18.30: He, however, would not, but went away and cast him into prison,—until he should pay what was owing.
texts.mat.18.31: His fellow-servants, therefore, seeing, the things that were done, were grieved exceedingly,—and went and made quite plain to their master all the things which had been done.
texts.mat.18.32: Then, calling him near, his master saith unto him—O wicked servant! All that debt, forgave I thee, because thou didst beseech me.
texts.mat.18.33: Was it not binding, upon thee also, to have mercy upon thy fellow-servant, as, I also, on thee, had mercy?
texts.mat.18.34: And, provoked to anger, his master delivered him up to the torturers, until he should pay all that was owing.
texts.mat.18.35: Thus, my heavenly Father also, will do unto you, if ye forgive not each one his brother, from your hearts.
texts.mat.19.1: And it came to pass, when Jesus ended these words, he removed from Galilee and came into the bounds of Judaea beyond the Jordan.
texts.mat.19.2: And there followed him large multitudes, and he cured them there.
texts.mat.19.3: And there came unto him Pharisees, testing him, and saying,—Whether is it allowed a man to divorce his wife, for every cause?
texts.mat.19.4: And, he, answering, said—Did ye never read—He who created at the beginning, Male and female, made them,—
texts.mat.19.5: and said—For this cause, will a man leave his father and his mother, and be united to his wife,—and, the two, will become, one flesh;
texts.mat.19.6: So that, the longer, are they, two, but, one flesh, What, therefore, God, hath yoked together, Let not, a man, put asunder.
texts.mat.19.7: They say unto him—Why then did, Moses, command, to give a writing of repudiation and to divorce?
texts.mat.19.8: He saith unto them—Moses, in view of your hardness of heart, permitted you to divorce your wives; From the beginning however, hath it not been done, thus.
texts.mat.19.9: And I say unto you—Whosoever shall divorce his wife, saving for unfaithfulness, and shall marry another, committeth adultery.
texts.mat.19.10: The disciples say unto him—If, so, is the cause of the husband with the wife, it is not expedient to marry.
texts.mat.19.11: But, he, said unto them—Not all, find room for he word, save they to whom it hath been given;
texts.mat.19.12: For there, are, eunuchs, who, from their mother’s womb, were born so, and there, are, eunuchs, who were made eunuchs, by men,—and there, are, eunuchs, who have made, themselves, eunuchs, for the sake the kingdom of the heavens: He that is able to find room, let him find room.
texts.mat.19.13: Then, were brought unto him children,—that he might lay his hands upon them, and pray. And, the disciples, rebuked them.
texts.mat.19.14: But, Jesus, said—Suffer the children—and do not hinder them—to come unto me,—for, of such, is the kingdom of the heavens.
texts.mat.19.15: And, laying his hands upon them, he went his way from thence.
texts.mat.19.16: And lo! one coming near unto him, said, Teacher! what good thing shall I do, that I may have life age-abiding?
texts.mat.19.17: And, he, said unto him—Why dost thou question me concerning that which is good? There is, One, that is good! But, if thou desirest, into life, to enter, be keeping the commandments.
texts.mat.19.18: He saith unto him, Which? Jesus, said—These: Thou shalt not commit murder, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not steal,—Thou shalt not bear false witness;
texts.mat.19.19: Honour thy father and thy mother,—and—Thou shalt love thy neighbour as, thyself.
texts.mat.19.20: The young man saith unto him—These all, have I kept,—What, further, do I lack?
texts.mat.19.21: Jesus said unto him—If thou desirest to be perfect, Withdraw! sell thy substance, and give to the destitute,—and thou shalt have treasure in the heavens; and come! be following me.
texts.mat.19.22: And the young man, hearing, this word, went away sorrowing,—for he was holding large possessions.
texts.mat.19.23: And, Jesus, said unto his disciples—Verily, I say unto you, A rich man, with difficulty, shall enter into the kingdom of the heavens.
texts.mat.19.24: Again I say unto you—Easier, is it for, a camel, through the eye of a needle, to enter, than a rich man—into the kingdom of God.
texts.mat.19.25: And, hearing it, the disciples were being struck with the greatest astonishment, saying—Who then can be saved?
texts.mat.19.26: And, looking intently, Jesus said unto them—With men, this is, impossible, but, with God, all things are possible.
texts.mat.19.27: Then, making answer, Peter said unto him—Lo! we, have left all, and followed thee,—What then shall there be, for us?
texts.mat.19.28: And, Jesus, said unto them—Verily, I say unto you, As for you who followed me in the regeneration, When the Son of Man shall take his seat on his throne of glory, ye also, shall be seated upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
texts.mat.19.29: And, whosoever left houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or children, or lands, for sake of my name, manifold, shall receive, and life, age-abiding, shall inherit.
texts.mat.19.30: But many shall be—first-last, and last-first.
texts.mat.20.1: For the kingdom of the heavens, is like, a man, a householder,—who went forth with the morning, to hire labourers into his vineyard;
texts.mat.20.2: and, when he had agreed with the labourers for a denary the day, he sent them into his vineyard.
texts.mat.20.3: And, going forth about the third hour, he saw others, standing in the market-place, unemployed;
texts.mat.20.4: and, to them, he said—ye also, go your way into the vineyard, and, whatsoever may be right, I will give you;
texts.mat.20.5: and, they, departed. And, again, going forth about the sixth and ninth hour, he did likewise.
texts.mat.20.6: And, about the eleventh, going forth, he found others, standing, and saith unto them—Why, here, stand ye, all the day, unemployed?
texts.mat.20.7: They say unto him—Because, no one, hath hired, us. He saith unto them—Ye also, go your way into the vineyard.
texts.mat.20.8: And, when evening came, the master of the vineyard saith unto his steward—Call the labourers, and pay the hire,—beginning from the last, unto the first.
texts.mat.20.9: And they of the eleventh hour, coming, received severally a denary.
texts.mat.20.10: And, when the first came, they supposed that, more, they should receive,—and, they also, received severally a denary.
texts.mat.20.11: And, having received it, they began to murmur against the householder, saying—
texts.mat.20.12: These last, one hour, wrought, and thou hast made them, equal unto us, who have borne the burden of the day, and the scorching heat.
texts.mat.20.13: And, he, answering, unto one of them, said,—Friend! I wrong thee not: Was it not, for a denary, thou didst agree with me?
texts.mat.20.14: Take thine own, and go thy way; but I please, unto this last, to give, as also to thee:
texts.mat.20.15: Is it not allowed me to do, what I please, with my own? or is, thine eye, evil, because I good?
texts.mat.20.16: Thus, shall be—The last first, and the first last.
texts.mat.20.17: And, Jesus, being about to go up unto Jerusalem, took unto him the twelve [disciples], apart, and, in the way, he said unto them—
texts.mat.20.18: Lo! we are going up unto Jerusalem; and, the Son of Man, will be delivered up unto the chief-priests and Scribes, and they will condemn him, [to death],
texts.mat.20.19: And deliver him up unto the nations, to mock and to scourge and to crucify,—and, on the third day, he will, arise.
texts.mat.20.20: Then came unto him the mother of the sons of Zebedee, with her sons, bowing down, and asking something from him.
texts.mat.20.21: And, he, said to her—What desirest thou? She saith unto him—Bid, that these my two sons may sit, one on thy right hand, and one on thy left, in thy kingdom.
texts.mat.20.22: But Jesus, answering, said—Ye know not what ye are asking: Are ye able to drink the cup, which, I, am about to drink; They say unto him—We are able.
texts.mat.20.23: He saith unto them—My cup, indeed, ye shall drink; but, to sit on my right hand and on my left, is not mine to give,—except unto those for whom it hath been prepared by my Father.
texts.mat.20.24: And the ten, hearing, were sorely displeased, concerning the two brethren.
texts.mat.20.25: But, Jesus, calling them near, said—Ye know that, the rulers of the nations, lord it over them, and, the great ones, wield authority over them:
texts.mat.20.26: Not so, is it, among you,—but, whosoever shall desire, among you, to become, great, shall be, your minister;
texts.mat.20.27: And, whosoever shall desire, among you, to be first, shall be, your servant:—
texts.mat.20.28: Just as, the Son of Man, came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom instead of many.
texts.mat.20.29: And, as they were going forth from Jericho, there followed him a great multitude;
texts.mat.20.30: and lo! two blind men, sitting beside the road, hearing that Jesus was passing by, cried aloud saying—Lord! have mercy on us! Son of David!
texts.mat.20.31: But the multitude rebuked them, that they might hold their peace. But, they, the more, cried aloud, saying—Lord, have mercy on us! Son of David!
texts.mat.20.32: And, standing still, Jesus called them, and said—What desire ye I should do for you?
texts.mat.20.33: They say unto him—Lord! that, our eyes, may open.
texts.mat.20.34: And, moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes,—and, straightway, they recovered sight, and followed him.
texts.mat.21.1: And, when they drew near unto Jerusalem, and came unto Bethphage, unto the Mount of Olives, then, Jesus sent forth two disciples;
texts.mat.21.2: saying unto them—Be going into the village that is over against you, and, straightway, ye shall find an ass, bound, and a colt with her,—loose them, and lead them unto me.
texts.mat.21.3: And, if anyone, unto you, say aught, ye shall say—Their Lord, hath, need,—and, straightway, he will send them.
texts.mat.21.4: But, this, hath come to pass, that it might be fulfilled, which was spoken through the prophet, saying:
texts.mat.21.5: Tell ye the daughter of Zion, Lo! thy King, is coming unto thee, meek and mounted upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of a toiling ass.
texts.mat.21.6: And the disciples, went, and did as Jesus directed them;
texts.mat.21.7: and led the ass and the colt, and laid upon them their garments, and he took his seat upon them.
texts.mat.21.8: And, the chief multitude, spread their own mantles in the way, and, others, were cutting off young branches from the trees, and spreading them in the way;
texts.mat.21.9: and the multitudes, they who were going before him and they who were following after, were crying aloud, saying—Hosanna! to the Son of David, Blessed is he that is coming in the name of the Lord, Hosanna in the highest.
texts.mat.21.10: And, when he entered into Jerusalem, all the city was startled, saying—Who is this?
texts.mat.21.11: And, the multitudes, were saying—This, is the prophet Jesus,—He from Nazareth of Galilee.
texts.mat.21.12: And Jesus entered into the temple, and cast out all who were selling and buying in the temple,—and, the tables of the money-changers, he overthrew, and the seats of them who were selling doves;
texts.mat.21.13: and saith unto them—It is written, My house, a house of prayer, shall be called; but, ye, are making it, A den of robbers!
texts.mat.21.14: And there came unto him blind and lame, in the temple, and he cured them.
texts.mat.21.15: But the Chief-priests and the Scribes, seeing, the marvels that he wrought, and the boys who were crying aloud in the temple, and saying, Hosanna to the Son of David! were greatly displeased;
texts.mat.21.16: and said unto him—Hearest thou what these are saying? And, Jesus, saith unto them—Yea: Have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings, hast thou prepared praise?
texts.mat.21.17: And, leaving them behind, he went forth outside the city into Bethany, and spent the night there.
texts.mat.21.18: And, early, returning into the city, he hungered;
texts.mat.21.19: and, seeing one fig-tree by the way, he came up to it, and nothing, found he thereon, save leaves only,—and he saith unto it—No more, from thee, let fruit spring forth, unto times age-abiding,—and the fig-tree, instantly withered away.
texts.mat.21.20: And the disciples, seeing it, marvelled, saying—How instantly, did the fig-tree wither away.
texts.mat.21.21: And Jesus, answering, said unto them—Verily, I say unto you, If ye have faith, and do not doubt, not only, this of the fig-tree, shall ye do,—but, even if, unto this mountain, ye shall say, Be lifted up, and be cast into the sea, it shall be done.
texts.mat.21.22: And, all things whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.
texts.mat.21.23: And, when he, entered, the temple, the Chief-priests and the Elders of the people, came unto him as he was teaching, saying, By what authority, these things, art thou doing? and, who, to thee, gave, this authority?
texts.mat.21.24: And, making answer, Jesus said unto them—I also, will ask, you, one thing,—which if ye tell me, I also, will tell, you, by what authority, these things, I am doing:—
texts.mat.21.25: The immersion by John, whence was it? Of heaven, or of men? But, they, began to deliberate among themselves, saying—If we say, Of heaven; He will say unto us, Wherefore then did ye not believe him?
texts.mat.21.26: But, if we say, Of men, we fear the multitude, for, all, as a prophet, are holding John.
texts.mat.21.27: And, making answer to Jesus, they said—We know not. He also, said unto them—Neither do, I, tell, you, by what authority, these things, I am doing.
texts.mat.21.28: But how, to you, doth it seem? A man, had two sons: coming unto the first, he said, Son! go thy way, to-day, be working in the vineyard.
texts.mat.21.29: And, he, answering, said, I, sir! and went not;
texts.mat.21.30: And, coming unto the second, he spake, in like manner,—and, he, answering, said, I will not: afterwards, smitten with regret, he went.
texts.mat.21.31: Which of the two, did the will of the father? They say, The latter. Jesus saith unto them—Verily, I say unto you, the tax-collectors and the harlots, are going before you, into the kingdom of God;
texts.mat.21.32: For John came unto you, in a way of righteousness, and ye believed him not,—but, the tax-collectors and the harlots, believed him; and, ye, seeing it, were not even smitten with regret, afterwards, so as to believe him.
texts.mat.21.33: Another parable, hear ye:—A man there was, a householder, who planted a vineyard, and, a wall around it, placed, and digged in it a wine-vat, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen,—and left home.
texts.mat.21.34: And, when the season of fruits drew near, He sent forth his servants unto the husbandmen to receive his fruits.
texts.mat.21.35: And the husbandmen, taking his servants, one, indeed, they beat, and, another, slew,—and, another, stoned.
texts.mat.21.36: Again, sent he forth other servants, more than the first, and they did unto them, likewise.
texts.mat.21.37: Afterwards, however, he sent forth unto them his son, saying,—They will pay deference unto my son!
texts.mat.21.38: But, the husbandmen, seeing the son, said among themselves,—This, is, the heir: Come on! Let us slay him, and have his inheritance.
texts.mat.21.39: And, taking him, they cast him forth outside the vineyard,—and slew him.
texts.mat.21.40: When therefore the master of the vineyard shall come, what will he do unto those husbandmen?
texts.mat.21.41: They say unto him—Miserable men! Miserably, will he destroy them; and will let out, the vineyard, to other husbandmen, who will render unto him the fruits in their seasons.
texts.mat.21.42: Jesus saith unto them—Have ye, never, read in the Scriptures, A stone which the builders rejected, the same, hath become, head of the corner: From the Lord, hath this come to pass, and is marvellous in our eyes.
texts.mat.21.43: Wherefore I say unto you, The kingdom of God, will be taken away from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof:
texts.mat.21.44: [And, he that falleth on this stone, will be sorely bruised; but, on whomsoever it may fall, it will utterly destroy him.]
texts.mat.21.45: And the Chief-priests and the Pharisees, hearing his parables, took note, that, concerning them, he was speaking.
texts.mat.21.46: And, seeking to secure him, they feared the multitudes; since, for a prophet, were they holding him.
texts.mat.22.1: And, answering, Jesus, again, spake in parables unto them, saying:—
texts.mat.22.2: The kingdom of the heavens hath become like a man, a king,—who made a marriage-feast for his son;
texts.mat.22.3: And sent his servants, to call the invited into the marriage-feast,—and they would not come.
texts.mat.22.4: Again, sent he other servants, saying—Say to the invited, Lo! my dinner, have I prepared, mine oxen and my fatlings, are slain,—and, all things, are, ready: Come ye into the marriage-feast.
texts.mat.22.5: And, they, slighting it, went off, one, indeed, into his own field, and, another, unto his merchandise,—
texts.mat.22.6: And, the rest, securing his servants, ill-treated and slew them.
texts.mat.22.7: And, the king, was provoked to anger,—and, sending his armies, destroyed those murderers, and, their city, set on fire.
texts.mat.22.8: Then, saith he unto his servants—The marriage, indeed, is ready,—but, the invited, were not, worthy;
texts.mat.22.9: Be going, therefore, into the crossways of the roads, and, as many as ye shall find, call ye into the marriage-feast.
texts.mat.22.10: And those servants, going forth, into the roads, gathered together all whom they found, both bad and good,—and filled was the bride-chamber with guests.
texts.mat.22.11: But the king, entering to view the guests, saw there a man, who had not put on a wedding-garment,—
texts.mat.22.12: And saith unto him—Friend! how camest thou in here, not having a wedding-garment? And, he, was put to silence.
texts.mat.22.13: Then, the king said unto the ministers, Binding him feet and hands, cast him forth into the darkness, outside: There, shall be wafting and gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.22.14: For, many, are called, but, few, chosen.
texts.mat.22.15: Then, went the Pharisees and took, counsel, that they might ensnare him, in discourse.
texts.mat.22.16: And they sent forth to him their disciples, with the Herodians, saying, Teacher! we know that, true, thou art, and, the way of God, in truth, dost teach, and it concerneth thee not about anyone,—for thou lookest not unto the face of men:
texts.mat.22.17: Tell us then, how, to thee, it seemeth? Is it allowable to give tax unto Caesar, or not?
texts.mat.22.18: But Jesus, taking note of their wickedness, said—Why are ye tempting me, hypocrites?
texts.mat.22.19: Shew me the coin appointed for the tax. And, they, brought unto him a denary.
texts.mat.22.20: And he saith unto them—Whose, is this image and the inscription?
texts.mat.22.21: They say—Caesar’s. Then, saith he unto them—Render, therefore, the things of Caesar, unto Caesar,—and, the things of God, unto God.
texts.mat.22.22: And, hearing, they marvelled,—and, leaving him, departed.
texts.mat.22.23: On that day, there came unto him Sadducees, who say, there is, no resurrection—and they questioned him,
texts.mat.22.24: saying—Teacher! Moses, said, If any man die not having children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
texts.mat.22.25: Now there were, with us, seven brethren; and, the first, marrying, died, and not having seed, left his wife unto his brother.
texts.mat.22.26: Likewise, the second also, and the third,—unto the seven.
texts.mat.22.27: And, last of all, died, the wife.
texts.mat.22.28: In the resurrection, therefore,—Of which of the seven, shall she be wife? For, all, had her.
texts.mat.22.29: And Jesus answering, said—Ye are deceiving yourselves, knowing neither the Scriptures, nor yet the power of God.
texts.mat.22.30: For, in the resurrection, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but, as messengers in the heaven, are they.
texts.mat.22.31: But, as touching the resurrection of the dead—Have ye not read what was spoken unto you by God, saying—
texts.mat.22.32: I, am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?—He is not God, of the dead, but, of the living.
texts.mat.22.33: And, the multitudes, hearing, were being struck with astonishment at his teaching.
texts.mat.22.34: Now, the Pharisees, hearing that he had silenced the Sadducees, were brought together with one accord;
texts.mat.22.35: and one from among them, a lawyer, proposed a question, putting him to the test:
texts.mat.22.36: Teacher! which commandment, is greatest in the law?
texts.mat.22.37: And, he, said unto him—Thou shalt love the Lord thy God—with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind:
texts.mat.22.38: This, is the great and first commandment.
texts.mat.22.39: The second, like it, is, this: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
texts.mat.22.40: In these two commandments, all the law, is contained, and the prophets.
texts.mat.22.41: Now, the Pharisees having come together, Jesus questioned them, saying—
texts.mat.22.42: How, to you, doth it seem, concerning the Christ? Whose son, is he? They say unto him—David’s.
texts.mat.22.43: He saith unto them—How then doth, David, in spirit, call him, Lord, saying—
texts.mat.22.44: The Lord, hath said unto, my Lord,—Sit thou on my right hand, until I make thy foes thy footstool?
texts.mat.22.45: If then, David, calleth him, Lord, How, is he, his son?
texts.mat.22.46: And, no one, was able to answer him a word, neither durst anyone, from that day, question him, any more.
texts.mat.23.1: Then, Jesus spake unto the multitudes and unto his disciples,
texts.mat.23.2: saying—Upon Moses’ seat, have sat down, the Scribes and the Pharisees:
texts.mat.23.3: All things, therefore, whatsoever they tell you, do and observe,—but, according to their works, do ye not, for they, say, and do not, perform.
texts.mat.23.4: But they bind together heavy burdens, and lay upon men’s shoulders, whereas, they, with their finger, are not willing to move them.
texts.mat.23.5: But, all their works, they do, to be gazed at, by men,—for they make broad their amulets, and make large their fringes,
texts.mat.23.6: And dearly love the first couch in the chief meals, and the first seats in the synagogues,
texts.mat.23.7: And the salutations in the market-places, and to be called by men, Rabbi.
texts.mat.23.8: But, ye,—do not be called Rabbi,—for, one, is your Teacher, and, all ye, are brethren;
texts.mat.23.9: And, father, be none of you called, upon the earth, for, one, is your Father, the Heavenly;
texts.mat.23.10: Neither be called leaders, for, your leader, is one, the Christ;
texts.mat.23.11: And, the greatest of you, shall be to you, a minister;
texts.mat.23.12: And, whoever shall exalt himself, shall be, abased, and, whoever shall abase himself, shall be, exalted,
texts.mat.23.14: But alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites; because ye are locking up the kingdom of the heavens before men,—for, ye, are not entering, neither, them who are entering, suffer ye to enter.
texts.mat.23.15: Alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: because ye compass sea and dry land, to make one convert—and, when it is done, ye make him a son of gehenna, twofold more than ye.
texts.mat.23.16: Alas for you, blind guides! that say—Whosoever shall swear by the Temple, it is, nothing, but, whosoever shall swear by the gold of the Temple, is bound:
texts.mat.23.17: Foolish and blind! for which is, greater, The gold, or the Temple that hath hallowed the gold?
texts.mat.23.18: And, whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is, nothing, but, whosoever shall swear by the gift that is upon it, is bound:
texts.mat.23.19: Blind! for which is greater, The gift, or the altar that halloweth the gift?
texts.mat.23.20: He therefore that hath sworn by the altar, sweareth by it, and by all that is upon it;
texts.mat.23.21: And, he that hath sworn by the Temple, sweareth by it, and by him who dwelleth therein;
texts.mat.23.22: And, he that hath sworn by heaven, sweareth by the throne of God, and by him who sitteth thereupon.
texts.mat.23.23: Alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites; because ye tithe the mint and the anise and the cummin,—and have dismissed the weightier matters of the law—the justice, the mercy, and the faith; whereas, these, it was binding, to do, and, those, not to, dismiss.
texts.mat.23.24: Blind guides! Straining out the gnat, but, the camel, swallowing.
texts.mat.23.25: Alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites; because ye cleanse the outside of the cup and of the dish,—while, within, they are full of plunder and intemperance.
texts.mat.23.26: Blind Pharisee! cleanse, first, the inside, of the cup [and of the dish], that, the outside thereof, may become, clean.
texts.mat.23.27: Alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites; because ye make yourselves like sepulchres whitewashed, which, outside, indeed, appear, beautiful, but, within, are full, of dead men’s bones and all uncleanness,—
texts.mat.23.28: Thus, ye also, outside, indeed, appear to men, righteous, but, within, are full, of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
texts.mat.23.29: Alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites; because ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and adorn the monuments of the righteous,
texts.mat.23.30: and say—If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners in the blood of the prophets:
texts.mat.23.31: So that ye bear witness against yourselves, that ye are, sons, of them who murdered the prophets.
texts.mat.23.32: And, ye, fill ye up the measure of your fathers!
texts.mat.23.33: Serpents! broods of vipers! how should ye flee from the judgment of gehenna?
texts.mat.23.34: For this cause, lo! I, send unto you, prophets and wise men and scribes,—some from among them, ye will slay and crucify, And some from among them ye will—scourge in your synagogues, and pursue from city to city:
texts.mat.23.35: That there may come upon you—all righteous blood poured out upon the earth, from the blood of Abel the righteous, unto the blood of Zachariah, son of Barachiah, whom ye murdered between the Temple and the altar.
texts.mat.23.36: Verily, I say unto you—All these things, will have come, upon this generation.
texts.mat.23.37: Jerusalem! Jerusalem! that slayeth the prophets, and stoneth them that have been sent unto her,—how often, would I have gathered thy children, like as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings,—and ye would not!
texts.mat.23.38: Lo! your house is left to you;
texts.mat.23.39: For I say unto you—in no wise, may ye see me, henceforth, until ye say, Blessed, is he that cometh, in the name of the Lord!
texts.mat.24.1: And, Jesus coming forth, from the temple, was taking his departure, when his disciples came forward to point out to him the buildings of the temple.
texts.mat.24.2: But, he, answering, said unto them—Are ye not beholding all these things? Verily, I say unto you—in no wise, shall there be left here, stone upon stone, which shall not be thrown down.
texts.mat.24.3: And, as he was sitting upon the Mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him, privately, saying—Tell us, when these things shall be,—and what the sign of thy presence, and the conclusion of the age.
texts.mat.24.4: And, answering, Jesus said unto them—Be taking heed, lest anyone, deceive, you;
texts.mat.24.5: For, many, will come upon my name, saying—I, am the Christ,—and will, deceive many.
texts.mat.24.6: Moreover ye will be sure to be hearing of wars, and rumours of wars: Mind! be not alarmed, for it must needs happen,—but, not yet, is, the end;
texts.mat.24.7: For there will arise—nation against nation, and kingdom against kingdom,—and there will be famines and earthquakes, in places.
texts.mat.24.8: But, all these things, are a beginning of birth-pangs.
texts.mat.24.9: Then, will they deliver you up into tribulation, and will slay you,—and ye will be men hated by all the nations, because of my name
texts.mat.24.10: And, then, will many be caused to stumble, and, one another, will deliver up, and will hate one another;
texts.mat.24.11: And, many false prophets, will arise, and deceive, many;
texts.mat.24.12: And, because of lawlessness being brought to the full, the love of the many, will grew cold.
texts.mat.24.13: But, he that hath endured throughout, the same, shall be saved.
texts.mat.24.14: And this glad message of the kingdom will be proclaimed in all the inhabited earth, for a witness unto all the nations,—and, then, will have come, the end.
texts.mat.24.15: Whensoever, therefore, ye shall see the abomination desolation, that was spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in a holy place,—he that readeth, let him think,
texts.mat.24.16: Then, they who are in Judaea, let them flee into the mountains;
texts.mat.24.17: And, he that is on the house-top, let him not come down, to take away the things out of his house;
texts.mat.24.18: And, he that is in the field, let him not turn back, to take away his mantle.
texts.mat.24.19: But alas! for the women with child, and for them that are giving suck, in those days;
texts.mat.24.20: But be praying that your flight, may not happen in winter, nor on sabbath;
texts.mat.24.21: For there will be then, Great tribulation, such as hath not happened, from the beginning of the world, until the present time, neither in any wise shall happen.
texts.mat.24.22: And, except those days had been shortened, no flesh had been saved; but, for the sake of the chosen, those days shall be shortened.
texts.mat.24.23: Then, if any, unto you, say—Lo! here, is the Christ, or, there, Do not believe it;
texts.mat.24.24: For there will arise, false Christs, and false prophets,—and they will show great signs and wonders, so that, if possible, even the chosen, should be deceived:—
texts.mat.24.26: If therefore they should say unto you, Lo! in the desert, he is, Do not go forth; Lo! in the chambers, Do not believe it.
texts.mat.24.27: For, just as the lightning goeth forth from the east, and shineth unto the west, so, shall be the presence of the Son of Man.
texts.mat.24.28: Wheresoever, the corpse, shall be, there, shall be gathered, the vultures!
texts.mat.24.29: But, straightway after the tribulation of those days, the sun, will be darkened, and, the moon, will not give her brightness, and, the stars, will fall from heaven,—and, the powers of the heavens, will be shaken;
texts.mat.24.30: And, then, will be displayed—The sign of the Son of Man in heaven, and, then, will smite their breasts—all the tribes of the earth; and they will see the Son of Man—coming upon the clouds of heaven, with great power and glory.
texts.mat.24.31: And he will send forth his messengers, with a great trumpet, and they will gather together his chosen—Out of the four winds, from heavens’ bounds, unto their bounds.
texts.mat.24.32: Now, from the fig-tree, learn ye, the parable:—When, already, her young branch, becometh tender, and the leaves, may be sprouting, ye observe, that, near, is, the summer:
texts.mat.24.33: Thus, ye also, when ye shall see all these things, observe ye, that, near, he is, at the doors.
texts.mat.24.34: Verily, I say unto you—In nowise, shall this generation, pass away, until all these things, shall happen:
texts.mat.24.35: The heaven and the earth, shall pass away, but, my words, shall, in nowise, pass away.
texts.mat.24.36: But, concerning that day and hour, no one, knoweth, neither the messengers of the heavens, nor the Son,—save the Father only.
texts.mat.24.37: For, just as the days of Noah, so, will be the presence of the Son of Man;
texts.mat.24.38: For, as they were in those days that were before the flood, feeding and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage,—until the day Noah entered into the ark;
texts.mat.24.39: And they observed not, until the flood came and took away all together, so, will be, the presence of the Son of Man.
texts.mat.24.40: Then, shall there be two men in the field,—one, is taken near, and, one, is left behind:
texts.mat.24.41: Two women grinding at the mill,—one, is taken near, and, one, is left behind.
texts.mat.24.42: Be watching, therefore, for ye know not, on what manner of day, your Lord is coming.
texts.mat.24.43: But there is, one thing, ye know—That, if the householder, had known, in what watch, the thief was coming, he would have been on the alert, and not have suffered his house to be dug through.
texts.mat.24.44: Wherefore, ye also, be getting ready, because, in what hour ye are, not thinking, The Son of Man doth come.
texts.mat.24.45: Who then is the faithful and prudent servant, whom the master hath appointed over his household, to give them food in season?
texts.mat.24.46: Happy! that servant, whom his master, when he cometh, shall find so doing!
texts.mat.24.47: Verily, I say unto you—Over all his substance, will he appoint him.
texts.mat.24.48: But, if that wicked servant should say in his heart—My master, delayeth,
texts.mat.24.49: And begin to be striking his fellow-servants, and eating and drinking with the drunken,
texts.mat.24.50: The master of that servant, will have come, on a day when he is not expecting, and in an hour when he is not observing,—
texts.mat.24.51: And will cut him asunder; and, his part, with the hypocrites, will appoint: There, shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth!
texts.mat.25.1: Then, will the kingdom of the heavens become like unto, ten virgins, who, taking their torches, went forth to meet the bridegroom.
texts.mat.25.2: Now, five of them, were foolish, and, five, prudent.
texts.mat.25.3: For, the foolish—though they took, their torches, took not with them, oil:
texts.mat.25.4: But, the prudent, took oil in their vessels, with their torches.
texts.mat.25.5: Now, the bridegroom, delaying, they all became drowsy, and were sleeping.
texts.mat.25.6: And, at midnight, an outcry hath been made—Lo! the bridegroom! Be going forth to meet him!
texts.mat.25.7: Then, arose all those virgins, and trimmed their torches.
texts.mat.25.8: And, the foolish, unto the prudent, said—Give us of your oil, because, our torches, are going out.
texts.mat.25.9: But the prudent, answered, saying—Lest once, by any means, there be not enough for us and you, be going rather unto them that sell, and buy for yourselves
texts.mat.25.10: But, as they were going away to buy, the bridegroom came; and, they who were ready, went in with him, into the marriage-feast, and, the door was locked.
texts.mat.25.11: But, afterwards, came the other virgins also, saying—Lord! Lord! open unto us!
texts.mat.25.12: And, he, answering, said—Verily, I say unto you, I know you not.
texts.mat.25.13: Be watching, therefore, because ye know, neither the day nor the hour.
texts.mat.25.14: For it is, just as a man, who, going from home, called his own servants, and delivered up to them his substance;
texts.mat.25.15: And, to one, indeed, gave he five talents, and, to another, two, and, to another, one,—to each according to his particular ability, and went from home.
texts.mat.25.16: Straightway, he who, the five talents, had received, went and traded with them, and gained other five:
texts.mat.25.17: Likewise, he of the two, gained other two:
texts.mat.25.18: But, he who the one had received, went away, and digged up ground, and hid the silver of his lord.
texts.mat.25.19: And, after a long time, cometh the lord of those servants, and reckoneth with them.
texts.mat.25.20: And he who the five talents had received, coming forward, brought other five talents, saying,—Lord! five talents, to me, thou didst deliver up: See! other five talents, I gained.
texts.mat.25.21: His lord said unto him—Well-done! good and faithful servant,—Over a few things wast thou faithful, over many things, will I appoint thee: Enter into the joy of thy lord.
texts.mat.25.22: He also of the two talents, coming forward, said—Lord! two talents, to me, didst thou deliver up: See! other two talents, I gained.
texts.mat.25.23: His lord said unto him—Well-done! good and faithful servant,—Over a few things, wast thou faithful, over many things, will I appoint thee: Enter into the joy of thy lord.
texts.mat.25.24: But he also who, the one talent, had received, coming forward, said—Lord I knew thee, that thou art a, hard, man, reaping, where thou hast not sown,—and gathering, whence thou hast not winnowed;
texts.mat.25.25: And, overcome with fear, I went away, and hid thy talent in the ground: See! thou hast what is thine!
texts.mat.25.26: And his lord, answering, said unto him—O wicked servant, and cowardly, knewest thou that I reap, where I have not sown, and gather, whence I have not winnowed?
texts.mat.25.27: It was binding on thee, therefore, to cast my silver into the money-changers,—and, I, when I, came, might have obtained what was mine, with interest.
texts.mat.25.28: Therefore take away, from him, the talent, and give unto him that hath the ten talents;
texts.mat.25.29: For, to every one that hath, shall be given, and he shall be made to abound; but, from him that hath not, even what he hath, shall be taken away from him:
texts.mat.25.30: And, the unprofitable servant, cast ye forth into the darkness, outside: There, shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.
texts.mat.25.31: But, whensoever the Son of Man shall come in his glory, and all the messengers with him, then will he sit on his throne of glory;
texts.mat.25.32: And there will be gathered before him, all the nations, and he will separate them one from another, just as, the shepherd! separateth the sheep from the goats,—
texts.mat.25.33: And he will set, the sheep, indeed, on his right hand, but, the goats, on the left.
texts.mat.25.34: Then, will the king say to those on his right hand: Come ye, the blessed of my Father! Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world;
texts.mat.25.35: For I hungered, and ye gave me to eat, I thirsted, and ye gave me drink, a stranger, was I, and ye took me home,
texts.mat.25.36: Naked, and ye clothed me, sick, and ye visited me, in prison, was I, and ye came unto me.
texts.mat.25.37: Then, will the righteous answer him, saying: Lord! when, saw we thee—hungry, and fed thee, or thirsty, and gave thee drink?
texts.mat.25.38: And, when, saw we thee—a stranger, and took thee home, or naked, and clothed thee?
texts.mat.25.39: And, when, saw we thee—sick, or in prison, and came unto thee?
texts.mat.25.40: And, answering, the king will say unto them: Verily, I say unto you—Inasmuch as ye did it unto one of these my least brethren, unto me, ye did it.
texts.mat.25.41: Then, will he say unto those also, on his left hand: Depart ye from me, accursed ones! Into the age-abiding fire, which hath been prepared for the adversary and his messengers;
texts.mat.25.42: For I hungered, and ye gave me not to eat, [and] I was thirsty, and ye gave me not to drink,
texts.mat.25.43: A stranger, was I, and ye took me not home, naked, and ye clothed me not, sick, and in prison, and ye visited me not.
texts.mat.25.44: Then, will, they also, answer, saying: Lord! when saw we thee—hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and ministered not unto thee?
texts.mat.25.45: Then, will he answer them, saying: Verily, I say unto you—Inasmuch as ye did it not, unto one of these least, neither unto me, did ye it.
texts.mat.25.46: And, these, shall go away, into, age-abiding, correction, but, the righteous, into, age-abiding, life.
texts.mat.26.1: And it came to pass, when Jesus ended all these words, he said unto his disciples:
texts.mat.26.2: Ye know that, after two days, the passover, taketh place,—and, the Son of Man, is to be delivered up, to be crucified.
texts.mat.26.3: Then, were gathered together, the High-priests and the Elders of the people, into the court of the High-priest who was called Caiaphas;
texts.mat.26.4: and they took counsel together, in order that, Jesus, by guile, they might secure, and slay.
texts.mat.26.5: They were saying, however: Not during the feast, lest, an uproar, arise among the people.
texts.mat.26.6: But, Jesus, happening to be in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
texts.mat.26.7: there came unto him a woman, holding an alabaster-jar of costly perfume, and she poured it down upon his head, as he was reclining.
texts.mat.26.8: And the disciples, seeing it, were greatly displeased, saying—To what end, this loss?
texts.mat.26.9: For this could have been sold for much, and given to the destitute.
texts.mat.26.10: But Jesus, taking note, said unto them—Why vex ye the woman? for, a seemly work, hath she wrought for me;
texts.mat.26.11: For, always, the destitute, have ye with you,—but, me, not always, have ye;
texts.mat.26.12: For, she, pouring this perfume upon my body, so as to prepare me for burial, did it.
texts.mat.26.13: Verily, I say unto you—Wheresoever this glad-message shall be proclaimed in all the world, also what she did, will be told, as a memorial of her.
texts.mat.26.14: Then, went one of the twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, unto the High-priests,
texts.mat.26.15: and said—What are ye willing to give unto me? and, I, unto you, will deliver him up. And they appointed him thirty pieces of silver.
texts.mat.26.16: And, from that time, was he seeking a favourable opportunity that he might, deliver him up.
texts.mat.26.17: And, on the first of the days of unleavened bread, the disciples came unto Jesus, saying—Where wilt thou, that we make ready for thee to eat the passover?
texts.mat.26.18: And, he, said—Go your way into the city, unto such-a-one, and say to him, The teacher, saith, My season, is, near, with thee, will I keep the passover, with my disciples.
texts.mat.26.19: And the disciples did, as Jesus directed them, and made ready the passover.
texts.mat.26.20: And, when, evening, came, he was reclining with the twelve [disciples];
texts.mat.26.21: and, as they were eating, he said—Verily, I say unto you, One from among you, will deliver me up.
texts.mat.26.22: And, being exceedingly grieved, they began to be saying to him, each one—Can it be, I, Lord?
texts.mat.26.23: And, he, answering, said—He who hath dipped with me his hand in the bowl, the same, will deliver me up.
texts.mat.26.24: The Son of Man, indeed, goeth his way, according as it is written concerning him,—But alas! for that man, through whom the Son of Man, is being delivered up: Well, had it been for him, if, that man, had not been born!
texts.mat.26.25: And Judas, who was delivering him up, answering, said—Can it be, I, Rabbi? He saith unto him—Thou, hast said.
texts.mat.26.26: And, as they were eating, Jesus, taking a loaf and blessing, brake,—and, giving to his disciples, said—Take, eat! This, is, my body.
texts.mat.26.27: And, taking a cup, and giving thanks, he gave unto them, saying—Drink of it, all of you;
texts.mat.26.28: For, this, is my blood of the covenant, which, for many, is to be poured out, for remission of sins.
texts.mat.26.29: Moreover, I say unto you—In nowise, will I drink, henceforth, of this produce of the vine, until that day, whensoever I shall drink it with you, new, in the kingdom of my Father.
texts.mat.26.30: And, having sung praise, they went forth unto the Mount of Olives.
texts.mat.26.31: Then, Jesus saith unto them—All ye, will find cause of stumbling in me, during this night; for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and, the sheep of the flock, will be scattered abroad;
texts.mat.26.32: But, after my arising, I will go before you into Galilee.
texts.mat.26.33: Now Peter, answering, said unto him—Though, all, shall find cause of stumbling in thee, I, shall never find cause of stumbling.
texts.mat.26.34: Jesus saith unto him: Verily, I say unto thee—During this night, before a cock crow, Thrice, wilt thou deny me.
texts.mat.26.35: Peter saith unto him: Even though it be needful for me, with thee to die, in nowise, will I deny thee. Likewise, all the disciples also, said.
texts.mat.26.36: Then Jesus cometh with them, into a place called Gethsemane,—and he saith unto his disciples, Sit ye here, while I go yonder and pray.
texts.mat.26.37: And, taking with him, Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be grieved and to be in great distress.
texts.mat.26.38: Then, saith he unto them: Encompassed with grief, is my soul, unto death: Abide ye here, and be watching with me.
texts.mat.26.39: And, going forward a little, he fell upon his face, offering prayer, and saying—My Father! If it is possible, let this cup pass from me,—Nevertheless, not as, I, will, but as, thou, wilt.
texts.mat.26.40: And he cometh unto his disciples, and findeth them sleeping, and said unto Peter—Thus, powerless are ye, one hour, to watch with me?
texts.mat.26.41: Be watching and praying, that ye may not enter into temptation: The spirit, indeed, is, eager, but, the flesh, weak.
texts.mat.26.42: Again, a second time, departing he prayed, saying: My Father! If it is impossible for this to pass, except I, drink, it, Accomplished, be, thy will.
texts.mat.26.43: And coming, he, again, found them sleeping, for their eyes had become heavy.
texts.mat.26.44: And, leaving them, he, again, departed, and prayed a third time, the same word, saying again.
texts.mat.26.45: Then, cometh he unto the disciples, and saith unto them,—Ye are sleeping what time remaineth, and taking your rest: Lo! the hour hath drawn near, and, the Son of Man, is being delivered up into the hands of sinners.
texts.mat.26.46: Arise! let us be going,—Lo! he that delivereth me up, hath drawn near.
texts.mat.26.47: And, while, yet, he was speaking, lo! Judas, one of the twelve, came, and, with him, a large multitude, with swords and clubs, from the High-priests and Elders of the people.
texts.mat.26.48: And, he who was delivering him up, gave them a sign, saying—Whomsoever I shall kiss, he, it is,—secure him.
texts.mat.26.49: And, straightway, coming unto Jesus, he said—Joy to thee! Rabbi, and eagerly kissed him.
texts.mat.26.50: But, Jesus, said unto him—Friend! wherefore art thou here? Then, coming forward, they thrust their hands upon Jesus, and secured him.
texts.mat.26.51: And lo! one of those with Jesus, stretching forth his hand, grasped his sword, and smiting the servant of the High-priest, cut off his ear.
texts.mat.26.52: Then, Jesus saith unto him—Put back thy sword into its place, for, all they who take a sword, by a sword, shall perish.
texts.mat.26.53: Or thinkest thou that I cannot call upon my Father, and he will set near me, even now, more than twelve legions of messengers?
texts.mat.26.54: How then should the Scriptures be fulfilled, that, thus, it must needs come to pass?
texts.mat.26.55: In that hour, said Jesus unto the multitudes: As against a robber, came ye forth, with swords and clubs, to arrest me? Daily in the temple, used I to sit teaching, and ye secured me not;
texts.mat.26.56: But, this, hath, wholly, come to pass, that, the Scriptures of the prophets, may be fulfilled. Then, the disciples, all forsaking him, fled.
texts.mat.26.57: And, they who secured Jesus, led him away unto Caiaphas the High-priest, where the Scribes and the Elders gathered themselves together.
texts.mat.26.58: Now, Peter, was following him afar off, unto the court of the High-priest,—and, entering within, was sitting with the attendants, to see the end.
texts.mat.26.59: Now, the High-priests and all the High-council, were seeking false-witness against Jesus, that they might, put him to death;
texts.mat.26.60: and found not any, though many came forward as false-witnesses. At length, however, there came forward, two,
texts.mat.26.61: and said: This, man said—I am able to pull down the shrine of God, and, in three days, to, build, it.
texts.mat.26.62: And the High-priest, arising, said unto him—Nothing, answerest thou? What are these, against thee bearing witness?
texts.mat.26.63: But, Jesus, was silent. And, the High-priest, said unto him: I put thee on oath, by the Living God, that, to us, thou say—Whether, thou, art the Christ, the Son of God.
texts.mat.26.64: Jesus saith unto him: Thou, hast said; Moreover, I say unto you—Hereafter, ye will see the Son of Man, sitting on the right hand of power, and coming upon the clouds of heaven.
texts.mat.26.65: Then, the High-priest rent asunder his garments, saying—He hath spoken profanely! What further need have we, of witnesses? Lo! now, ye have heard the profanity!
texts.mat.26.66: How, to you, doth it seem? And, they, answering, said: Guilty of death, he is.
texts.mat.26.67: Then, spat they into his face, and buffeted him; and, others, struck him smartly,
texts.mat.26.68: saying—Prophesy unto us, O Christ! Who is he that struck thee?
texts.mat.26.69: Now, Peter, was sitting without, in the court; and there came unto him a certain female servant, saying—Thou also, wast with Jesus, the Galilaean.
texts.mat.26.70: But, he, denied before all, saying—I know not what thou sayest.
texts.mat.26.71: And, when he went out into the porch, another female saw him, and said unto them who were there—This, one was with Jesus the Nazarene.
texts.mat.26.72: And, again, he denied, with an oath—I know not the man.
texts.mat.26.73: And, after a little, the by-standers, coming forward, said unto Peter: Truly, thou also, art, from among them, for, thy very speech, maketh thee, manifest.
texts.mat.26.74: Then, began he to be cursing and swearing—I know not the man! And, straightway, a cock crowed.
texts.mat.26.75: And Peter was put in mind of the declaration of Jesus, of his having said—Before a cock crow, thrice, wilt thou utterly deny me; and, going forth outside, he wept bitterly.
texts.mat.27.1: Now, when morning came, all the High-priests and Elders of the people took, counsel, against Jesus, so as to put him to death:
texts.mat.27.2: and, binding him, they led him away, and delivered him up unto Pilate the governor.
texts.mat.27.3: Then, Judas who had delivered him up, seeing that he was condemned, being smitten with remorse, returned the thirty pieces of silver unto the High-priests and Elders,
texts.mat.27.4: saying—I have sinned, in delivering up righteous blood. But, they, said—What is that to us? thou, shalt see to it for thyself.
texts.mat.27.5: And, throwing the pieces of silver into the Temple, he withdrew, and, going away, hanged himself.
texts.mat.27.6: But, the High-priests, taking the pieces of silver, said—It is not allowed, to cast them into the treasury; since, a price of blood, they are.
texts.mat.27.7: And, taking counsel, they bought with them, the field of the potter, as a burial-place for strangers.
texts.mat.27.8: Wherefore, that field hath been called Field of Blood, until this day.
texts.mat.27.9: Then, was fulfilled, that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying: And they took the thirty pieces of silver, as the value of him whom they had valued, whom they had valued, of Israel’s sons,—
texts.mat.27.10: And gave them for the field of the potter, as, the Lord, directed me.
texts.mat.27.11: Now, Jesus, stood before the governor; and the governor questioned him, saying—Thou, art the king of the Jews? And, Jesus, said—Thou, sayest.
texts.mat.27.12: And, while he was being accused by the High-priests and Elders, he answered nothing.
texts.mat.27.13: Then, Pilate saith unto him—Hearest thou not how many things against thee they are bearing witness?
texts.mat.27.14: And he answered him, no not so much as a single word, so that the governor was marvelling exceedingly.
texts.mat.27.15: But, feast by feast, the governor had been wont to release one unto the multitude, a prisoner whom they were desiring.
texts.mat.27.16: Now they had at that time a distinguished prisoner, called, Barabbas.
texts.mat.27.17: They therefore having come together, Pilate, said to them—Whom will ye I should release unto you? Barabbas? or Jesus, who is called Christ?
texts.mat.27.18: For he knew that, for envy, they had delivered him up.
texts.mat.27.19: And, as he was sitting upon the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying: Have thou nothing to do with that righteous man, for, many things, have I suffered this day, by dream, because of him.
texts.mat.27.20: But, the High-priests and the elders, persuaded the multitudes, that they should claim Barabbas, but, Jesus, should, destroy.
texts.mat.27.21: Now the governor, answering, said unto them—Which of the two desire ye I should release unto you? And they said—Barabbas!
texts.mat.27.22: Pilate saith unto them—What then shall I do unto Jesus, who is called Christ? They all say—Let him be crucified!
texts.mat.27.23: But, he, said—Indeed! what evil hath he done? But, they, vehemently, were crying aloud, saying—Let him be crucified!
texts.mat.27.24: And Pilate, seeing, that, nothing, it availed, but rather, a tumult, was arising, taking water, washed his hands of it before the multitude, saying—Innocent, am I, of the blood of this man,—Ye, shall see to it for yourselves.
texts.mat.27.25: And all the people, answering, said—His blood be upon us and upon our children!
texts.mat.27.26: Then released he unto them Barabbas, but, scourging, Jesus, delivered him up, that he might be crucified.
texts.mat.27.27: Then the soldiers of the governor, taking Jesus aside into the judgment-hall, gathered unto him all the band;
texts.mat.27.28: and, unclothing him, a scarlet scarf, put they about him,—
texts.mat.27.29: and, plaiting a crown out of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand,—and, kneeling before him, began to mock him, saying—Joy to thee, King of the Jews!
texts.mat.27.30: And, spitting upon him, they took the reed, and began striking upon his head.
texts.mat.27.31: And, when they had mocked him, they put off him the scarf, and put on him his garments, and led him away unto the crucifying.
texts.mat.27.32: And, as they were going forth, they found a man of Cyrene, by name, Simon,—the same, they impressed to bear his cross.
texts.mat.27.33: And, coming into a place called Golgotha, that is to say, Skull-place,
texts.mat.27.34: they gave him to drink, wine, with gall, mingled, and, tasting, he would not drink.
texts.mat.27.35: And, having crucified him, they parted among themselves his garments, casting a cloth;
texts.mat.27.36: and, being seated, were watching him there.
texts.mat.27.37: And they put up, over his head, his accusation, written—THIS, IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
texts.mat.27.38: Then, are crucified with him, two robbers,—one on the right hand, and one on the left.
texts.mat.27.39: And, they who were passing by, were reviling him, shaking their heads,
texts.mat.27.40: and saying—The man that taketh down the Temple and in three days buildeth it! Save, thyself! If thou art God’s, Son, come down from the cross.
texts.mat.27.41: Likewise, the High-priests, [also], mocking, with the Scribes and Elders, were saying: Others, he saved,—Himself, he cannot save:
texts.mat.27.42: Israel’s King, he is! Let him come down, now, from the cross,—and we will believe on him!
texts.mat.27.43: He hath put confidence upon God, Let him rescue him, now, if he desireth him; for he said, I am, God’s Son.
texts.mat.27.44: And, the same thing, the robbers also, who were crucified with him, were casting in his teeth.
texts.mat.27.45: Now, from the sixth hour, darkness, came upon all the land—until the ninth hour.
texts.mat.27.46: And, about the ninth hour, Jesus uttered a cry, with a loud voice, saying—Eloi! Eloi! lema sabachthanei? that is, My God! my God! to what end hast thou forsaken me?
texts.mat.27.47: Now certain of them who were there standing, when they heard, began to say—This man, calleth, Elijah.
texts.mat.27.48: And, straightway, one from among them, running, and taking a sponge, and filling it with vinegar and putting it on a reed, was giving him to drink;
texts.mat.27.49: but, the rest, said—Stay! let us see whether Elijah is coming, and will save him. [[But, another, taking a spear, pierced his side, and there came forth water and blood]].
texts.mat.27.50: And, Jesus, again crying out with a loud voice, dismissed the spirit.
texts.mat.27.51: And lo! the veil of the Temple, was rent, from top to bottom, into two; and, the earth, was shaken, and, the rocks, were rent;
texts.mat.27.52: and, the tombs, were opened and, many bodies of the holy ones who had fallen asleep, arose,—
texts.mat.27.53: and, coming forth out of the tombs after his arising, entered into, the holy city, and plainly appeared unto many.
texts.mat.27.54: Now, the centurion, and those with him watching Jesus, seeing the earthquake and the things coming to pass, were violently affrighted, saying—Truly, God’s Son, was, he!
texts.mat.27.55: Now there were there, many women, from afar, beholding, who indeed had followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering unto him;
texts.mat.27.56: among whom was Mary the Magdalene, also Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
texts.mat.27.57: And, when, evening, arrived, there came a rich man from Arimathaea, whose name was Joseph, who also, himself, had been discipled unto Jesus.
texts.mat.27.58: The same, going unto Pilate, claimed the body of Jesus. Then, Pilate commanded it to be given up.
texts.mat.27.59: And Joseph, taking the body, wrapped it up in a clean Indian-cloth,
texts.mat.27.60: and laid it in his new tomb, which he had hewn in the rock, and, rolling near a large stone unto the door of the tomb, departed.
texts.mat.27.61: Now there were there, Mary the Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre.
texts.mat.27.62: And, on the morrow, which is after the preparation, the High-priests and the Pharisee were gathered together unto Pilate,
texts.mat.27.63: saying—Sir! we have been put in mind that, that deceiver, said, while yet living,—After three days, will I, arise.
texts.mat.27.64: Command, therefore, that the sepulchre be made secure until the third day,—lest once the disciples should come and steal him, and say unto the people, He hath arisen from the dead! and, the last deception, shall be, worse than the first.
texts.mat.27.65: Pilate saith unto them—Ye have a guard: Go your way, secure it for yourselves, as ye know how.
texts.mat.27.66: And, they, went and secured for themselves the sepulchre, sealing the stone, with the guard.
texts.mat.28.1: And, late in the week, when it was on the point of dawning into the first of the week, came Mary the Magdalene, and the other Mary, to view the sepulchre.
texts.mat.28.2: And lo! a great commotion occurred,—for, a messenger of the Lord, descending out of heaven, and coming near, had rolled away the stone, and was sitting upon it.
texts.mat.28.3: Now his appearance, was, as lightning, and, his clothing, white as snow;
texts.mat.28.4: and, for fear of him, they who were keeping watch were thrown into a commotion, and became as dead men.
texts.mat.28.5: But the messenger, answering, said unto the women—Be not, ye, afraid! For I know that, Jesus the crucified, ye are seeking:
texts.mat.28.6: He is not here, for he hath arisen, as he said. Come! see the place where he lay;
texts.mat.28.7: And, quickly going, tell his disciples—He hath arisen from the dead, and lo! he is going before you into Galilee;—There, shall ye yourselves see him: Lo! I have told you.
texts.mat.28.8: And, departing quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, they ran to bring tidings unto his disciples.
texts.mat.28.9: And lo! Jesus, met them, saying—Joy to you! And, they, going forward, held his feet, and worshipped him.
texts.mat.28.10: Then, Jesus saith unto them—Be not afraid! Go your way, bear tidings unto my brethren, that they may depart into Galilee; and, there, shall they themselves see me.
texts.mat.28.11: Now as they were, going, lo! certain of the guard, went into the city and reported unto the High-priests all the things that had come to pass;
texts.mat.28.12: and, being gathered together with the Elders and taking counsel, sufficient pieces of silver, gave they unto the soldiers,—
texts.mat.28.13: saying—Say ye, His disciples, coming, by night, stole him, while we were sleeping;
texts.mat.28.14: And, if this be reported unto the governor, we, will persuade him, and will make, you, free from care.
texts.mat.28.15: And, they, taking the pieces of silver, did as they were instructed. And this account was spread abroad among the Jews…until this [very] day.
